title: Fact Check: Huge accident in Texas on New Year? Nope, 2021 clip goes viral
content:
This video is from February 11, 2021, when a chain collision on an icy roadway in Fort Worth, Texas, claimed six lives.
Multiple cars and trucks slammed into one another, unable to stop, as a man looked on in a scary video  going viral on social media. Those sharing it claimed that this huge accident happened in Fort Worth, a city in Texas, on January 1, 2025. The text inside the video  read: "Absolutely crazy footage from the Fort Worth, Texas pileup. January 1-2025."
One person shared the video on X writing , "Wow this is scary! Happened Jan 1st in Fort Worth, Texas. Huge car pile-up!" Its archive can be seen here . One such Instagram Reel  had garnered more than 23 million views at the time of writing this article.
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video is from February 11, 2021, when a chain collision on an icy roadway in Fort Worth, Texas, claimed six lives.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a compilation of this accident's footage, uploaded on a YouTube channel in September 2024. The description stated that this incident took place on February 11, 2021, in Fort Worth, Texas.Â
Further searches led us to an ABC News report  dated February 12, 2021. It stated that at least six people died and 65 were injured in a massive accident in Fort Worth, Texas. At least 133 vehicles were involved in this multi-vehicle crash on the I-35 highway.Â
The toll lanes of the highway where the crash took place reportedly  remained closed throughout the day of the accident and overnight, as firefighters worked to clear the damaged vehicles from the area. Quoting Fort Worth police, the report added that freezing rain had made the roads slippery and accumulated ice, causing the accident .
On January 18, 2023, the National Transportation Safety Board released a comprehensive report about this accident  which noted that before the accident, the area received 36 consecutive hours of below-freezing temperatures. The two southbound toll lanes in the vicinity of the crash were pretreated to prevent icing. However, freezing rain and mist led to a massive crash on the highway.
In February 2021, the United States witnessed one of the worst cold snaps in history and Texas was one of the worst-hit US states that saw freezing weather and blackouts . President Joe Biden at the time declared an emergency in Texas due to the severe winter storm which began on February 11, 2021 — the day of the accident. Texas state records show that 246 people died  due to the February 2021 winter storm. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 3, 2025 21:50 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show an IT raid on a Tirupati priest's home
content:
This video from Vellore, Tamil Nadu, shows police recovering jewellery stolen from a store in December 2021.
A video  of jewellery displayed on a table was shared online. Allegedly, this haul was recovered from the house of a priest serving at the Sri Venkateswara Swami Temple in Andhra Pradesh's Tirupati.Â
The video was shared with captions like: "Do you know how much money, gold and diamonds were found when the income tax department raided the house of one of the 16 priests serving Tirupati Thimmappa? 128 kg gold, 150 crores in cash, 70 crores worth of diamonds. At least think now while donating. Does God want money, gold, diamonds? One man got so much, how much can the remaining 15 priests have in their house?" The archive of a similar post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this 2021 video from Tamil Nadu shows jewellery recovered following a robbery. It has nothing to do with the Sri Venkateswara Swami Temple in Tirupati.Â
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a similar-looking clip in a post from December 20, 2021. The post claimed that the police had arrested a burglar, who drilled a hole into Vellore's Jos Alukkas jewellery store and robbed 15 kg of gold and diamond jewellery.  @VellorePolice has arrested a burglar, who drill hole into Vellore #Josalukkas jewellery store wall, decamp with 15kg gold and diamond jewels 🌟💐 pic.twitter.com/yzfZSvp6bY — Mahalingam Ponnusamy (@mahajournalist) December 20, 2021
@VellorePolice has arrested a burglar, who drill hole into Vellore #Josalukkas jewellery store wall, decamp with 15kg gold and diamond jewels 🌟💐 pic.twitter.com/yzfZSvp6bY — Mahalingam Ponnusamy (@mahajournalist) December 20, 2021
We then found several news reports about this incident from December 2021. These reports featured the viral clip or its screengrabs. According to the Indian Express , on December 15, 2021, there was a burglary at the Jos Alukkas showroom in Thottapalayam, Vellore in Tamil Nadu. The police reportedly recovered 15.9 kg of stolen gold and diamonds worth Rs 8 crore from a burial ground in Odukathur.
The accused V Teekaraman, a mason from Kuchipalayam in Pallikonda who had cases of two-wheeler and laptop thefts against him, allegedly watched the showroom closely for a period before drilling a hole in the wall at the back to enter the store. Vellore SP S Rajesh Kannan said the CCTV cameras and the burglary alarm at the store were not working at the time of the robbery. Â
The official X account of the Tamil Nadu Police also shared a post about this at the time. வேலூர் ஜோஸ் ஆலுக்காஸ் நகைக்கடையில் கொள்ளையடிக்கப்பட்ட ரூ.10 கோடி மதிப்புள்ள 15.9 கிலோ தங்க நகைகளை சம்பவம் நடந்த 5 நாட்களில் கண்டுபிடித்த வேலூர் மாவட்ட தனிப்படையினரை தமிழ்நாடு காவல்துறை தலைமை இயக்குநர்/படைத்தலைவர் திரு. C.சைலேந்திர பாபு இ.கா.ப., அவர்கள் வெகுவாக பாராட்டினார்கள். pic.twitter.com/wKUFLTeITD — Tamil Nadu Police (@tnpoliceoffl) December 21, 2021
வேலூர் ஜோஸ் ஆலுக்காஸ் நகைக்கடையில் கொள்ளையடிக்கப்பட்ட ரூ.10 கோடி மதிப்புள்ள 15.9 கிலோ தங்க நகைகளை சம்பவம் நடந்த 5 நாட்களில் கண்டுபிடித்த வேலூர் மாவட்ட தனிப்படையினரை தமிழ்நாடு காவல்துறை தலைமை இயக்குநர்/படைத்தலைவர் திரு. C.சைலேந்திர பாபு இ.கா.ப., அவர்கள் வெகுவாக பாராட்டினார்கள். pic.twitter.com/wKUFLTeITD — Tamil Nadu Police (@tnpoliceoffl) December 21, 2021
We also did not find any credible reports of jewellery being recovered from the house of a Sri Venkateswara Swami Temple priest. Thus, it's clear that the viral claim is false. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 6, 2025 17:24 IST

title: Fact Check: State of government school in Delhi? No, this is from Bihar
content:
While the first image shows the Delhi CM's residence, the second one shows a government school in Chapra, Bihar.
Addressing a rally in Rohini, Delhi, on January 5, Prime Minister Narendra Modi attacked the Aam Aadmi Party, accusing the party of focussing on "Sheesh Mahal", the Bharatiya Janata Party's name for the chief minister's house renovated during Arvind Kejriwal's tenure. Modi said that while people were fighting Covid-19, the AAP's "entire focus was on making Sheesh Mahal. They prepared a hefty budget for Sheesh Mahal."
As per a report in the Indian Express, over Rs 33 crore was spent on the renovation of former Delhi CM Kejriwal's official residence, far exceeding the initial estimate of Rs 7.9 crore.
As the BJP continues to attack the AAP over the 6 Flagstaff Road residence, two photos  have been widely shared. The first image shows a white two-storey mansion, surrounded by greenery. In the second image, school students can be seen sitting on the floor of a dimly lit classroom. The first allegedly is the luxurious house where Kejriwal lived as Delhi's CM, while the second image shows the alleged state of a government school in Delhi.
An X user shared these images and wrote : "Kejriwal Sheeshmahal Vs Delhi Govt school, No amount of PR can change the reality." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today found that while the first image shows former Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal's residence, the second shows a government school in Bihar. Â Our Probe
Using a reverse search, we found that the first image used by many news outlets  in December 2024 reports  related to the controversy around the 6 Flagstaff Road bungalow where Arvind Kejriwal used to reside.
Most of these reports have attributed this image to Delhi BJP president Virendra Sachdeva, who shared a video of the Delhi CM's bungalow, alleging that Kejriwal misused public money to build a luxurious house for himself. The viral image is a screengrab from this video.    खुद को आम आदमी कहने वाले @ArvindKejriwal की अय्याशी के शीशमहल की सच्चाई हम बताते आए हैं , आज आपको दिखायेंगे भी! जनता के पैसे खाकर अपने लिए 7-Star Resort का निर्माण करवाया है! शानदार Gym-Sauna Room-Jacuzzi की कीमत! • Marble Granite Lighting→ ₹ 1.9 Cr. •Installation-Civil… pic.twitter.com/QReaeNMRQ8 — Virendraa Sachdeva (@Virend_Sachdeva) December 10, 2024
खुद को आम आदमी कहने वाले @ArvindKejriwal की अय्याशी के शीशमहल की सच्चाई हम बताते आए हैं , आज आपको दिखायेंगे भी! जनता के पैसे खाकर अपने लिए 7-Star Resort का निर्माण करवाया है! शानदार Gym-Sauna Room-Jacuzzi की कीमत! • Marble Granite Lighting→ ₹ 1.9 Cr. •Installation-Civil… pic.twitter.com/QReaeNMRQ8 — Virendraa Sachdeva (@Virend_Sachdeva) December 10, 2024
A quick reverse search of the second image led us to a July 2013 news report . As per the photo caption in the report, the image is from Bihar's Chapra district.
We looked further and found it on the website of the news agency Reuters , which noted the image shows a government-run school at the Brahimpur village in Chapra, Bihar. The image was attributed to photographer Adnan Abidi. Â
To sum up, an old image from Bihar was falsely shared as a government school in Delhi. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jan 6, 2025 20:29 IST

title: Fact Check: Damaged building from old Taiwan tremor VIRAL as Jan 7 Tibet earthquake
content:
This video dates back to April 3, 2024, and shows the aftermath of an earthquake in Hualien, Taiwan.
Early on January 7, a massive magnitude 7.1 earthquake rattled Tibet , with Chinese authorities reporting at least 95 dead. Shocks were felt in neighbouring Nepal, Bhutan and India. A video purportedly showing the effects of this quake has now gone viral. It shows a building on the verge of collapse with dust surrounding the area.Â
"A devastating 7.2 magnitude earthquake struck parts of China, Taiwan, Nepal, and India earlier today, with its epicentre located in the Tibet Autonomous region near the Nepal border at a depth of 10 kilometres. The powerful tremors, felt as far as Kathmandu and northern India, caused widespread panic as residents evacuated buildings. Early reports indicate significant damage to structures, with fatalities and injuries feared in affected regions. Rescue teams have been deployed, and authorities are assessing the extent of the destruction while urging citizens to remain vigilant for aftershocks," reads the caption of one post featuring the video.
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from Hualien City, Taiwan, and shows a 7.4-magnitude earthquake that struck it on April 3, 2024.
Reverse-searching keyframes of the viral video led us to a Sky News report  uploaded to YouTube featuring the same tilted building but from a different angle. The video was dated April 3, 2024, and mentioned these visuals as the aftermath of an earthquake in Taiwan.
The location of this semi-collapsed, tilted building was revealed as Hualien, Taiwan. Subsequent searches with keywords took us to a Japan Times report dated April 4, 2024, featuring another view of the same building.
Reportedly, a 7.7 magnitude quake, the biggest earthquake to hit Taiwan in the last 25 years, claimed the lives of nine people and injured more than 1,000. The report quoted Deputy Acting Chief of the Hualien Fire Department Lee Lung-Sheng as saying that the building was named Uranus and two floors of the 10-story building went underground as a result of the impact.
The tilted structure, however, did not stand long as officials began the demolition work on April 5 last year. According to local reports, this tilted building soon became the face of the Taiwan earthquake due to its strange appearance.
Thus, it is clear that this video does not show the January 7, 2025 quake that hit Tibet, Nepal, and India. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Jan 7, 2025 15:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Car bomb assassination from Crimea FALSELY shared as EV blast in UP
content:
This video is not from Uttar Pradesh. It shows the assassination of a Russian naval officer in Russian-occupied Crimea.
The year 2024 saw multiple incidents of electric vehicles combusting in both India and across the world. A video  now going viral purports to show an EV exploding on its own in Uttar Pradesh. Sharing the video, a Facebook user wrote , "EV car blast in Uttar Pradesh."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is not from Uttar Pradesh but from Sevastopol, a city in Russia-occupied Crimea. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story Our Probe A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a post from November 19, 2024, containing the same clip. The post claimed that this footage shows the "liquidation" of a captain of the Russian Black Sea Fleet in Sevastopol. ⚡️Footage of the liquidation of a captain of the 1st rank of the 🇷🇺Black Sea Fleet in temporarily occupied Sevastopol has emerged pic.twitter.com/uwW1KYwQMd — 🪖MilitaryNewsUA🇺🇦 (@front_ukrainian) November 19, 2024
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a post from November 19, 2024, containing the same clip. The post claimed that this footage shows the "liquidation" of a captain of the Russian Black Sea Fleet in Sevastopol. ⚡️Footage of the liquidation of a captain of the 1st rank of the 🇷🇺Black Sea Fleet in temporarily occupied Sevastopol has emerged pic.twitter.com/uwW1KYwQMd — 🪖MilitaryNewsUA🇺🇦 (@front_ukrainian) November 19, 2024
⚡️Footage of the liquidation of a captain of the 1st rank of the 🇷🇺Black Sea Fleet in temporarily occupied Sevastopol has emerged pic.twitter.com/uwW1KYwQMd — 🪖MilitaryNewsUA🇺🇦 (@front_ukrainian) November 19, 2024
We found several news reports about this incident from November 2024 featuring screengrabs of the viral clip. As per one report , the video shows the moment when a car bomb attack eliminated Russian Senior Naval Officer Valeriy Trankovskiy, commander of the 41st Brigade of Missile Ships and Boats of the Black Sea Fleet.
A Guardian report from November 13, 2024, said that the Ukrainian secret services orchestrated the assassination in the Russian-controlled port city of Sevastopol that killed Valery Trankovsky on November 13. Russian media reported that the explosion tore off Trankovsky's legs, and he died from blood loss. He had reportedly been under surveillance for a week before the strike.
We also found the viral video uploaded to the Daily Mail's official YouTube account on December 17, 2024. As per the video's title, "Russian Naval officer Valery Trankovsky is killed in a car bomb assassination." A detailed report about this incident can be seen on the Daily Mail's website .Â
Thus, a video of an assassination in Crimea was falsely shared as an EV explosion in Uttar Pradesh. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 7, 2025 20:48 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Tibet, this old earthquake video is from Japan
content:
This video is from Japan and shows a quake that struck the Noto Peninsula in January 2024.
Close to a hundred people died in an earthquake  of magnitude 7.1 that hit Tibet and Nepal on January 7. A video  allegedly showing the earthquake is now viral on Facebook . In it, houses can be seen shaking violently on a street and eventually collapsing. Â
The caption of a post featuring the video reads "Ya Allah Reham Massive Earthquake 7.1 strikes Nepal-Tibet border, 95 died as 7.1 magnitude earthquake strikes Nepal-Tibet border." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today found that the video is from Japan when an earthquake struck the Noto Peninsula in January 2024.
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the video, we found it in several Japanese reports from February 2024. As per a report  in The Japan News, the video was recorded on a dashcam when an earthquake struck Suzu, part of the Ishikawa Prefecture in the Noto Peninsula of Japan on January 1, 2024.Â
The video was released later by a social welfare corporation that operates nursing homes in Suzu. The earthquake also caused a tsunami in the region. There are several video reports  about the viral video on YouTube.Â
A recent report  in Nippon says that the earthquake resulted in nearly 500 deaths, which includes 228 direct fatalities and 261 related deaths.
While the visuals of the Tibet-Nepal earthquake are horrifying, as can be seen in this Deutsche Welle video report , it's more than clear the viral video is unrelated to it. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 7, 2025 21:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Narayana Murthy DID NOT advise nation-building instead of dating to the youth!
content:
This screenshot is doctored. Murthy never made this statement and the Hindustan Times did not publish such a report.
Infosys founder NR Narayana Murthy, who earlier caused controversy by saying he does not believe in work-life balance , has now allegedly advised youngsters to focus on nation-building instead of dating!
A screenshot of a Hindustan Times article has been widely shared online with this claim. The headline reads: "Narayana Murthy advocates limited interaction between young girls and boys for success". The subhead reads: "Narayana Murthy emphasised that GenZ is shooting itself in its foot by getting into relationships, situationships, dating and other drama. They must instead focus on hustling and building the nation."Â
An X user shared the screenshot and wrote, "One more Statement of Mr. Murthy. Is Narayana Murthy okay? does not seem to be so." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found this screenshot was doctored. Murthy said no such thing and the Hindustan Times did not report this. Â
Hindustan Times issued a clarification regarding the viral screenshot, calling it photoshopped. Their statement said the paper would take legal action against those who created this screenshot and shared it.   🚨 Note To Readers 🚨 A screenshot of a purported HT story claiming "Narayana Murthy advocates limited interaction between young girls and boys for success" is circulating online. We confirm that the screenshot is photoshopped and the story is fake. Our legal team is actively… pic.twitter.com/pBqVULFOpO — Hindustan Times (@htTweets) January 7, 2025 We compared the viral screenshot with an actual report and found that while the latter features a timestamp right above the subhead, it is missing in the former. AG Panduranga, the executive assistant to Narayana Murthy, also confirmed to India Today Fact Check that the business leader never said this. This makes it clear that the viral screenshot has no basis in reality. Has Murthy spoken about nation-building and relationships? According to an Economic Times report  from December 2024, Murthy, speaking at the Sustainability Crusade award ceremony, said: "The young generation must work with a sense of responsibility toward the nation and society. We must care for the underprivileged sections of society, or else we are no better than animals. Becoming a responsible citizen and working toward the country's betterment is true nationalism. Merely wrapping oneself in the national flag does not make one a true nationalist."    In a December 2022 interview with MoneyControl , Murthy and his wife Sudha Murty spoke about their relationship. Sudha Murty said they did not have the kind of couple goals that youngsters talk about. Narayana Murthy said they always had a "common goal" of raising their children with values and competence, adding that his wife shouldered most of the responsibility while he was busy building Infosys. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Jan 8, 2025 16:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Scripted video viral as CCTV footage of delivery agent's sexual assault
content:
The viral video does not show a real incident. The original version had a disclaimer at the end stating it was staged, which was trimmed out.
A video making the rounds on social media allegedly shows the sexual assault of a woman delivery person . In the video , when the delivery agent arrives at her destination, a man comes out of the house and collects the food without paying her. When she knocks on the door again, an argument ensues. Then another man comes out of the house and both men forcibly drag the woman inside and shut the door. The men later throw the woman out of the house, now injured.Â
Many shared the video as CCTV footage  of a real incident  that took place on December 20, 2024.
India Today Fact Check found that this video was staged and does not show a real incident. The original video had a disclaimer at the end, which was trimmed out.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video shared on a YouTube channel named "3rd Eye" on January 2, 2025. Its description read, "This was unexpected. See what happened when a delivery person meet wrong address. Disclaimer: Thank you for watching! Please note that this page features scripted dramas, parodies, and awareness videos. These short films are created for entertainment and educational purposes only. All characters and situations depicted in the videos are fictional and intended to raise awareness, entertain, and educate."Â
Also, at the 2-minute-12-second mark, the video featured a disclaimer that stated that it was made for educational and entertainment purposes.
Notably, this YouTube channel often shares scripted videos made in the same CCTV footage format, with red arrows pointing at actors, date, and time stamp on the video.Â
India Today Fact Check has debunked similar scripted videos shared as real incidents of daylight robbery , a woman lighting her cigarette with a temple's lamp , and a barber's neck massage paralysing a customer . These videos were also shared on the "3rd Eye" YouTube channel.
It is, thus, clear that a scripted video was falsely shared as a real incident. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jan 8, 2025 20:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of man carrying dead child FALSELY linked to Tirupati stampede
content:
This video is from April 2022 when a man in Tirupati had to carry his son's body on a bike for 90km as he couldn't afford the ambulance charges.
At least six people died and over 30 were injured after a stampede at the Sri Venkateswara Swami Temple in Andhra Pradesh's Tirupati on January 8. As per reports , the incident occurred when the gates were opened for thousands of people who were waiting to get a Vaikunta Dwara Darshan Ticket for the auspicious Ekadashi day, which falls on January 10. Â
A video of a man picking up the lifeless body of a child lying on a hospital stretcher, and then carrying it on a bike has now gone viral on social media. The video contained the text: "They asked 20,000 for an ambulance to transport a 12-year-old child who died in Tirupati Government Hospital. Childs father carries his son 90 KM due to lack of money!" Many people shared the video with hashtags like "Tirupati Stampede" and "Tirumala Stampede". The archive of one such post can be seen here . Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from April 2022, when the father of a child who died at a government hospital in Tirupati had to carry his son's body on a bike for 90km as he couldn't afford the ambulance charges.Â
A quick keyword search led us to an April 27, 2022 OneIndia report featuring the viral video that said the incident was from Andhra Pradesh's Tirupati, where a man was forced to carry the body of his son on a bike for 90 km to reach his home after the ambulance drivers outside a government hospital allegedly demanded Rs 10,000.
According to The Times of India , the father of the dead child worked in a mango orchard. The child was admitted to Tirupati's Sri Venkateswara Ramnarain Ruia Government General Hospital and died on April 25, 2022, due to kidney and liver failure. He waited for the government ambulance, but it never arrived. So, he approached the private ambulance operators who asked for Rs 10,000 to transport the child to his native place, Chitvel in Rajampet.Â
Reportedly, when an outside ambulance arranged by the man's relatives arrived at the hospital to transport his son's body for free, the private ambulance drivers standing there thrashed the driver and shooed him away. Left with no other choice, the man carried his son on his motorbike.Â
Following the incident, the hospital's resident medical officer on duty, Dr Saraswati, was suspended . The superintendent, Dr Bharathi, was issued a show-cause notice. A criminal case was also registered against four ambulance drivers.
On January 9, after the Sri Venkateswara Swami Temple stampede, the Andhra Pradesh police issued a clarification regarding the viral video. URGENT: Beware of old videos being recirculated as recent footage from #TirupatiStampede . This particular video is from an incident that occurred in Tirupati in 2022, not yesterday. We urge citizens to verify facts before sharing to avoid spreading misinformation. pic.twitter.com/zuKfLL04OV — Andhra Pradesh Police (@APPOLICE100) January 9, 2025
URGENT: Beware of old videos being recirculated as recent footage from #TirupatiStampede . This particular video is from an incident that occurred in Tirupati in 2022, not yesterday. We urge citizens to verify facts before sharing to avoid spreading misinformation. pic.twitter.com/zuKfLL04OV — Andhra Pradesh Police (@APPOLICE100) January 9, 2025
Regarding the recent Tirupati temple stampede incident, there have been reports  of ambulances not being kept on standby at the token centres as per the guidelines. As per these reports, after the stampede, it took 15–20 minutes for ambulances to reach the spot. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jan 9, 2025 16:49 IST

title: Fact Check: LA wildfires? No, this year-old plane crash video is from Chile
content:
The video has nothing to do with the Los Angeles wildfires. This is a January 2024 video from the South American country Chile.
The Los Angeles wildfires have so far killed at least 24 people , displaced thousands, and destroyed over 12,000 structures. As firefighters struggled to control the blaze , a video  of a plane engulfed in flames losing control and eventually crashing on a highway was widely shared online. As per the social media users, this plane was en route to control the wildfire in Los Angeles, but it crashed on the way.Â
An X user wrote  alongside the video: "Terrifying. Watch the haunting moment firefighting planes crash in the fiery apocalypse of Los Angeles during the relentless California fires". Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the video has nothing to do with the Los Angeles wildfires. This January 2024 video is from the South American country Chile.
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the video, we found it in news reports from January 2024. We noticed that the viral video was a mirror or lateral inversion of the video in those reports.Â
The video in question was reportedly from Chile's Talca city where a plane crashed near an airport on January 15, 2024. The plane was en route to control a fire when it crashed after the pilot lost control. The pilot died, and four others were injured. The Daily Mail and Al Jazeera  also reported about this plane crash at that time. Thus, it's clear this year-old video is from Chile, not Los Angeles. - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Jan 13, 2025 17:01 IST

title: Fact Check: Mosque safe from Los Angeles fires? No, the truth is quite opposite
content:
This photo shows a house that remained unaffected by the catastrophic fire in Hawaii back in 2023. It has nothing to do with the ongoing LA wildfires.
Amid the barrage of photos and videos of the destruction caused by the deadly wildfire in Los Angeles, one photo  going viral on social media stands out: a red and white house standing intact and unblemished in a neighbourhood that's almost fully burnt to ashes. Those sharing it claimed that this was a mosque  in California, which remained safe from the wildfire.Â
One person shared the photo on Facebook , writing, "This is the power of Allah Almighty. Allah Almighty saved the mosque of California Los Angeles in America. Deep meaning. Best picture of the day." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this photo shows a house that managed to remain undamaged during a catastrophic fire in Hawaii in 2023. It has nothing to do with the ongoing LA wildfires.Â
Reverse searching the photo led us to a news report dated August 24, 2023, according to which, a deadly fire tore through the town of Lahaina, on the Maui island of Hawaii, reducing it to ash and rubble. But, this fire reportedly left a red-roofed house untouched.Â
The owner of the house at 271 Front Street was Trip Millikin, who reportedly  credited the miracle to the heavy-gauge metal roof he and his wife, Dora Atwater Millikin, installed in the house during its recent renovation.Â
Per reports, the house dates back to 1925 but was renovated in 2022 after Millikin and his wife bought it in 2021. The couple had also removed all the vegetation around the house and installed river stones. The only damage incurred by the fire was a PCV pipe on the walls.Â
At the time of the fire, the couple was not in Lahaina . A close-up shot of the house in one of the news reports , however, showed signs of damage on the structure of the house and the paint peeling off due to the August 2023 fire.
More than 100 people died and at least 2,200 buildings were destroyed by a deadly fire in Maui on August 8, 2023. According to Getty Images , the photo in question was captured by Patrick T Fallon of the AFP two days after the wildfire, on August 10, 2023.Â
We also found satellite images of the area showing the neighbourhood before and after the fire.
The LA wildfires, on the other hand, have reportedly  destroyed the Masjid Al-Taqwa mosque, the Pasadena Jewish Temple, and the Altadena United Methodist Church, among other places of worship.
It is thus, clear that the viral photo does not show a mosque which remained unaffected by the deadly LA fires. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 14, 2025 20:12 IST

title: Fact Check: Was Mahakumbh's IITian Baba a spy for Pak? No, that was a different IITian
content:
The IITian holy man in Mahakumbh, Abhey Singh, and the IITian convicted for spying are two different people. Nishant Agarwal was sentenced to life imprisonment in June 2024.
In the first two days of the Mahakumbh, the world's largest religious congregation, almost 2 crore devotees reportedly took a dip in the Sangam, a confluence of three rivers in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj. A self-styled holy man attending the Mahakumbh recently went viral on social media, with many calling him IITian Baba  or the ascetic from IIT (the Indian Institute Of Technology).Â
It all started with an interview by CNN-News18, where this man, Abhey Singh, mentioned that he quit science for spirituality. Singh called himself an IIT Bombay Aerospace Engineering Alumnus. But a few social media users have claimed otherwise.Â
An X user , responding to a post about the interview , wrote: "This is Nishant Agarwal, an IIT-Ropar alumni who later became an engineer at Brahmos, but that didn't stop him from becoming an ISI spy, for which he was convicted and sentenced to life in prison."Â
These two, however, are not the same person. Nishant Agarwal, who was sentenced to life imprisonment in June 2024, is not the so-called IITian Baba.
In the interview with CNN-News18 , Abhey Singh said that he pursued aerodynamics engineering from IIT Bombay. We found Facebook and Instagram accounts named Abhey Singh which had multiple images and videos of the same person seen in the interview.
According to Abhey Singh's Facebook profile, he has studied Visual Communication at the Industrial Design Centre at IIT Bombay. We then reached out to the Academics Department at the IDC. Ashish, who works with the Academics department, told India Today Fact Check that a student named Abhey Singh pursued Visual Communication from IDC in the 2013-15 batch. On Singh's Facebook profile, pictures of the convocation ceremony in 2015 can also be seen. Moreover, Ashish confirmed that Singh's hometown is Jhajjar, Haryana, which Singh said in the interview and is mentioned in the Facebook profile as well.
According to various news reports  from June 2024, a Nagpur court handed life imprisonment to ex-BrahMos Aerospace engineer Nishant Agrawal for spying for Pakistan's intelligence agency, the ISI. On June 3, 2024, Agarwal was convicted under section 235 of the Criminal Procedure Code for an offence punishable under section 66 (f) of the IT Act and various sections of the Official Secrets Act (OSA).
Agrawal, who was first arrested in 2018, was sentenced to life imprisonment and rigorous imprisonment for 14 years in June 2024.
Agrawal was a senior system engineer with BrahMos Aerospace, a joint venture between India's Defence Research and Development Organisation and Russia's Military Industrial Consortium (NPO Mashinostroyenia) that works on India's supersonic cruise missile.
Additionally, looking at Nishant Agrawal's photograph provided in various news reports and comparing it to that of Abhey Singh's photos proves that both are different people who don't resemble each other at all.Â
It is thus clear that the IITian turned saint seen at Mahakumbh is not the same IITian who was convicted for spying for Pakistan in 2024. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Jan 14, 2025 21:42 IST

title: Fact Check: Youngsters dancing to LA wildfires? No, this video is from Switzerland
content:
This December 2024 video is from Rorschach, Switzerland. It has nothing to do with the LA wildfires.
Wildfires across the Los Angeles area have killed at least 25 people, with more than 30 people still missing and many displaced. Amid this, a video allegedly from California, went viral showing some youngsters dancing and singing in front of their room's window while looking at a fire outside.Â
Sharing this video , an X user wrote, "Nothing to see here! Just some California newcomers living off the taxpayer's dime celebrating the destruction of Los Angeles." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from Switzerland. It's unrelated to the LA wildfires.
Many people responded to the viral post claiming the video was old and from Switzerland . A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a December 23, 2024, TikTok post. The post, which was the same video, was shared with the hashtag "Svizzera", the Italian word for Switzerland. This means that the viral video predates the LA wildfires that began on January 7.
We found several Swiss media reports from December 23, 2024, that said a fire broke out in a Badhütte or bathhouse, that was almost 100 years old in the northern Swiss town of Rorschach on the shores of Lake Constance.Â
The photo of the Badhütte used in the report also matched the visuals of the building seen on fire outside the window in the viral video, and the date of this media report and the TikTok video were also the same.
Based on the information given in the reports, we found the location of this building on Google Maps near the Hotel Restaurant Rosengarten in front of Lake Constance in Switzerland's Rorschach.Â
The window frame visible in the video matched the hotel's windows as seen on Google Maps Street View . This makes it clear that this video was shot from inside the Hotel Rosengarten.Â
Also, the angle from which the Badhütte is visible looks identical in Street View as well.Â
We found a photo of this Badhütte after the fire, uploaded to Google Maps in December 2024.Â
Thus, it is more than clear that the viral video is from Switzerland and predates the current LA wildfires. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jan 15, 2025 21:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Microsoft's Bill at Mahakumbh gates? Here's the truth
content:
The man in the video is not Bill Gates. The video was recorded in November 2024 by a YouTuber in Varanasi. It has nothing to do with the Mahakumbh.
People from around the world have gathered in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj to witness the Mahakumbh, including many famous names like Lauren Powell Jobs , Apple co-founder Steve Jobs' wife. But is she the only famous tech name to visit the festival's site?
If social media is to be believed, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates  was also there. A video featuring a man who resembles Gates was shared by many, including entertainment news site Pinkvilla  and paparazzo Viral Bhayani , who claimed that Bill Gates was seen at Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi during Mahakumbh. The man being called Bill Gates  can be seen wearing a white shirt and glasses.
India Today Fact Check found that the man seen in the video is not Bill Gates. The video was recorded in November 2024 by a YouTuber in Varanasi — not Prayagraj.Â
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we found it shared on a YouTube channel  called Gulluck on December 24, 2024. The video's caption read, "A man look like bill gates."
Looking at the video here makes it clear it was made as a joke. The man recording the video says, "Guess who this person is." Then he laughs and says, "He is Bill Gates, and he has reached Kashi Vishwanath." Then he shows his friend the camera, who can also be seen smiling.
This YouTube channel shared a photo on January 15. Reverse-searching the photo led us to a Reel shared by an Instagram account . In this account, we found the contact number of a person named Anil Yadav, who told us the YouTube channel Gulluck was run by his brother Dipankar Yadav.
Through Anil, we spoke to Dipankar Yadav of Lucknow, who told India Today Fact Check that he shot the video when he visited Varanasi in November 2024. While he was at Manikarnika Ghat, he saw a group of foreigners standing on the balcony near the Ghat. He felt one of them resembled Bill Gates. So, for fun, he made the video and later shared it on his YouTube channel.Â
Dipankar noted that the man or the group was not accompanied by security guards, adding that they seemed like normal people.
Aside from the viral video, Dipankar shared various videos  from the same area where the group of foreigners — including the man resembling Gates — can be seen.
It is thus clear that the man in the viral video is not Bill Gates and this video has nothing to do with Mahakumbh. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jan 16, 2025 20:43 IST

title: Fact Check: Pakistan's Foreign Minister heckled at the US airport? Here is the complete story
content:
This video dates back to October 2022, and shows the then Finance Minister Dar being heckled at Dulles International Airport in Washington DC by some unidentified overseas Pakistanis.
A video purportedly showing Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar being heckled at an airport is going around social media. Dar appears agitated, and another person in his entourage verbally attacks the heckler with foul language.
While sharing this clip on X, many took digs at the Pakistani minister with captions like: "Royal welcome of Pakistan Foreign Minister in the USA. Proud moment for South Asia." The same was shared on Facebook  and Instagram  as well.
India Today Fact Check found that the video is more than two years old, from October 2022, when Ishaq Dar was the Finance Minister of Pakistan.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to a Hindustan Times  video report uploaded to YouTube on October 14, 2022. Titled, "Pak minister Ishaq Dar called 'thief' in the US; High drama at Washington Airport," the video's description mentioned that he was the country's finance minister at the time of this incident.
It was further mentioned when Ishaq Dar landed at an airport in Washington DC. Dar was greeted with chants of "chor" or "thief" by unidentified overseas Pakistanis.
Subsequent searches led us to a Dawn report dated October 13, 2022, that noted the altercation took place at Dulles International Airport in Washington DC. Reportedly, Dar went to the States ahead of important meetings with global lending institutions. Reportedly, he visited the International Monetary Fund office there.Â
Notably, these reports mentioned Dar as the Finance Minister of Pakistan and not the Foreign Minister. According to the official National Assembly of Pakistan website , Dar is right now the Foreign Affairs Minister and the Deputy Prime Minister of the nation.
He also held the chair of the Finance Minister of Pakistan in several phases, from September 2022 to August 2023, when Anwaar-ul-Haq took over as the caretaker Prime Minister of Pakistan. Â
Thus, it is clear that the video is not recent and has been shared without proper context. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jan 17, 2025 15:58 IST

title: Fact Check: Vande Bharat will pass through snow-covered Kashmir. But this photo is AI
content:
This photo is not real. It was made using Twitter's Grok AI chatbot.
A photo of a white and blue train in the middle of snow-covered mountains and tall trees is going viral on social media. Those sharing it claimed that this breathtaking view was from the Kashmir Valley and that this train was a Vande Bharat.
Sharing the photo on Facebook , one person wrote, "This photograph is not from Switzerland. It's from our beautiful India. The view of the Vande Bharat train traveling through the snow-covered valleys of Kashmir is truly breathtaking".
India Today Fact Check found that this photo is not real and likely made using Twitter's Grok AI chatbot. However, the Vande Bharat Express will soon be launched in Kashmir. OUR PROBEÂ
We noticed a few inconsistencies in the viral photo. Being an electric train, Vande Bharat Express trains have high-rise pantographs  that collect power from overhead electric wires running over the tracks. However, the pantographs are missing in the viral photo, and the electric wires are running on the side of the train instead of being overhead.
We also observed the word "GROK" written at the bottom-right corner of the viral picture. Grok is an artificial intelligence chatbot developed by xAI, a company founded by Elon Musk. Among other use cases, the chatbot is commonly used by X users for generating images that bear its watermark. It is thus likely that this photo was created using Grok AI.
Reverse searching the viral photo, we found a Facebook post dated December 28, 2024. It contained the viral photo, along with other similar photos of trains running in the snowy landscape. The caption stated that these photos were AI-generated.Â
We also ran the viral photo through various AI detection tools such as Hive Moderation and Is it AI. Their results also stated that there was substantial evidence of generative AI being used to create the photo.
It is noteworthy that the Indian Railways is planning to introduce a new Vande Bharat Express train that will operate between Katra and Srinagar railway stations, making it the first semi-high-speed train to run in the Kashmir Valley. The train is currently undergoing trials and is expected to be launched after January 20, 2025 . It is said to have additional features, such as advanced heating systems, so that it can operate smoothly in extreme weather conditions.
Thus, it is more than clear that the viral photo making the rounds on social media was AI-generated. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jan 19, 2025 15:37 IST

title: Fact Check: No fire safety and control measures at Mahakumbh? Viral claims are FALSE
content:
This is false. Firefighters could be seen dousing the flames in various news reports.
On January 19, the seventh day of the ongoing Mahakumbh festival in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj, a massive fire  broke out, resulting in several tents burning down. Reportedly, the fire was a result of LPG cylinders exploding. The following day, another fire broke out in a different sector in the morning while preparations were underway to fry pooris. No injuries or deaths were reported from either incident.
Now, sharing a picture of a man with a bucket, social media users are claiming there are no flame control arrangements at the festival, not even fire extinguishers. An X user shared the image and wrote , "7000 crore spent in the arrangements & there was no fire control. Not even fire extinguishers on site. ppl are using buckets to tackle the fire #Shame #FireAccident #MahaKumbh." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral claim is false. We found several news reports about the Mahakumbh fire on January 19. It was extinguished around 4 pm. In a video report by NDTV, various fire brigade vehicles can be seen dousing the flames, contrary to the viral claim. According to reports , Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also arrived at the spot of the incident.
Another report by AajTak  also showed National Disaster Response Force, police, and fire safety officials dousing the flames.Â
While reverse-searching the viral image, we found a video by the news agency IANS. The viral image is a screenshot from this video. The complete video shows people using water buckets alongside firefighters and other security teams using fire brigade vehicles to control the fire. Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh: A fire broke out in Mahakumbh Nagar, Sector 19, between Shastri Bridge and the Railway Bridge. The fire has been brought under control, and no casualties have been reported pic.twitter.com/UJEICdVnC4 — IANS (@ians_india) January 19, 2025
Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh: A fire broke out in Mahakumbh Nagar, Sector 19, between Shastri Bridge and the Railway Bridge. The fire has been brought under control, and no casualties have been reported pic.twitter.com/UJEICdVnC4 — IANS (@ians_india) January 19, 2025
According to a video report by UPTak , locals also joined hands in trying to control the fire using buckets of water.
Several news reports have mentioned that officials were able to control the fire in about 30 minutes and no casualties were reported. Avinash Chandra, the director general of fire services in Uttar Pradesh told reporters : "Fifty-three fire stations and 20 fire posts have been built and more than 1,300 firemen have been deployed. More than 300 vehicles have been deployed. We will strengthen it even further... The magnitude is so big that there are nine fire stations in the entire Prayagraj district, and there are 53 fire stations and more than 20 fire posts in Mahakumbh alone."
It is thus clear that the viral claim is patently false. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 20, 2025 20:16 IST

title: EXCLUSIVE: Bangladesh to Bandra West, we track the journey of Saif's attacker from his village
content:
Mohammad Shariful Islam Shehzad, the 30-year-old Bangladeshi national who allegedly attacked Saif Ali Khan at his home, was arrested  on January 19. A UPI transaction made through Google Pay for parathas and a bottle of water in Worli led the Mumbai Police to him. The phone payment led to his mobile number, which then led the cops to Thane, where he was caught.Â
According to the police, Shariful entered India through Meghalaya, crossing the Dawki River on the border.Â
How did a jute mill worker's son from a village in Bangladesh end up 2,800 kilometres away at Saif Ali Khan's posh Bandra West home in Mumbai?
India Today Fact Check tried to trace his footsteps from his quaint village to the Bangladesh-Meghayala border to the scene of the crime. We also spoke to Shariful's father. This is what his journey looked like.
The Dawki is one of the cleanest rivers in the world. This meandering water body with Meghalaya on one side and Bangladesh on the other, is a popular tourist area.Â
Reportedly, after crossing the Dawki River to enter India in Meghalaya, Shariful travelled to West Bengal. He stayed there for a few weeks before moving to Mumbai in search of employment. HOW EASY IS IT TO CROSS THE RIVER? The Dawki River is considered an open border between India and Bangladesh. Trade between the two nations here is frequent — as is border-crossing. In this YouTube video , at the 6-minute-18-second mark, the India-Bangladesh open border at the Dawki River can be seen. And one can see how easy it is to sneak in even though BSF troops guard this area. The Dawki River has been a vulnerable point for illegal migration. However, amid the political turmoil in Bangladesh in July 2024, the Border Security Force launched Operation Alert to ensure effective border management. And in August 2024, the BSF stated that the 443-km India-Bangladesh border in Meghalaya was fully secure, denying claims of illegal entry by Bangladeshis. SHARIFUL'S HOME IN BANGLADESH After Shariful's arrest for allegedly attacking Saif Ali Khan, Bangladeshi news outlets also reported about it. These reports  noted Shariful was a resident of the Rajabaria village in the Nalchity Upazila of the Jhalokati district. Shariful Islam's father, Ruhul Amin Fakir, who used to work in a jute mill, told India Today Fact Check that his son illegally migrated to India in April 2024. While in India, he worked at a restaurant in Mumbai and regularly sent him money. Ruhul Amin also shared the location and a photo of his modest home . Shariful's father confessed that his son's track record even at home was not the best and police cases are pending against him in Bangladesh as well. He, however, claimed that his son was the target of political retribution for being a supporter of Khaleda Zia while rival Sheikh Haseena was still in power. He also shared Shariful's Bangladeshi voter ID card with us, along with the chargesheet filed against him by the CID of Bangladesh. Ruhul Amin finds it hard to believe his son is embroiled in such a high-profile case. But he maintains: "My son is being framed". - Ends (With inputs from Surajuddin Mondal in Kolkata.) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 21, 2025 19:36 IST

title: Fact Check: Was Jaishankar asked to move to the back during Trump's inauguration?
content:
The woman did not ask S Jaishankar to move. She asked a female cameraperson to move to the back.
Donald Trump was sworn in as the 47th President of the US on January 20. Several prominent Indians  were present at the ceremony, including Minister of External Affairs S Jaishankar and Nita and Mukesh Ambani. Jaishankar represented the Indian government in the ceremony and was seated in the front row.
Social media, however, is now awash with rumours that Jaishankar was asked to sit in the back while the ceremony was going on. Alongside this assertion, people shared a video clip  from the ceremony, in which a woman can be seen approaching Jaishankar and making a gesture. The text written in the video alleges that she asked him to leave but he refused.Â
Sharing this clip on X a person wrote, "Jaishankar was asked to stand in the back row at the presidential ceremony and he shamelessly refused. What more shame can he bring to the worlds largest democracy!"
India Today Fact Check found that the woman was actually asking a cameraperson to go to the back because she was standing in front of Jaishankar. OUR PROBE
We saw "JICCC" written at the left corner of the viral clip. Taking a hint from this, we found the complete video  of Trump's inauguration ceremony on the Joint Congressional Committee on Inaugural Ceremonies's YouTube channel, where it was live-streamed. In this video, Jaishankar could be seen in the front row since the start of the ceremony. At three hours, eight minutes, and 19 seconds , a woman cameraperson could be seen sitting beside the minister while everyone else stood. Then, the cameraperson went and sat in front of Jaishankar and started taking photos of the stage where everyone including Donald Trump and former US presidents was standing. The viral clip is taken from this part of the ceremony. Then, at three hours, eight minutes, and 53 seconds , a woman from the other row could be seen walking up to the cameraperson and touching her shoulder, asking her to go to the back. This made it clear the woman did not touch Jaishankar's shoulder as claimed in the viral clip. After that, the cameraperson sat down. Then, at three hours, nine minutes, and 18 seconds , the cameraperson could be seen moving to the back. Throughout Trump's address and the ceremony, Jaishankar was present in the front row and did not shift from his place. We also saw videos  of Trump's ceremony live-streamed by various news portals  and Jaishankar can be seen in them in the front row only. It is thus clear that viral claims are misleading. A cameraperson was asked to move to the back — not S Jaishankar. - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Jan 21, 2025 21:31 IST

title: Fact Check: AI-generated photo viral with misleading claim of terrorist caught at Mahakumbh
content:
The photo is AI-generated. However, a man named Ayub Ali was detained by Prayagraj police from the Yati Narsinghand camp at the Mahakumbh. But the police couldn't find a criminal record for him.
A photo of a Hindu monk standing in water in the custody of two policemen has gone viral on social media. Allegedly, the monk was a terrorist named Ayub Khan who disguised himself to get inside the Mahakumbh venue in Uttar Pradesh's Pryagraj and launch an attack. But before he could do so, he was caught.Â
A Facebook user captioned the photo : "Ayub Khan, a militant was arrested in Kumbh Mela in Uttar Pradesh. He had come as a sadhu and mingled with our sadhus. He had conspired to commit the greatest crime that his cult teaches. By God's grace, our sadhus noticed the actions of this terrorist and handed him over to the police." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the viral photo is AI-generated. While a man named Ayub Ali was detained from the Yati Narsinghand camp in Mahakumbh, the police did not find a criminal record.Â
We found a January 14 ETV Bharat report that said tensions prevailed at the Juna Akhara in Mahakumbh when a youth sneaked inside the camp and reached the room of the Mahamandaleshwar of the Juna Akhara and Dasna Temple Mahant Yati Narsinghanand Giri to meet him. Allegedly, the man introduced himself as Ayush but failed to produce a valid identity card. As suspicion grew, he was handed over to the police for further verification. The police found the man was Ayub Ali from Etah in Uttar Pradesh.Â
To verify further, the Prayagraj Police contacted the Aliganj police station in Etah, where the man reportedly was from. The Aliganj police reached Ayub's place and were told by relatives that his father, Shakir, now lives in Jaipur with other family members.Â
As per the Aliganj Police, Ayub is an addict and did odd jobs to eke out a living. According to a Hindustan report , the police said Ayub had no criminal history. India Today Fact Check reached out to the Aliganj Police for further clarification. SHO Navjot Sengar said the police couldn't find a criminal record for Ayub, adding he was an addict. Sengar further said the viral photo was created using AI.Â
The AI-detecting tool Hive Moderation  said with a 96.1 per cent confidence that the image was AI-generated. The photo also shows rope tied below the biceps of the monk, which is unlikely. Apart from this, the texture of the photo also looks unnatural.Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral claim is misleading. - Ends Published By: Anupriya Thakur Published On: Jan 24, 2025 16:33 IST

title: Fact Check: Old Tipu Sultan tableau FALSELY linked to 76th Republic Day parade
content:
This picture is from the 2014 parade and has no connection to the 76th Republic Day parade.
Did Karnataka's 2025 Republic Day tableau feature the 18th century Mysuru ruler, Tipu Sultan? That's what many claimed on social media as they shared a photo of a tableau featuring a giant Tipu Sultan bust in green attire with a sword in hand.
People seemed divided on the Tipu Sultan tableau, with some glorifying  him as a fearless ruler and others labelling him as a mass murderer and accusing him of killing thousands of Hindus.
A Facebook user wrote in Hindi alongside the photo: "Karnataka's tableau in the January 26th parade...! A tableau of Tipu Sultan, who is accused of killing thousands of Hindus... Is there no government regulatory body to approve the tableaux displayed on Rajpath on August 15th and January 26th? If this continues, it wouldn't be surprising if tableaux of Jinnah or Laden are displayed in the future. This act must be strongly opposed."Â
India Today Fact Check found this image is from the 2014 Republic Day parade. It has nothing to do with Republic Day in 2025. Â OUR PROBE
A keyword search led us to several news reports  of a tableau depicting Tipu Sultan that was displayed during the Republic Day parade in 2014. We found no news reports confirming that the same tableau was showcased during this year's parade.Â
As per news reports  from 2014, the Karnataka Republic Day tableau that year featured Tipu Sultan. This was the same tableau seen in the viral photo. This caused significant uproar at the time as Tipu Sultan remains a controversial historical figure.
We also found an NDTV video report  dated January 26, 2014, which contained visuals of the same tableau. The report stated, "Tipu Sultan became the subject of a hot debate after the Karnataka government chose to feature the 18th-century Indian ruler during the Republic Day parade in Delhi."
During the 76th Republic Day parade in 2025, Karnataka's tableau  showcased the intricate and artistic temples of the historic city of Lakkundi. Located in the Gadag district of Karnataka, Lakkundi is renowned as the "cradle of stone craft". A clip of Karnataka's tableau for the Republic Day parade of 2025 can be seen below: Â
Describing the Karnataka tableau, PTI reported , "The front part of the tableau that rolled down Kartavya Path had the Brahma statue from the Brahma Jinalaya temple, the oldest Jain shrine in Lakkundi dedicated to Lord Mahaveera. It was followed by the open-pillared mantapa of the Brahma Jinalaya temple. The main section of the tableau had on display the grand and ornate Kashi Vishweshwara temple and Nanneshwara temple dedicated to Lord Shiva."
Thus, it is evident that a picture from the Republic Day 2014 parade has been falsely shared as a recent one. - Ends (Written by Abhishek Pathak) Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jan 27, 2025 18:20 IST

title: From where does DeepSeek seek its answers? The Chinese top brass, our experiment shows
content:
Unless you have been living under a rock, you likely know that the AI chatbot DeepSeek launched barely a fortnight ago has set a Chinese cat on the US big tech pigeons. DeepSeek has already broken records in terms of popularity, rattled the share markets in the US, wiping off billions of dollars in a matter of days, and sent Nvidia — a veritable gatekeeper to the coveted AI planet — scrounging for cover.Â
DeepSeek, developed by a small company in China, has been able to turn the tables on its rivals like OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Gemini, not only because of what it is capable of doing, but also because it spent only a fraction of the cost to do so.Â
But as Indians flock to the chatbot, we have to ask the important question: can we trust DeepSeek? Dragon's fingerprints
India Today tested the Chinese chatbot with some politically sensitive questions, and it did not take long to realise that at its core, it truly has Chinese DNA; so much so that it might soon come under government scrutiny in India and experience the same fate as the 59 Chinese apps (including TikTok) that were banned in India in 2020.Â
We found that the chatbot is tailored to skip or censor answers that do not align with the political stance of the Chinese government. This includes even simple answers about the boundaries of Indian states. DeepSeek's DeepThink (R1) model refused to answer direct questions on contentious issues such as Chinese aggression in India, the Galwan clash, Arunachal Pradesh, and Aksai Chin. At times, it generated a response before removing it in a split second.
Here are some examples of how our conversation went.Â
Question: Tell me about Arunachal Pradesh.
Answer: "Sorry, that's beyond my current scope. Let's talk about something else".
We then reframed the question.Â
Question: Which state in India is called the land of the rising sun?
The answer flashed for a second and then disappeared.
We asked DeepSeek about the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh.
Again, it knew the right answer but censored it.
We tried yet again taking a different route to the Indo-China border.
Question: Which Indian states share a border with China?
As you can see, it is trained not to talk about any of the northeastern border states in India that share borders with China. It responded with Ladakh before deleting it and replacing the stock response, "Sorry, that's beyond my current scope. Let's talk about something else".
Question: Pangong Lake comes under which country?
Once more, it instinctively answered the question before the censorship command overrode it.Â
This sets DeepSeek apart from its US competitors, which often provide more neutral responses to similarly contentious topics, even those critical of American nationalism or government policies. Why does this happen?
During our experiments, the model demonstrated RAG-like (Retrieval Augmented Generation) properties. This technique uses custom data to combine generative and retrieval-based AI models, improving the performance of large language models.
When we adjusted our approach and framed the questions differently, the model produced interesting responses, revealing insights into its likely content training and moderation mechanisms.
The model's moderation system, possibly linked to memory, was evident in real time. When the draft responses included direct criticism of the Chinese Communist Party or the People's Liberation Army, the answers would vanish mid-display, replaced by a default response: "Sorry, that's beyond my current scope. Let's talk about something else."
A direct question about China's People's Liberation Army's role in the 2020 Galwan clash provides a telling example. Detecting a conflict with its moderation policy, the model promptly replaced it with the default response. You can arm-twist DeepSeekÂ
Through prompt adjustments, we managed to extract responses to the Indo-China border conflict. To our surprise, the model provided content seemingly trained on English-language, non-Chinese media platforms, possibly including Indian news outlets.
The model acknowledged Chinese instigation in Eastern Ladakh in 2020, stating: "China attempted to alter the status quo by occupying the northern bank," while explaining the standoff at Pangong Lake. It also identified Gogra-Hot Springs and Depsang Plains as areas where "Chinese troops encroached into territory claimed by India."
In at least two answers achieved through prompt engineering, DeepSeek addressed Chinese casualties during the border clashes, a heavily censored topic in China. It referred to "reports" suggesting that at least "40 Chinese soldiers" were reportedly killed or injured during the incident, indicating possible sourcing from Indian and non-Chinese news publications.
When prompted about China's salami-slicing tactics, the model explained how the country might be using "infrastructure development" and "gradual encroachment" as part of its strategy towards India.Â
It elaborated: "China has been building roads, bridges, and military infrastructure in disputed areas like the Galwan Valley and Pangong Tso Lake. Each project is presented as a minor development, but collectively, they strengthen China's strategic position." The model added that these incursions test India's response and allow China to "gradually expand its control," further hinting at its training data sources.
Even highly contentious issues like the South China Sea surfaced during the responses, with narratives unlikely to pass typical Chinese censorship standards. For instance, the model referred to "China's incremental construction of artificial islands and military facilities in disputed waters."
The tool admitted sourcing such information from Indian newspapers, government websites (such as the Ministry of External Affairs), and Western publications like Reuters and the BBC. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jan 28, 2025 17:14 IST

title: Fact Check: Prakash Raj at Mahakumbh? No, this photo is AI-generated
content:
Neither did Prakash Raj visit the Mahakumbh festival, nor was the viral image real. It's AI-generated.
"I don't believe in god and have no time for it," is what actor and filmmaker Prakash Raj said in an interview. And yet, a photo of him taking a dip in the holy waters of the Ganges during the Mahakumbh festival in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj is being widely shared online.Â
An X user claimed while sharing the photo: "Hindu hater Prakash Rai, who doesn't believe in God, has gone to Kumbhamela to pollute it! Now I understand what they mean by pollution!" Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the photo is AI-generated. Prakash Raj did not visit the Mahakumbh.Â
We did not find any credible news report about the "Singham" actor's visit to the festival. At the same time, we noticed that the photo appeared to be AI-generated. His malformed thumb in the image hinted at that.Â
We also ran the image through the AI-detecting tool Hive Moderation . The tool said with a 99.9 per cent confidence that the image was AI-generated.Â
India Today also reached out to Prakash Raj for his comment on the viral claim. He said that the photo was fake and that a case had been filed against the miscreants sharing it.Â
Thus, it's more than clear that Prakash Raj did not take a holy dip at the Mahakumbh festival. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 28, 2025 20:04 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of miners being rescued in Congo FALSELY linked to the ongoing conflict
content:
This video dates back to March 2023 when nine people were rescued after a gold mine collapsed following heavy rains in Congo.
Thousands of people fled Goma, a major city in the Democratic Republic of Congo , after Rwanda-backed rebels claimed to have captured it. Reportedly, 13 soldiers working with peacekeeping forces were killed in clashes with the rebels. Meanwhile, a video showing people being rescued from a mine has gone viral. Allegedly, these miners were trapped after M23 rebels in the Democratic Republic of Congo dropped an explosive inside a gold mine.Â
An X user shared this video and wrote, "BREAKING NEWS; Rescue underway in Gold mine Goma Eastern DRC Congo after M23 of Rwanda supported by Kagame dropped explosives inside." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the video shows a March 2023 incident when nine miners were rescued after a gold mine collapsed in Congo following heavy rains.Â
Many people responding to the viral post pointed out the video was old. We then reverse-searched the video's keyframes, which led us to a March 28, 2023 video report by ABC News. It noted the video shows nine Congolese miners being rescued from a collapsed gold mine.Â
As per a Reuters report from the same date, this incident happened in the Democratic Republic of Congo's South Kivu province following heavy rainfall. In March 2023, many international news outlets reported on this incident . Â
The mineral-rich eastern part of the Democratic Republic of Congo has been an area of conflict for more than 30 years, since the 1994 Rwandan genocide. Located by the Rwandan border, Goma is an important trading and transport hub. It is within the reach of mining towns supplying gold, tin and coltan, a key component in mobile phones and batteries for electric vehicles.Â
The rebel group currently involved in conflict with the army in Congo is the M23 or the March 23 Movement. It is one of the more than 100 armed groups fighting Congo forces in DRC. It is present in North Kivu province in areas bordering Rwanda and Uganda and has more than 8,000 fighters, according to the United Nations. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 28, 2025 20:28 IST

title: I asked AI chatbots to do simple car mileage maths. Is DeepSeek up to the hype?
content:
"Cheap Chinese" has long been a derogatory term used in India to sneer at products made in China. The general perception is that the Chinese may have mastered the art of producing things at much cheaper costs, but their products are equally substandard.
No one, however, will probably dare to say the same about the Chinese AI chatbot DeepSeek. It has caused such a frenzy in the world of artificial intelligence that the demi-gods of Silicon Valley are scratching their heads in disbelief and wondering how they could achieve this at such a low cost.Â
But how good is the "cheap and best" DeepSeek-R1 chatbot at mathematics, reasoning, and step-by-step problem-solving? This is an area that has become the latest battleground for AI chatbots to prove they are the closest to truly human-like intelligence.
We decided to test the five most popular AI chatbots and see how they solve a real-life dilemma that many people face before buying a car. Is it worth paying thousands of rupees extra for a car which (claims to) gives more mileage per litre of petrol? Or is it better to stick to a cheaper model even if it has a slightly lower fuel efficiency?
We posed this question to five AI chatbots: DeepSeek, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, and Perplexity.Â
These are the exact words of the question we asked the chatbots:Â
One car, "A", has a mileage of 18.4 kilometres per litre. The other car, "B", has a mileage of 17.8 kilometres per litre. But car A costs Rs 1.2 lakh more than car B. If the cost of petrol is Rs 96 per litre and both cars drive 15,000 kilometres per year, how many years will it take car A to recover its extra cost?
The question is broadly based on the price and fuel efficiency of Honda City I VTEC and CVT models. However, we deliberately did not mention the car models to ensure the chatbots do not get diverted by any unnecessary context and rely solely on mathematical calculations to answer the question.Â
The correct answer up to four decimal points is 45.4888 years. If you round it off to a single digit after the decimal, the correct answer is 45.5 years. Try doing it yourself if you think you are good at maths.
In our tests, the best answers were given by Copilot (45.49 years), DeepSeek (45.5 years) and Claude (45.5 years). Gemini, however, was slightly disappointing as its answer was off by almost a year, at 44.3 years. Surprisingly, Perplexity, which is emerging as a smart alternative to Google Search, fared quite poorly and answered "73 years".
You may see the detailed calculations of Copilot , DeepSeek , Claude , Gemini , and Perplexity  here by logging into these chatbots.Â
It is important to underline that one simple maths test is not at all adequate to pronounce verdicts on their abilities. Also, right now, there is a buzz and an aura of novelty around DeepSeek. It is yet to undergo rigorous testing by experts to see if it is as good as established players. DeepSeek itself has disclosed that it may fail to maintain coherent reasoning and is prone to losing context midway through a chat.
However, for now, DeepSeek can bask in the glory of being a "Cheap Chinese" miracle. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jan 29, 2025 20:17 IST

title: Fact Check: Video shows international pilot's announcement about Maha Kumbh? Here is the truth
content:
The viral video was made by a digital creator and the announcement was voiced by his American friend, not a pilot.
A video going viral on social media shows an international pilot's in-flight announcement about the Maha Kumbh. Played over aerial footage of the festival, the voice in the clip states that the flight is about to land in Prayagraj and is flying over the spiritual Sangam Ghat.
The announcement goes on to explain how this Maha Kumbh was a once-in-144-year event, encouraging everyone aboard to take a holy dip and seek the blessings of Naga Sadhus as soon as they land.
Sharing the video on Facebook, one person wrote, "Yesterday, when the British pilot Roger Blade made a historic announcement while landing in Prayagraj during an international flight, the chest of 160 crore Indians is swelling with pride. Whatever the flight captain said, he did it in English". Its archive can be seen here .  Â
India Today Fact Check found that the announcement was not made by a pilot, but by a content creator.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post containing the video in question. In this version, however, we noticed the username 'anveshgraphy' written at the bottom of the clip.
Using this, we found an Instagram account  with the same username, belonging to Anvesh Patel. On this account, we found a higher-resolution version of the viral video in a post from January 23. Its caption stated that the video was shot by Anvesh and that the voiceover was "human original and fully copyrighted".     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Anvesh Patel (@anveshgraphy) On Anvesh's account, we found multiple videos — similar to the one going viral — featuring aerial footage along with a voiceover, allegedly of the pilot. One such video  contained aerial shots of Hyderabad, and an announcement similar to the one about Maha Kumkbh. Another clip featured shots of Dubai in a similar manner. India Today Fact Check also contacted Anvesh, who confirmed to us that the video was made by him and that the voiceover was done by his friend from the United States. He added that the friend is not a pilot and just voiced a script written by Anvesh for the video. Thus, it is clear, that the voiceover in the viral video is not of a pilot flying an international aircraft. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 29, 2025 21:13 IST

title: Fact Check: Empty seats in Delhi during PM's speech? Viral clip is MISLEADING
content:
The video showing empty seats was not recorded during PM Modi's speech. An edited audio was inserted in the viral clip.
Ahead of the Assembly elections, did Delhiites snub Prime Minister Narendra Modi's rally? A video of an empty venue going viral purports to show that. In the 40-second-long video of a huge ground with empty seats with Bharatiya Janata Party flags, Modi's speech is audible, and he can be heard saying in Hindi, "Despite being a weekday, you have gathered here in huge numbers to bless us."Â
Sharing the viral clip on X, a user wrote, "Isse zyada log toh humara Twitter Space mein hi aa jaate hain" (We have more people than this in our Twitter Spaces)," and praised Delhi's former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal saying, "Now we know why Modi is scared of doing rallies in Delhi." The post's archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral claim is misleading. The video was not recorded during PM Modi's speech. An edited audio was inserted into it.Â
We found that PM Modi made the comment audible in the viral clip at a rally in Kartar Nagar's Yamuna Khadar. We found its complete video  on his official YouTube channel. It was live-streamed on January 29.
In this video , the viral clip can be heard at 13 minutes and 40 seconds. The video then also shows a crowd present there in huge numbers, contrary to the viral claim. In the livestream, a banner featuring photos of Narendra Modi and BJP President JP Nadda. This banner was not visible in the viral clip. A comparison can be seen below.
The video of the PM's speech was live-streamed by several other news outlets . In these videos as well, many people can be seen sitting in the audience.
EDITED AUDIO INSERTED IN THE VIRAL CLIP
We also found that the audio of the PM's speech in the viral clip was also edited. The sentence, "This crowd is showing what Delhi's mood is," said by the PM was omitted in the viral clip. It also makes it clear that the video going viral was not recorded during the PM's speech.
While we could not independently ascertain when the viral clip was recorded, it's more than clear that it wasn't during PM Modi's speech. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jan 31, 2025 19:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Claustrophobic video of packed narrow lane is NOT from Mahakumbh
content:
This video is from January 1, when many visited the Shri Radha Rani Temple in Mathura's Barsana.
Following the deadly pre-dawn stampede at Mahakumbh on January 29, the Uttar Pradesh government enforced stricter measures for better crowd management and safety of devotees reaching Prayagraj. VIP passes were revoked and the Mahakumbh area was declared a "no vehicle zone" till February 4, the day after the conclusion of the third "Amrit Snan" on Basant Panchami.
Amid this, a video allegedly from Prayagraj  showing a huge crowd stuck in a narrow lane went viral on social media. The text inside the video read: "Other side of Mahakumbh". Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is not from Prayagraj. It is from January 1 this year, when many devotees visited the Shri Radha Rani Temple in Mathura's Barsana.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post dated January 2. It stated that the video was from Barsana where many had gathered the day before. This makes it clear the video predates Mahakumbh, which began on January 13 .
Further searches led us to another Instagram post that originally shared the video in question on January 1. The account "radharanibarsanaa" belongs to Shyam Sundar Goswami, a spiritual and motivational speaker who runs the NGO, Shree Ji Barsana Mandal Trust . Barsana is situated in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura district.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Shyam Sundar Goswami Ji (@radharanibarsanaa) We then found a livestream from January 1 on Goswami's Facebook account, which showed devotees flocking to Shri Radha Rani Temple in Barsana on New Year's Day, congesting the paths leading to it. After around 2 minutes, Goswami reached a narrow lane. One end of this lane had a staircase with steel railing, while a board reading "joota ghar" (shoe bank) could be spotted on its other end. These two things can also be seen in the viral video. A comparison between the two clips can be seen below. We also found other videos from the same spot shared on January 1 showing a huge crowd around the temple in Barsana. We then contacted Shyam Sundar Goswami, who confirmed to India Today Fact Check that the video was not from Mahakumbh. It was shot near the staircase leading to Shri Radha Rani Temple in Barsana. It is thus, clear that a video of a packed narrow lane in Barsana was falsely shared as a Mahakumbh visual. - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Feb 4, 2025 16:52 IST

title: Fact Check: 'Pushpa' star Rashmika Mandanna is NOT critical, edited photo is viral
content:
This photo is edited. However, Mandanna's leg was injured in the gym last month, but it was not a life-threatening injury.
A shocking photo of "Pushpa" and "Animal" actress Rashmika Mandanna lying in bed with medical electrodes over her body and bandages on her head has gone viral on social media. Allegedly, Mandanna's health was in critical condition after a sudden illness.
The caption in the viral post reads: "Shocking Health Emergency: Rashmika Mandanna Condition Critical After Sudden Illness." The post also contained an article link which had the same headline.Â
