title: Fact Check: Yamuna Aarti in Delhi DID NOT start after BJP won
content:
The viral claim is misleading. This video shows Yamuna Aarti at the Vasudev Ghat in Delhi's Civil Lines area, where it has been regularly offered since March 2024.
The Bharatiya Janata Party defeated the Aam Aadmi Party in the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections and regained power in the capital after 27 years. A video now going viral claimed that only a few days after BJP's victory, Yamuna Aarti was performed in the capital's ghats for the first time. Â
Sharing the viral clip, a Facebook user wrote, "Today for the first time Yamuna ji's Aarti was seen in Delhi. The hope is that Delhiites will get to see Yamuna ji's Aarti meaning now. Delhi will soon become Indraprastha." The video was also widely shared by many YouTube channels .
India Today Fact Check found that viral claims are misleading. This video shows Yamuna Aarti at the Vasudev Ghat in Delhi's Civil Lines area, where it has been regularly offered since March 2024.
Many who shared the viral video claimed it was from Delhi's Kashmere Gate area. A keyword search using this led us to several news reports about Yamuna Aarti at the Vasudev Ghat located in the Civil Lines area. According to reports, Aarti is offered there every Sunday and Tuesday.
In several videos and news reports , we found visuals of Yamuna Aarti at the Vasudev Ghat. A comparison with the viral clip can be seen below.
According to news reports, the Vasudev Ghat was constructed by the Delhi Development Authority under the initiative of Vinai Kumar Saxena, the Lieutenant Governor of the capital. The Vasudev Ghat was inaugurated on March 12, 2024. News reports also mentioned that the first Yamuna Aarti was performed in 2015 by the then-Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal.
  It is thus clear that the claims regarding Yamuna Aarti being offered for the first time in Delhi after the BJP's victory are misleading. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Feb 13, 2025 20:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of US journo mocking Indian reporter linked to recent PM-Trump meet
content:
Viral video is from a White House briefing held in 2020. The Indian journalist is an American news channel C-SPAN's correspondent.
During his two-day visit to the US, Prime Minister Narendra Modi met American President Donald Trump at the White House on January 13. They discussed India-US bilateral ties and later held a joint press conference, where Trump dismissed a question about anti-India activities in the US, citing difficulty understanding the reporter's accent .
Meanwhile, a video claiming to be from this press conference has gone viral on social media. It shows a woman laughing at a man speaking at the event. Some users claimed the clip showed an American journalist mocking an Indian journalist during the Modi-Trump press conference.
Sharing it on Facebook , one person wrote, "American journalists are laughing at the stupidity of India's brainless spineless journalists during the joint Trump-Modi press conference! The local slang is 'Godi Media journalist'." Its archive can be seen here.
However, an India Today Fact Check investigation found that the video is actually from a White House briefing on COVID-19 held in February 2020. The Indian journalist seen in the clip is Raghubir Goyal, a White House correspondent for India Globe, a program on the American news channel C-SPAN (Cable-Satellite Public Affairs Network).
A reverse image search led to an X post dated February 28, 2020 , where a user noted that a New York Post reporter mocked a veteran Indian journalist during a White House media briefing. This confirms the video predates the Modi-Trump press conference. New York Post reporter @ebonybowden mocks veteran Indian journalist while sitting at #Trump media briefing. Laughing at someone different from your race is bad though, even if Americans believe they have "freedom of speech" @nypost @zlj517 @cgtnamerica pic.twitter.com/OEmwTKgiYg — Wang Xianfeng王险峰 (@WangXianfeng8) February 28, 2020 Following this, we found multiple news reports about this incident. According to them, this media briefing took place at the White House on February 26, 2020. The conference was about the outbreak of COVID-19. Donald Trump was the President of the US at the time as well.
New York Post reporter @ebonybowden mocks veteran Indian journalist while sitting at #Trump media briefing. Laughing at someone different from your race is bad though, even if Americans believe they have "freedom of speech" @nypost @zlj517 @cgtnamerica pic.twitter.com/OEmwTKgiYg — Wang Xianfeng王险峰 (@WangXianfeng8) February 28, 2020
Following this, we found multiple news reports about this incident. According to them, this media briefing took place at the White House on February 26, 2020. The conference was about the outbreak of COVID-19. Donald Trump was the President of the US at the time as well.
A video from this conference showed a New York Post journalist mocking an Indian reporter during the briefing.Â
Further investigation found multiple reports stating that the incident occurred at a White House COVID-19 briefing on February 26, 2020, when Trump was President.Â
We also found a live stream of this media briefing on CNBC Television's YouTube channel. The question, asked in the viral video, can be heard after the mark of 25 minutes 40 seconds . Answering the question about India-US ties and his trip, Trump called PM Modi "a great gentleman, and a great leader" and that "a lot of progress was made" in terms of the relationship between the two nations. The same could be read in the press briefing's archives on the "Trump White House" website .Â
The video showed a New York Post journalist, Ebony Bowden , mocking Raghubir Goyal as he asked Trump about the progress in India-US relations after Trump's visit to India on February 24-25, 2020.
It is thus, clear that a 2020 video was falsely linked to the recent Trump-Modi press conference with misleading claims. - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Feb 15, 2025 21:13 IST

title: Fact Check: These images of destruction are NOT from the Delhi earthquake
content:
Both images are old and have nothing to do with the recent earthquake in Delhi-NCR.
People in Delhi-NCR woke up to strong tremors of 4.0 magnitude on Monday (February 17) morning. The epicentre of the earthquake was in Delhi's Dhaula Kuan. A few hours later, another quake of the same magnitude hit Bihar.Â
Two images of partially collapsed multi-storey buildings are now going viral on social media. Allegedly, they show the after-effects of the Delhi earthquake. These images were shared on Facebook , Instagram , and X .
India Today Fact Check found that both images are old and have nothing to do with the recent earthquake in Delhi-NCR.
With the help of a reverse image search, we found one photo in a Hindustan Times news report , published on November 9, 2015. Reportedly, a four-storey building at an unauthorised colony in Delhi's Safdarjung Enclave collapsed partially after an earthquake in October 2015. Serious damage to the structure led to its occupants vacating it. No casualties were reported.Â
We found the other image in a Facebook post from 2021. The photo was also used in many articles related to earthquakes.Â
A similar photo was also used in an article  in a Turkish magazine called Cornucopia. The article was about the earthquake that struck northwestern Turkey on August 17, 1999, killing at least 17,000 people.Â
While we couldn't confirm that the picture was from Turkey, it's nonetheless clear it's old.Â
It's noteworthy that no casualties or damage were reported after the recent Delhi earthquake. As per some reports , a 20-25-year-old tree was uprooted at Jheel Park in Dhaula Kuan. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Feb 17, 2025 20:15 IST

title: Fact Check: Deepfake at Mahakumbh. 'Beautiful Sadhvi' Harsha Richhariya DID NOT kiss a policeman
content:
The viral video is a deepfake. Harsha Richhariya shared the original video on her official Instagram handle on January 19.
Many people attending the Mahakumbh in Uttar Pradesh's Prayagraj captured the internet's attention. One of them was Harsha Richhariya, an influencer dubbed the "Beautiful Sadhvi" by social media. A video now going viral shows Richhariya stepping out of a car, posing for a photo with a police officer, and then kissing him.Â
India Today Fact Check found that this is an AI-generated video. Harsha Richhariya posted the original video on her official Instagram account on January 19. That video was manipulated with the help of AI to create the viral clip.
Upon closely examining the viral video, we noticed Richhariya's hand suddenly shrinking to an unusually small size. This hinted at the video being created or manipulated using AI.Â
A reverse image search of the video's keyframes led us to an Instagram post from January 15 featuring the same clip. This video, however, was watermarked "PixVerse.ai", suggesting that the video may have been altered using this tool.
PixVerse.ai, an AI tool, primarily offers services such as image and image-to-video generation, editing, and enhancement through advanced AI algorithms. Notably, the website's homepage features a demo that showcases how to create a kissing video from a still image of two people using a specific prompt. This further supports the likelihood that the viral video was a deepfake.
We also found the original video on Richhariya's Instagram account , shared on January 19 with the caption "#mahakumbh2025." This video is largely the same except there was no kiss.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Anchor harsha richhariya (@host_harsha) Thus, it's evident that the viral video is a deepfake.  (Written By Surajuddin Mondal) - Ends Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Feb 18, 2025 14:12 IST

title: Took the dip at Maha Kumbh? Photos of you bathing could be for sale on Telegram
content:
Imagine you are a woman who has travelled on trains and buses bursting at their seams, walked for kilometres on end, and passed through seas of people, to take the holy dip at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. Now imagine that this extremely spiritual (and vulnerable) moment was secretly recorded from many angles by someone and shared on social media as bait for explicit content.Â
This is, sadly, not a hypothetical scenario.Â
India Today Fact Check found photos and videos of women bathing and changing clothes, allegedly at the Maha Kumbh, being shared on social media and Telegram. And some of these are being shared as teasers to sell more such images and videos. THE SCARY TALE OF KUMBHLEAKS
There's a deluge of videos of women bathing and changing clothes on river banks all over social media platforms like Facebook, YouTube, and Instagram. Many of these videos lead people to Telegram, for alleged access to full videos of women bathing.    Â
Some Facebook pages promoting pornographic content are constantly sharing videos of bathing women with captions like "Maha Kumbh Ganga Snan Prayagraj". Some also use hashtags like #mahakumbh2025, #gangasnan, and #prayagrajkumbh in these posts.Â
In one such video, a woman can be seen bathing in a river with her lower back and buttocks exposed. Unaware she is being recorded, she continues to bathe while the person filming her intentionally zooms in on her body. This is just one example of the obscene visuals posted on such accounts. Â
Notably, some of these videos and images we examined, shared with trending keywords related to Maha Kumbh, are actually old and not from Prayagraj. However, they are being shared as visuals of the great festival.Â
Some have even created a data bank of such objectionable videos of women bathing and getting dressed on the river banks.    Â
We found two Telegram channels offering access to private groups containing secretly recorded videos of women bathing and changing clothes. These videos are being shared in groups with names like "Ganga river open bathing group", "Hidden bath videos group", and "Open bath videos group".Â
According to Telemetrio, a Telegram search engine and analytics platform, there was a significant surge in the search term "open bathing" in India between February 12 to February 18.Â
In many of these videos and photos, women can be seen changing clothes or covering themselves with towels. The charge for accessing these channels ranges from Rs 1,999 to Rs 3,000.Â
While we were investigating this story, some of those Telegram channels were deleted.Â
Apart from the bathing videos and images of women, these Telegram channels also offer CCTV footage showing women being examined by doctors or nurses — many of them show their private parts being treated or examined. - Ends Published By: Dev Goswami Published On: Feb 18, 2025 21:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Ranveer and Samay being arrested? No, this video is unrelated to 'India's Got Latent' row
content:
The viral video is from 2023 and shows police detaining two men over a parking dispute in Greater Noida.
A video making the rounds on social media shows the police arresting people, seemingly from a residential area. A huge crowd can be seen present at the spot as police nab two men, while some can be heard arguing in the background.Â
Those sharing the clip claimed that the video showed police arresting Samay Raina and Ranveer Allahbadia from their homes, following the controversial joke on the " India's Got Latent " show. Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found this video has no links to the ongoing controversy. It is from 2023 and shows the police detaining two men over a parking dispute in Uttar Pradesh's Greater Noida.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a Times of India report dated August 15, 2023. According to it, the video in question was from a residential society in Greater Noida, where a clash broke out between two groups over parking issues.Â
Per other news reports , the incident took place on August 13, 2023, at the Flora Heritage housing society in Greater Noida West. Clashes erupted between two groups after a parking dispute. As the fight escalated, police reached the spot, but the residents reportedly  attacked the cops as well. Following this, two people were taken into police custody. Some women also tried to stop the police from arresting the men.Â
The police arrested Daya Shankar and Hriday Shankar, and also filed cases against other unidentified people for obstructing them during the arrest.
At the time, the Gautam Buddha Nagar Police made an X post regarding the incident. pic.twitter.com/iTA7e29Hu6 — POLICE COMMISSIONERATE GAUTAM BUDDH NAGAR (@noidapolice) August 14, 2023
pic.twitter.com/iTA7e29Hu6 — POLICE COMMISSIONERATE GAUTAM BUDDH NAGAR (@noidapolice) August 14, 2023
It's noteworthy that the Supreme Court granted interim protection from arrest to Ranveer Allahbadia in connection with the FIRs registered against him over his objectionable remarks on February 18. The apex court, however, restrained Ranveer from doing any other shows for the time being, asking him to cooperate with the investigation.Â
Thus, it's clear that a 2023 video of police action in Greater Noida was falsely linked to the ongoing "India's Got Latent" row. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Feb 20, 2025 16:24 IST

title: Woman showing impressive sword-wielding skills is NOT Delhi's new CM Rekha Gupta
content:
The woman seen in this video is not Rekha Gupta, but an actress named Payal Jadhav.
Rekha Gupta, the debutante MLA from Shalimar Bagh, was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Delhi on February 20. Born in Haryana's Jind, Gupta's political journey goes back to the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad, the student wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. A video now going viral purports to show Gupta demonstrating her sword-wielding skills.Â
Sharing it on X, one person wrote , "Old video of RSS worker and she is worked at ABVP and after in a long time working in BJP 1st time elected in MLA worker Rekha Guptaji. Now Delhi CM. Many congratulations Shri @gupta_rekha ji." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the woman seen in this video is not Rekha Gupta, but actress Payal Jadhav.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post  shared by Payal Jadhav. The post dated February 19 was a tribute to the Maratha ruler Chhatrapati Shivaji. She credited " Savyasachi Gurukulam ", a training institute in Maharashtra for her martial arts skills.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Payal Jadhav (@i_mpayal)
A post shared by Payal Jadhav (@i_mpayal)
Payal Jadhav is an actress who made her debut in Marathi cinema with the film "Baaplyok" in 2023. She has also worked in " Manvat Murders ", a TV series, and played a small role in the " Three of Us ", a movie.Â
Jadhav graduated from Pune University and has a master's degree in Bharatanatyam from Lalit Kala Kendra. Earlier, on January 5, 2023, she shared a photo of herself in an attire  similar to the one seen in the viral video.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Payal Jadhav (@i_mpayal) It is thus, clear that a video of actress Payal Jadhav was falsely shared as an old video of Delhi CM Rekha Gupta. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Feb 20, 2025 22:10 IST

title: Fact Check: India-Bangladesh players lock horns during Champions Trophy? This video is OLD
content:
This video is not recent. This scuffle broke out in the Under-19 World Cup final in 2020.
Before the victory over Pakistan, the India national cricket squad defeated Bangladesh on February 20 in its first match in the 2025 Champions Trophy. A video  now going viral online purports to show an on-field scuffle between India and Bangladesh players in that match.
The video shows players sporting Bangladesh jerseys rushing to the ground with flags in their hands and engaging in a heated altercation with players in blue jerseys.Â
Those sharing the clip claimed it was shot during the India-Bangladesh match in the 2025 Champions Trophy on February 20.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from the Under-19 World Cup final in 2020.
With the help of keywords, we found several news reports from February 2020 regarding the viral video. A Times of India report published on February 10, 2020, said players from the Indian and Bangladeshi teams almost came to blows after the Under-19 World Cup Final match.
Bangladesh players were reportedly over-aggressive while fielding and even sledged Indian batsmen. After defeating India, Bangladeshi players rushed to the ground and many displayed aggressive body language. The match was played in Potchefstroom, South Africa.
Per the report, an Indian player confronted and pushed a Bangladeshi player who allegedly said uncharitable things. The Hindustan Times  and The Quint also published reports about the incident at that time.
Reportedly, two Indian and three Bangladeshi players were charged by the ICC for their involvement in the on-field fight. Bangladeshi captain Akbar Ali also apologised for the incident.
Hence, it is clear that a five-year-old video was falsely shared as recent. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Feb 24, 2025 20:34 IST

title: Fact Check: Ganesha song played after India-Pak Champions Trophy match? These clips aren't from Dubai
content:
The viral video is a compilation of two old videos from Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai and the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, unrelated to the Champions Trophy.
Following India's smashing victory against Pakistan in the Champions Trophy match on February 23 in Dubai, a video  of a song praising Lord Ganesha being played in a stadium was widely shared. The video consists of two clips — one showing people enjoying a light show in a stadium, while the other featured aerial shots of a crowded stadium.Â
Some of these viral clips featured the song "Deva Shree Ganesha" from the 2012 film "Agneepath". Others featured a song called "Gajanan", produced by T-Series for the occasion of Ganeshotsav.Â
The text inside the video reads, "India jeetne k khushi pe Ganesh Aarti laga di, Pakistan wale k samne lagai apni Ganesh aarti (Ganesh Aarti was played after India won against Pakistan). India won by 6 wickets. India winner." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the two videos are unrelated to the Indo-Pak Champions Trophy match in Dubai. These are old clips from Wankhede Stadium and the Narendra Modi Stadium respectively. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes from the video led us to its extended version shared on Instagram by an account belonging to one Sanchit Desai. The post dated January 19 mentioned that the video of people singing "Deva Shree Ganesha" was from the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai, making it clear that it predates the Champions Trophy match.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Sanchit Desai (@sanchitd43) We then found multiple news reports about this video clip. According to them, the Mumbai Cricket Association hosted a series of events to mark the Wankhede Stadium's golden jubilee on January 19. Cricket legends like Sachin Tendulkar, Sunil Gavaskar, and Rohit Sharma were also present for the event, which featured performances by Indian music composer duo Ajay-Atul and singer Avadhoot Gupte, along with a laser show. The song "Deva Shree Ganesha" was composed by Ajay-Atul. Other videos of the celebration also featured people singing along with the song about Lord Ganesha  at the stadium. We then reverse-searched keyframes from the second portion of the viral clip featuring aerial shots of a packed stadium. This video  was also shared by the same Instagram user, Sanchit Desai, on February 13. However, in the original version, the song "Maa Tujhe Salaam" was playing in the stadium. The caption stated that the video was from Ahmedabad.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Sanchit Desai (@sanchitd43) In the video, "ENG" can be seen written on the scoreboard in the stadium. Using this clue, we found that the video was from the India-England ODI match on February 12 at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad. At one point in this match, England was at 175/8 , which is visible on the scoreboard seen in the viral video. advertisement Thus, it's clear both clips predate the India-Pakistan Champions Trophy match. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Feb 25, 2025 20:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Unexpected guest! Did an Indian woman discover a tiger in her room?
content:
This video shows a man from Russia who keeps wild animals as pets.
Remember the 2009 cult classic comedy "Hangover", where three friends wake up in a trashed hotel room and find a full-grown tiger in their bathroom? Something similar allegedly happened to a woman in India. Â
In a video that's been widely shared online, a woman opens the door of her room and finds a tiger inside. The tiger stares directly at her, who quickly shuts the door in shock.Â
Some who shared the video suspected it to be staged, while others claimed it to be a real-life incident.
India Today Fact Check found that this video shows a man from Russia with his pet tiger.
We conducted a keyword search and found that the video is not from India and does not feature a woman. Instead, it was originally filmed by a man called Yara Goryanskiy, who lives in Saint Petersburg, Russia.Â
A quick look at Goryanskiy's Instagram and YouTube accounts reveals he owns several unusual pets, including various kinds of wild cats, bears, and wolves. Goryanskiy shared the viral video on his Instagram account on January 30. The video has since gained over 93 million views on Instagram alone.
We also came across several other videos on his profile featuring tigers and other wild animals inside his house.Â
Another video featuring Goryanskiy went viral in January 2024, where he was playing with a tiger cub. This was reported by several news outlets .Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral video is not from India.Â
(Written by Diya Jain) - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Feb 26, 2025 19:20 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Afghani fans hold Indian flag in Lahore during match against England?
content:
This image dates back to November 2023 and was taken in Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium during a match against Australia in the ICC World Cup.
The Afghan national cricket team proved itself on the pitch, knocking out England from the ICC Champions Trophy in a nail-biting encounter in Lahore on February 26. In its aftermath, many social media users shared a photo of Afghani fans on stands holding a banner featuring the national flags of India and Afghanistan.
The banner depicts two hands shaking, painted in each country's national flag colours. Allegedly, this is how Afghani fans cheered their team in Lahore during the match with England.Â
One such post read: "Afghanistan's fans with the Indian flag & Afghanistan flag at Lahore during the match today." It's noteworthy that the Indian and Afghanistan cricket boards share a special bond, as the BCCI provides facilities, coaching, playing opportunities, and stadiums to the team.
India Today Fact Check has found that the image is not from Lahore, Pakistan, but from Mumbai and dates back to November 2023. OUR PROBEÂ
Recently, reports surfaced that a man was apprehended in Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium for carrying and displaying an Indian national flag during a match between Australia and England on February 22. This suggests there must be some restrictions on the free display of the Indian flag in Pakistani stadiums.
A reverse search of the image led us to a News18 report  dated June 25, 2024, featuring the same photo. As per this report, this photo was captured during Afghanistan's victory over Bangladesh during the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup hosted by West Indies.
However, we noticed a watermark of the 2023 Men's Cricket World Cup hosted by India on a similar image shared on X on the same day, suggesting the image could be from India. #AFGvsBAN Only India and Afghanistan fans are allowed to like this post ❤️ pic.twitter.com/k5R1OEhKzA — BOBjr (@superking1816) June 25, 2024
#AFGvsBAN Only India and Afghanistan fans are allowed to like this post ❤️ pic.twitter.com/k5R1OEhKzA — BOBjr (@superking1816) June 25, 2024
Next, we found the image shared by journalist Jafar Haand on November 7, 2023, stating that it is from the match between Afghanistan and Australia in Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium. He said: "Today's crowd in the #AFGvAUS match in Mumbai." Today's crowd in the #AFGvAUS match in Mumbai. #Afghanistan #India #CWC2023 #CWC2023INDIA #AUSvAFG pic.twitter.com/rfrlaauUM0 — Jafar Haand (@jafarhaand) November 7, 2023
Today's crowd in the #AFGvAUS match in Mumbai. #Afghanistan #India #CWC2023 #CWC2023INDIA #AUSvAFG pic.twitter.com/rfrlaauUM0 — Jafar Haand (@jafarhaand) November 7, 2023
We also tried to find the exact frame from the original video of the match but found out that the broadcasters had scrapped the replay of the full match from their platform.
Next, we compared the pattern of the seats of the Wankhede stadium from a vlog by a YouTuber who visited it during a 2023 World Cup match and found them identical.
Thus, it is evident that the image in question is not from Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium but from Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Feb 27, 2025 17:26 IST

title: Fact check: Don't be rattled. This snake was not a viewer at the ENG-AFG Champions Trophy match
content:
This video was shot during the Lanka Premier League in 2023, during a match at R Premadasa Stadium in Colombo, Sri Lanka.
After a feline guest , did a snake crash the Champions Trophy 2025 match in Pakistan? After Afghanistan eliminated England from the semi-final race on February 26 in Lahore's Gaddafi Stadium, a video of a snake wriggling through electric wires at the boundary of a stadium went viral on social media. Allegedly, this was during the Afghanistan-England match.Â
Many in the comments criticised and laughed at Pakistan's Champions Trophy arrangements because of this alleged incident.
India Today Fact Check found that this is a 2023 video from a match in Sri Lanka.
The scorecard at the bottom of the screen in the viral video noted ENG vs AFG, 31-2 in 7.2 overs.Â
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a YouTube video  shared by the official YouTube channel of Sri Lanka Cricket on August 12, 2023. In this extended version, the snake can be seen roaming around the stadium boundary as the match continues. The video description stated that it is from the Lanka Premier League 2023. Â
Unlike the viral clip, the scorecard at the bottom of the YouTube video read Jaffna vs Kandy, 140-5 in 17.1 overs. Also, the players are in blue and red jerseys in this match, while the jerseys of both England and Afghanistan in the Champions Trophy are blue. This means that this clip was edited to change the scoreboard and players in the stadium.
We then found multiple news reports about this incident from Sri Lanka. According to them, a snake appeared at the boundary of the stadium during a match on August 12, 2023, during the Lanka Premier League. The snake reportedly appeared twice during the game between Jaffna Kings and B-Love Kandy.Â
At one point, the snake was spotted crawling near Kandy pacer Isuru Udana in the stadium itself. The other time, a snake was seen crawling on the boundary line near electric wires , scaring the cameramen there. The incident reportedly took place in the R Premadasa Stadium in Colombo, Sri Lanka.Â
Per reports , it wasn't the first time that a snake appeared in an LPL match. Earlier, on July 31, 2023, a snake was spotted in the stadium during another LPL match, bringing the game to a halt .
According to the highlights of the ENG vs AFG Champions Trophy match, during the 7th over of the match, Afghan cricketer Rahmat Shah was batting with Ibrahim Zadran while England's Mark Wood was balling. The scorecard superimposed in the viral clip has been taken from the second bowl of that over .
It is, thus, clear that an old video from a match played in Sri Lanka was edited to share as from Pakistan's Champions Trophy match. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Feb 28, 2025 17:43 IST

title: Fact Check: Music video BTS goes viral as Ukrainian soldiers fake combat for US funds
content:
This video does not show Ukrainian soldiers creating fake combat scenes. It's a behind-the-scenes shot from a music video.
While US President Donald Trump shocked the world when he got into a verbal spat in the Oval Office with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy — just days after the Russian invasion of Ukraine completed three years — the US President's position on American aid to Ukraine has been no secret. He has often claimed that the US has spent more than $300 billion on Ukraine under Joe Biden's command.Â
A video now making the rounds purports to show a Ukrainian female soldier applying makeup in a war zone-like. Sharing the video , people claimed that this was a crisis actor and that Ukraine was manufacturing fake combat scenes to get money from the US. A Facebook user wrote , "Ukraine soldiers have resorted to faking combat to appear war-torn, so the slush fund from the US keeps churning money their way. What do you think about this?
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is a behind-the-scenes shot from a music video by Ukrainian artists Misha Scorpion and Vitsik.
In the viral post , several people pointed out that the video is not from the war zone but from a music video . In the comments, we also found a link to the music video for a song titled "Brothers" by Ukrainian music artists Misha Scorpion and Vitsik, uploaded to YouTube on February 25 this year. The video depicts the struggles of Ukrainian soldiers in the war zone.Â
Like the viral clip, this music video also featured a female soldier. We compared the viral video to the music video and found that the woman was the same — many other identical details could be seen in both videos.Â
When we checked the musician Vitsik's Instagram account , we found that on February 25, through an Instagram story, the singer pointed out that the claim made in the viral video was not true. The singer said the viral clip was from the music video.Â
It's noteworthy that in 2022, several similar claims , accusing Ukraine of manufacturing fake war videos , went viral just after Russia's invasion of Ukraine began. At the time, India Today Fact Check debunked these claims.
Thus, it's clear that in the viral video, Ukrainian soldiers are not creating fake combat scenes to ask for money from the United States. - Ends Published By: Soumya Published On: Mar 3, 2025 19:53 IST

title: Fact Check: Majestic fireworks video from Kuwait FALSELY shared as of India's victory over Australia
content:
This video shows fireworks celebrations during the opening ceremony of a Football Championship in Kuwait.
India registered a nail-biting win over Australia in the Champions Trophy's first semifinal held in Dubai, securing a four-wicket win to reach the final.
Now, a video, making the rounds on the internet, shows spectacular fireworks celebrations in Dubai International Cricket Stadium after India's win against Australia. Sharing this video, a Facebook user wrote, "India's explosive victory sparks sky above Dubai into the parade of color. The Dubai International Cricket Stadium erupted in celebration as fireworks lit up the night sky following India's 4-wicket victory over Australia in the ICC Champions Trophy 2025 semifinal." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video shows fireworks celebrations during the opening ceremony of a Football Championship in Kuwait. OUR PROBE
In the viral post, several people claim that the fireworks video does not show Dubai International Cricket Stadium but Jaber Al-Ahmad International Stadium, a Football stadium , in Kuwait. A reverse search of screengrabs from the viral video led us to a December 22, 2024, Instagram post containing the viral video with the hashtag Kuwait. This means the viral video predates the India vs Australia Semi-Final match. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bcarekw (@bcarekw)
A post shared by Bcarekw (@bcarekw)
We found a video similar to the viral one in which the same stadium and fireworks celebrations pattern can be seen. In this December 22, 2024 post, it is written that the video shows Jaber Al-Ahmed Stadium in Kuwait during the opening celebrations of the Gulf Cup. View this post on Instagram A post shared by SK Robiul (@robiul_8136) When we compared the stadium in the viral video with Kuwait's Jaber Al-Ahmad International Stadium, we found that both stadiums are the same proving that the viral video is not from Dubai but from Kuwait. We found several media reports from December 2024 in which it was written that the fireworks can be seen during the opening ceremony of the Arabian Gulf Cup Football Championship in Jaber Al-Ahmad International Stadium during the 26th edition of the Arabian Gulf Cup football championship on December 21, 2024, at the Jaber Al Ahmad International Stadium in Kuwait City. According to the Qatar Tribune report , the ceremony merged traditional Gulf folk arts with modern technology. It further said that at the end of the ceremony, a spectacular fireworks celebration was held, which mesmerized the audience. Also, we did not find any credible media report that mentioned that there were any fireworks at the Dubai International Stadium after India's win. Thus, the video of fireworks celebrations during the opening ceremony of a Football Championship in Kuwait was falsely shared as from the India vs Australia Semi-Final match. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Mar 6, 2025 12:37 IST

title: Fact Check: This Hashim Amla fasting story being used to criticise Shami is NOT TRUE
content:
Hashim Amla himself has said that he was not fasting when he scored 311 runs against England.
Indian pacer Mohammed Shami has faced criticism from a Muslim cleric for not observing a fast during the holy month of Ramadan. On March 5, India played the semi-final of 2025 Champions Trophy against Australia. While India beat the Aussies to reach the final, a picture of Shami drinking an energy drink went viral on social media. While some praised Shami for prioritising cricket, several others, including a cleric from Bareilly, criticised him for not observing a fast.
Amid this, many social media users are using another Muslim cricketer to criticise Shami. This cricketer is South African legend Hashim Amla. Many are claiming that when Amla scored his maiden triple hundred against England, he was fasting during Ramadan. Users are comparing Amla and Shami and criticising the latter.
A user wrote , "Hashim Amla scored a triple century while fasting, but Mohammad Shami needed water after the first over List soms are calling him a 'national hero'. The double standards are real".
India Today Fact Check found that Amla himself had said that he was not fasting when he scored 311 runs against England.
The test match in which Amla scored the triple hundred against England was played from July 19, 2012 at The Oval. In the same year, the month of Ramadan started from July 19. On the second day of the match, Amla scored 311 runs without getting out.
Taking hints from the above mentioned details, we ran a keyword search and found an article by The Guardian , published on July 22, 2012. According to this news report, "The only surprise is that this devout Muslim is eating at all, for it is Ramadan and in the past not even Test cricket has been allowed to interrupt the vigilance of his religious observance. Here, though, he has put fasting on hold".
The report has also quoted Amla saying that he was not fasting while playing. Amla said, "Because I'm travelling away from home I don't have to fast. So I haven't been fasting. But I will make it up when I get home."
Tristan Holme, a journalist, also wrote about Amla's 311* innings at The Oval. In an article published on Cricbuzz , Holme wrote, "And as it was Ramadan, Amla did not drink any water out on the field - although he was not fasting on match days, he kept his consumption to the confines of the dressing room out of respect for his fellow Muslims who were."
A report by SA Cricketmag has also mentioned that Amla was not fasting when he scored the triple century against England in the 2012 test match.
It is thus clear that users are falsely claiming that Amla was fasting during his 300* innings, just to criticise Indian cricketer Mohammed Shami. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Mar 6, 2025 18:48 IST

title: Fact Check: Was Mohammed Shami forced to break his fast?
content:
Viral video is edited. In the actual video, shared back in April 2024, Mohammed Shami wished everyone a Happy Eid.
Did Indian pacer Mohammed Shami release a video apologising to Muslims amid the controversy over fasting , claiming he was forced to break roza during a Champions Trophy match? A viral video circulating on social media , featuring Shami in a skull cap and kurta, allegedly suggests just that.
In the video, Shami appears to say, "Yes, I broke roza that day. Muslim brothers and sisters, please do not misunderstand me. I did not do it on purpose. I was forced to break roza, otherwise, they would have destroyed my career. I apologise to my Muslim brothers and sisters again."
Recently, Shami faced heavy criticism for not observing a fast during India's Champions Trophy semifinal match against Australia.
A controversy erupted as Shami was seen consuming an energy drink during the match held in Dubai on March 5.
Muslim cleric Maulana Shahabuddin Razvi Bareilvi even labelled Shami a "criminal and sinner" for not fasting during roza.
Sharing the viral video, one user on Instagram wrote : "Mohammed Shami explained the reasons for breaking his fast. He regrets and apologises for doing so."
India Today Fact Check found that this video was edited. The original video, shared back in April 2024, showed Mohammed Shami wishing everyone a Happy Eid.
With the help of keyword search, we found Shami's Instagram post dated April 11, 2024 . In this carousel of photos, he is seen wearing the same attire as in the viral video. View this post on Instagram A post shared by (@mdshami.11)
A post shared by (@mdshami.11)
We then looked at Shami's social media posts from the same day, leading us to another Instagram video, which contained the original version of the viral clip . In it, Shami can be seen wishing everyone a Happy Eid on behalf of his friends and family. View this post on Instagram A post shared by (@mdshami.11)
A post shared by (@mdshami.11)
Meanwhile, Shami's cousin Mumtaz, along with several others, defended him against criticism for not observing roza during the ongoing Champions Trophy. However, we found no statement issued by Shami himself regarding the controversy.
With the Champions Trophy 2025 final set to take place on March 9, where India and New Zealand will face off at the Dubai International Stadium, it is important to separate fact from misinformation.
It is, hereby, clear that the viral video was edited and the original one, from April 2024, only featured Shami extending Eid wishes. - Ends Published By: Sayan Ganguly Published On: Mar 8, 2025 21:05 IST

title: Investigation: How social media vultures feed on misery of sick children
content:
(Content warning: This story includes distressing visuals)
When five-year-old Raghad developed swelling around her eyes, her mother assumed it was an ordinary infection. After all, in the war-torn Gaza Strip where they lived, this was an obvious possibility. Their world, however, came crashing down when doctors diagnosed it as a cancerous tumour. How would Raghad get treatment amid Israel's near-constant shelling?
"We managed to take her to Jordan for treatment last year, but she barely survived a few months in a hospital there," her mother, Hoda Al Khawli, told us. "She was such a bubbly, sweet girl. But her last days with chemotherapy were agonising."
"We still find it difficult to look at pictures of her in the hospital bed. She was in acute pain. We could see her fading away."
Thousands of miles away in Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur, a man called Atul Singh scours the internet for photos like Raghad's.
His social media portrait is that of a football-loving engineering student with a vibrant social life . But his blue sunglasses belie a dark truth: he's a vulture who preys on the misery of terminally ill children. The more distressing the child's condition in the photo, the better.
This is Atul's sickening side hustle. He emotionally exploits people using heart-rending photos of children in critical condition. Posing as a saviour, he collects donations for these children's treatment. And then he pockets the money.
He and others in this "business" don't care if the child is from Gaza , Russia , or Pakistan . They are not bothered by the fact that they are harvesting donations using pictures of children like Raghad, who may be long dead. No one is spared. Everyone is bait.
Hoda Al Khawli never received any financial assistance from India for her daughter. And she was horrified to learn her daughter's photos were being used for fraudulent fundraising two months after her death. She sent us a photo of Raghad's grave. It bore the date of her passing: January 13, 2025.
India Today Fact Check's investigation uncovered Atul's direct connection to the Instagram account "@shree_ram_faimly", which has 1.4 million followers, that regularly solicits donations using photos and videos of sick children, even dead ones. We traced QR codes from the account's fundraising posts to a GooglePay UPI ID featuring the photo of the same young man who is all over Atul Singh's personal Instagram account . Multiple pieces of evidence link Atul to the "@shree_ram_faimly" Instagram account. The chart below explains how they are connected.
When we confronted Atul, he said that the children, whose photos were used to ask for donations, were from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. He said he had documentary evidence to prove the money went to the rightful people. However, when we questioned him about the whereabouts of these children, he disconnected and stopped answering the phone. And soon after we contacted him, he began deleting his posts related to donations.
Atul and others like him prefer photos and videos of children who are either badly injured, battling severe illness, or crying in pain. They layover videos of sick children from foreign countries with Hindi audio , creating the illusion that they are Indian. Often, the audio features a woman desperately pleading for financial help, claiming that her child is in critical condition.
Using videos of children from foreign countries, especially conflict zones, offers an advantage: their parents are unlikely to find out, eliminating the risk of getting caught. Several of the photos being used by these people are of children from Gaza, taken by journalists who have risked their lives (and even died ) to document the horrors of the war. They could never have imagined that their work would be exploited like this.
For example, the Instagram account "@hyc_help_foundation" shared a video of an injured child on a hospital stretcher, soliciting donations without disclosing the child's identity or location.
We found that journalist Mohammed Qandeel Abu Omar originally shared this clip in May 2024 , claiming the child was severely injured during the bombing of Gaza's Al Shaboura region. He told India Today Fact Check, "This child died the same day he was brought to the hospital. His family members also lost their lives in the bombing."
Yet, in October last year, five months after the child's death, "@hyc_help_foundation" was still asking for donations in his name.
It's hard to say how many people fall for such frauds, but comments on these posts indicate that at least a few do. We spoke to the families of three children from Gaza whose videos were used in such scams. None of them have received a single rupee from Indian donors.
Some scammers also impersonate social work organisations, like Hyderabad Youth Courage which operates in Hyderabad. Fraudsters behind the Instagram account "@hyc_help_foundation" cloned the NGO's content and replaced the donation QR codes with their own . advertisement No shame, no guilt While families in Gaza struggle to secure treatment for their sick and injured children, some scammers appear to be making big bucks. Case in point, a Saharanpur-based influencer called Abdul Raheem. He loves luxury cars , wears stylish clothes , holidays at hill stations , and also poses alongside politicians. He, too, is part of a network making money off fake donation campaigns for sick children. There is a direct link between his personal Instagram account "@official_raheem_0" and "@harry_lifestyle_1", an Instagram account filled with donation appeals. Many of these fraud accounts follow each other and share the same videos with different QR codes. Our investigation found many such suspicious accounts . So next time you feel like scanning a QR code to help someone, look closely. There could be a scammer hiding behind it. (With inputs from Rahul Kumar, Saharanpur) - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Mar 10, 2025 19:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of vandalism falsely linked to boycott of Salman Khan's film
content:
This video is from Ajmer, Rajasthan, where lawyers resorted to vandalism while protesting against the murder of a fellow lawyer.
Ahead of the release of Salman Khan's film "Sikandar", a video of a person vandalising the actor's clothing brand store, Being Human, made the rounds online. Many claimed that Salman Khan's store was vandalised by people boycotting his upcoming movie. An X user wrote, "Boycott gang attack on Being Human store. All of them are boycotting the movie, Sikandar."
India Today Fact Check found that the video shows a protest against the murder of a lawyer in Rajasthan. It has nothing to do with Salman Khan's upcoming movie.
A reverse search of screengrabs from the video led us to a report by NavBharat Live from March 8. This report featured a longer version of the viral video and said the incident was from Ajmer, Rajasthan, where many resorted to violence and vandalism in major markets such as City Square and Mirage Mall amid police presence.
We found several news reports from March 8 containing the viral video's screengrabs. As per the Free Press Journal , on March 2, senior advocate Purushottam Jakhetia was fatally attacked by a group of people who were dancing and playing loud music in their car near a liquor shop on Budha Pushkar Road.
Jakhetia, who lived nearby, objected and asked them to turn off the music. The altercation led the miscreants to attack him. He succumbed to his injuries on March 7 while undergoing treatment. Angry over Jakhetia's death, lawyers called for a city-wide bandh , except for medical stores, schools, and petrol pumps. However, the protest turned violent when the angry lawyers started vandalising shops at major markets in Ajmer. The viral video shows this.
We searched for boycott campaigns against Salman Khan's movie "Sikandar". However, we did not find any report that confirmed the viral claim.
Thus, it's clear that the video has nothing to do with Salman Khan or his upcoming film. - Ends Published By: Sayan Ganguly Published On: Mar 10, 2025 21:05 IST

title: Fact Check: Afghans in viral video are NOT celebrating India's Champions Trophy win
content:
This video from Afghanistan has nothing to do with India winning the Champions Trophy. It was shot after Afghanistan defeated England in the group stage of the same tournament.
Indian cricket fans poured onto the streets on March 9 to celebrate India's Champions Trophy 2025 final win. But Indian cricket fans weren't the only ones celebrating. Many online alleged that people in Afghanistan, too, celebrated India's win against New Zealand, sharing a compilation of clips showing people dancing on the streets and setting off firecrackers.
A Facebook user captioned this compilation , "Burnol moment for Pakistan lovers! Massive celebrations in Afghanistan after India's CT victory! Afghanistan stood with India Respect Forever!" Its archive can be seen here .
India Today found that while the video is from Afghanistan, it has nothing to do with India winning the Champions Trophy. The video shows celebrations after Afghanistan defeated England in the group stage of the same tournament.
The video featured the Instagram watermark of the account "zekria.zeer". We found that this account shared the video on February 27, making it clear it precedes the Champions Trophy final. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Zekria Zeer (@zekria.zeer)
A post shared by Zekria Zeer (@zekria.zeer)
The caption of the Instagram video implied that these celebrations happened in Afghanistan after the nation defeated England in the Champions Trophy. As per his Instagram bio , "zekria.zeer" is a Jalalabad-based Afghani photographer.
India Today Fact Check spoke to Zekria regarding the viral video, who said that he shot the video when people in Jalalabad celebrated Afghanistan's win over England in the Champions Trophy. The match took place on February 26 in Lahore. Afghanistan registered a historic win , defeating England by eight runs.
While we can't independently comment on whether Afghani people celebrated India's Champions Trophy final win, it's more than clear the viral video is unrelated to it. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Mar 12, 2025 12:27 IST

title: Fact Check: 2022 video of Baloch militant attack VIRAL as recent Pakistan train hijack
content:
The viral video shows a 2022 train attack in Balochistan — not the recent train hijacking by BLA militants.
The Balochistan Liberation Army, a separatist group, hijacked the Peshawar-bound Jaffar Express on March 11 in Pakistan. At the time of writing this, 27 militants were reportedly killed in a rescue operation that freed 155 passengers.
A video of an explosion on a moving train is now making the rounds online. Those sharing claimed it showed the BLA attack on the Jaffar Express. An X user wrote , "Balochistan Pakistan: A militant group, BLA Separatist, has hijacked a train with 400 passengers. Baloch women and children were released and held hostage. Six army men were killed. A train carrying military men is underway to fight the militants." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from 2022 and therefore unrelated to the train hijack.
A reverse search of screengrabs from the video led us to a post from April 15, 2022, containing the viral video. The post reads: "BLA has released footage of an IED attack on a train carrying FC (Frontier Corps) near Sibbi, Balochistan." Many responded to this post saying that the video could be from January 2022. This means that this video predates the recent train hijacking by BLA militants. BLA has released footage of an IED attack on Train carrying FC(Frontier Corps) near Sibbi, Balochistan. pic.twitter.com/ztOuBBznJz Rohan Panchigar (@rohanpanchigar) April 15, 2022
BLA has released footage of an IED attack on Train carrying FC(Frontier Corps) near Sibbi, Balochistan. pic.twitter.com/ztOuBBznJz Rohan Panchigar (@rohanpanchigar) April 15, 2022
We then found a January 2022 report containing the viral video. As per the report, the video shows a January 18, 2022, improvised explosive device or IED attack on a train in the northeast Balochistan town of Sibi. The train was allegedly carrying Pakistani troops. Several were killed and the injured were hospitalised. Then-Balochistan Chief Minister, Mir Abdul Qaddos Bizenjo, condemned the attack, claiming it was a passenger train also carrying civilians.
Another January 2022 report suggested the explosion caused multiple bogies of the Jaffar Express to get derailed and kill several Pakistani army personnel.
Thus, it's clear that a 2022 video of a BLA attack on a train in Balochistan was falsely shared as the recent Jaffar Express hijacking. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Mar 12, 2025 14:51 IST

title: Fact Check: Illegal mosque being demolished in India? No, this video is from Indonesia
content:
The viral is from an amusement park in Indonesia and does not show a mosque in India being razed.
A video allegedly showing the demolition of a mosque in India has been widely shared online. Sharing this video, an X user wrote , "Bulldozers in India demolish illegal mosques". Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from an amusement park in Indonesia. Our Probe
Several people responded to the viral post and pointed out that the video was not from India but from Indonesia. Upon reverse-searching its keyframes, we found several similar videos on Indonesian YouTube channels from March 2025. Many of these videos show a similar white and green structure being demolished. As per these YouTube videos, this video was from Hibisc Fantasy.
Hibisc Fantasy is an amusement and theme park in Bogor, Indonesia. We compared the viral video with the videos from the amusement park in Indonesia and found many similarities between the demolished structures and the logo marked on the bulldozer. This proves that the viral video is from Indonesia.
Subsequent keyword searches led us to several March 2025 Indonesian news reports. According to Kompas , an Indonesian newspaper, West Java's governor, Dedi Mulyadi instructed the demolition orders of the amusement park on March 6. Mulyadi told Kompas there were land permit violations. The park was allowed to be built on only 4,800 square metres of land but had spread to 15,000 square metres.
The illegal construction and violations reportedly caused rainwater stagnation and flash flooding in the Puncak area of Bogor, Indonesia.
Thus, it's clear that a video from Indonesia was falsely shared as an illegal mosque in India being demolished. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Mar 13, 2025 14:00 IST

title: Fact Check: 2012 US airstrike video FALSELY shared as Pak crackdown on train hijackers
content:
This video has been online since 2012. It has nothing to do with Pakistani forces eliminating the BLA hijackers.
On March 11, the Peshawar-bound Jaffar Express, carrying more than 400 passengers, was hijacked by Baloch Liberation Army separatists. After a tense standoff, Pakistani forces reportedly eliminated all hijackers and secured hostages.
Now, footage allegedly showing an aerial view of Pakistani forces eliminating the BLA train hijackers has been widely shared online. Sharing this video, an X user wrote, "Pakistani troops successfully rescue Jaffar Express train. Conducting Operation against Baloch Liberation Army." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video has been online since 2012. It has nothing to do with Pakistani forces eliminating BLA train hijackers.
A reverse search of screengrabs from the viral video led us to a 15-minute-long version of the viral clip, uploaded to YouTube on July 19, 2012. The video was titled, "2 Apache Helicopters Engage over 20 Taliban fighters." The viral portion can be seen at the 56-second mark. This means the video does not show Pakistani forces killing BLA train hijackers.
Subsequent keyword searches led us to the same video clip posted on July 18, 2012, on Military.com. This website publishes news and information on the United States military and its foreign policy. As per the video's description, it showed "Apache helicopters eliminate a platoon of Taliban setting up to ambush a US special forces patrol. Footage taken during operations in 2009 in Afghanistan."
This video can be seen on Wikimedia Commons . According to the website, the video shows "US Apache helicopters engaging a group of 20 Taliban fighters setting up to ambush a US special forces patrol in the nearby valley in Afghanistan."
Currently, Pakistan does not operate Boeing AH-64 Apache helicopters. At the time of writing this article, the Pakistan army or local authorities had not officially released any footage of its forces engaging with the hijackers.
Thus, it's more than clear that the video has nothing to do with the recent train hijacking by BLA rebels. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Mar 13, 2025 19:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of colourful firecrackers in China DOES NOT show Holi celebrations
content:
The viral video predates Holi and shows Chinese New Year celebrations held between January 29 and February 12 this year.
A video allegedly showing Holi celebrations in China is making the rounds on social media. The video shows a long line of firecrackers going off on a street, erupting colours in the air. Several people could be seen looking on from the balconies of their homes as people celebrated on the streets.
While many shared it as Indians celebrating Holi in China, some social media users also called it Holi celebrations from Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video predates Holi and shows the Chinese New Year celebrations. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video shared on an Instagram account named "Its China baby" . The Instagram post from February 16 stated that the video showed the sixteenth day of the first month of the Chinese New Year. It is hereby clear that the video predates Holi, which falls on March 14 this year. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Wander Joy (@itschina.baby)
A post shared by Wander Joy (@itschina.baby)
We then found multiple videos similar to the one going viral on social media , stating that the fireworks were part of the Chaozhou Spring Festival celebrations . Chaozhou is a city in eastern Guangdong province, China.
One such YouTube video, from February 14 showed the same fireworks seen in the viral clip from a different angle. In this clip, we observed some of the buildings had boards featuring Mandarin text.
Per news reports, Chinese New Year, also known as the Spring Festival , spans 15 days and is marked by traditions such as colourful parades and cultural activities every year. In 2025, the celebrations began on January 29 and concluded with the Lantern Festival on February 12. During this, a fireworks display was held in Guangdong and Jiangxi Province , among other places in China.
It is thus clear that the viral video predates Holi and shows Chinese New Year celebrations held between January 29 and February 12 this year. - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Mar 13, 2025 20:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Man chopping wife's hair in Dhaka FALSELY viral as communal incident in Bengal
content:
This video shows a husband cutting his wife's hair in Bangladesh in September 2024.
A video doing the rounds on social media shows a woman crying as a man chops her hair off angrily. Some people can be seen approaching the man as the incident takes place.
Some shared the clip , claiming that this video was from West Bengal, where a Muslim man publicly chopped off the hair of a Hindu woman against her will. Some also claimed that he was punishing the woman for not paying his fare.
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this 2024 video shows an angry husband cutting his wife's hair after a fight in Bangladesh's capital Dhaka. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video shared as a YouTube Short in February. The video was shared in collaboration with a YouTube channel called "City Voice 1986". This channel originally shared the video in question on September 15 last year.
We then found a Facebook account with the same name as the YouTube channel that posted a longer version of the viral video along with two other videos linked to the incident. The account belongs to Mohammad Air Khan, a resident of the Gulshan neighbourhood in Dhaka.
The captions of these posts stated that the man in the video was beating his wife on the street. In one of the videos , the man says in Bengali that it is his family matter when confronted. Later, he could be seen getting beaten up by a group of people for mistreating his wife.
We contacted Sanjay Adhikari, a journalist from Bangladesh, who identified the location of the video as the Airport Railway Station in Dhaka. On Google Maps, we found photos and videos of the Airport Railway Station. Near the station, we saw a public toilet, a building and a minaret - all of which are visible in the viral video. A comparison can be seen below.
It is, thus, clear that the viral video does not show a communal incident in West Bengal. - Ends Published By: Prateek Chakraborty Published On: Mar 13, 2025 20:28 IST

title: Fact Check: RSS leader attended Iftar party — but before Nagpur violence broke out
content:
This video of RSS leader Indresh Kumar attending an Iftar party in Delhi is from March 15 — two days before the Nagpur violence.
Communal violence rocked Maharashtra's Nagpur on March 17. Large-scale arson, vandalism, and stone pelting left at least 34 police personnel injured . The unrest was triggered by rumours that the holy book of a community was desecrated during a right-wing protest, demanding the removal of Mughal emperor Aurangzeb's tomb from the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district. On March 19, police arrested Fahim Shamim Khan, a local leader of the Minorities Democratic Party, for allegedly masterminding the violence.
Amid this, a video allegedly showed Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh leader Indresh Kumar attending an Iftar party on the night of the Nagpur violence.
Sharing the clip on Facebook , one person wrote in Hindi, "The night when Hindu houses and vehicles were identified and burnt in Nagpur, RSS leader Indresh Kumar was having dates with Muslims."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the viral video is from an Iftar party held in Delhi on March 15 — two days before communal violence broke out in Nagpur. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes of the viral video led us to a video report dated March 16 on the YouTube channel of News18 India. According to it, the video showed RSS leader Indresh Kumar at an Iftar party at the Community Centre in Delhi.
At the party, Kumar was accompanied by Dr Umer Ahmed Ilyasi, chief Imam of the All India Imam Organisation. In the video, Ilyasi consumed dates from Kumar's hands to break his fast.
We then found multiple video reports and articles about the Iftar party. Additionally, we found another video of Indresh Kumar eating, dressed in the same attire as seen in the viral video. This video was shared by Shahzad Ali Idrisi , a Bharatiya Janata Party leader, on March 15. RSS MRM Indresh Kumar Shahzad Ali pic.twitter.com/IBwaQQKcro — Shahzad Ali Idrisi (@SHAHZADALISHAI8) March 15, 2025
RSS MRM Indresh Kumar Shahzad Ali pic.twitter.com/IBwaQQKcro — Shahzad Ali Idrisi (@SHAHZADALISHAI8) March 15, 2025
On March 16, Indresh Kumar shared some photos from the party on his official Facebook account. One of these photos showed the invitation to the Iftar party. According to it, the party was on March 15 at 6 pm.
Kaushal Pandey, India Today's correspondent from Nagpur, told us that Vishva Hindu Parishad and Bajrang Dal staged a protest in Nagpur over the removal of Aurangzeb's tomb on the afternoon of March 17. By the evening, violence had broken out in the Mahal area of the city, leading to the vandalisation of vehicles and stone pelting.
However, before March 17, the situation in the city remained normal. Union Minister Nitin Gadkari even attended an event in Nagpur on March 16 .
Thus, it's clear that the video of RSS leader Indresh Kumar attending an Iftar party predates the Nagpur violence. - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Mar 19, 2025 20:46 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show open cheating at IAS exam centres
content:
This video shows cheating during a law examination in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh. The exam was later voided.
A shocking video making the rounds online purports to show the scale of cheating for Union Public Service Commission exams in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Jharkhand. The video, shot on a phone, takes viewers from classroom to classroom where civil service aspirants can allegedly be seen copying answers directly from booklets.
Most of these videos were shared online with captions like , "IAS Exam centres of UP, Bihar, Jharkhand !!!". One person wrote : "As an educationist, it's heartbreaking to see the state of IAS exam centres in UP, Bihar, and Jharkhand. This is where the future of Indian governance is shaped—yet, look at the conditions! If this is how we treat our brightest minds, can we really expect development? Time for a serious change! ed to change... Qualified person should go to position... Shame on you government."
India Today Fact Check found that this video from February 27, 2024, shows rampant cheating during a law exam in UP's Barabanki. The exam was later voided.
A reverse search of the video's keyframes led us to news reports from early 2024. According to reports in Zee News and India Today , this video was from a law college in Uttar Pradesh's Barabanki.
On February 27, 2024, students were caught collectively cheating during an examination. They were openly copying answers from student guides and notes during an LLB paper. While this was going on, a student captured the whole thing on video and demanded action against the college authorities for allowing this.
According to ETV Bharat , TRC Law College student Shivam Singh's exam centre was this college in Barabanki and that the college's principal demanded a bribe from Shivam to let him cheat during the exam.
When he refused, the college reportedly refused to issue him an examination pass. On February 27, 2024, Shivam went to the college campus and recorded the open cheating on a Facebook Live.
According to reports , when the video surfaced, this exam was cancelled and the examination centre was fined Rs 2 lakh. The college was also blacklisted as an examination centre for six years. A committee was also set up to look into the matter.
Thus, it's clear that this video has nothing to do with civil service exams in UP, Bihar, or Jharkhand. - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Mar 21, 2025 18:38 IST

title: Fact Check: CSK fan holds anti-Aurangzeb poster at IPL? No, this photo is edited
content:
This picture has been digitally altered. In the original poster, he was admiring cricketer Mahendra Singh Dhoni.
Amid the ongoing controversy over Aurangzeb's grave in Maharashtra, a photo of a man at an Indian Premier League (IPL) match holding a poster featuring offensive language directed at the Mughal emperor is making rounds on social media.
The photo shows a Chennai Super Kings fan in a yellow jersey holding an anti-Aurangzeb poster. Sharing it, an Instagram user wrote, "Another reason to love CSK." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this image was digitally altered. The original photo shows film director Rathna Kumar, a CSK fan, holding a poster with admiring words for cricketer Mahendra Singh Dhoni.
We observed that in the viral photo, there was a Grok watermark in the bottom right corner. Grok is a free artificial intelligence chatbot designed by xAI. Additionally, the hands of the man holding the poster do not appear natural. One of his hands is behind the poster, indicating that the photo may have been edited.
Upon reverse-searching the viral photo, we found the original image uploaded to an X account named Rathna Kumar. It was posted on March 23, the same day the IPL match between the Mumbai Indians and Chennai Super Kings took place at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai.
He also shared this photo in a carousel post on his Instagram account on March 24. In the original photo, the poster read, "The man, the myth, the Mahi", an appreciation for Dhoni, who is part of CSK.
Moreover, the caption stated, "Mahi is part of my life. CSK is part of my heart. They never lost whenever I went to the ground and saw the match. 100 per cent success ratio. Whatta night." He also used hashtags such as #CSKvsMI and #WhistlePodu.
Rathna Kumar is an Indian filmmaker and writer. He directed movies like Meyaadha Maan, Aadai and Gulu Gulu. He also wrote for films such as Master, Vikram, Sardar 2, and Karathey Babu. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rathna Kumar (@mr.rathna)
A post shared by Rathna Kumar (@mr.rathna)
Thus, it is evident that a digitally altered image is being falsely shared amid calls for the demolition of Aurangzeb's tomb in Maharashtra, which caused violence in Nagpur earlier this month.
