title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show Bihar cops and Buddhist monks scuffling
content:
This protest was held outside the Chief Minister's residence in Rajasthan on December 21, 2024.
Buddhist monks are protesting in Bihar's Bodh Gaya , seeking complete control of the Mahabodhi temple and demanding the repeal of the Bodh Gaya Temple Act 1949. The act gives Hindus a say in temple operations, disallowing a complete handover of the temple to Buddhists. Support has poured in from across the country, with Buddhist organisations holding rallies in Ladakh, Mumbai, and Mysuru, among other places.
Amid this, a video of protesters allegedly taking to the streets in Bodh Gaya is going viral on social media. A large police force, armed with batons, could be seen stopping protesters from moving forward. The text inside the video in Hindi stated: "Bhim Army on the ground, in honour of the Mahabodhi Bihar."
This video was shared with Hindi captions like: "India is the country of the Buddha. We have been knocking on the doors of the system for a long time. We are demanding justice for the Mahabodhi Mahabihar Mufti movement and are getting nothing. Now, the time has come to break those doors. Shame on the Bihar government and the central government."
India Today Fact Check found that this was a demonstration outside the Chief Minister's residence in Rajasthan on December 21, 2024. It has nothing to do with the Buddhist protests.
Reverse-searching the keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook post from December 2024 that stated this was a Youth Congress protest against Amit Shah in Rajasthan for allegedly insulting Dr BR Ambedkar. On December 17, 2024, Home Minister Amit Shah made a controversial comment about Dr BR Ambedkar during his speech in Parliament, leading to several protests. In December 2024, the official Facebook account of the Indian Youth Congress also shared the viral video .
We found several news reports about this demonstration. According to them, Youth Congress workers held this demonstration in Jaipur on December 21, 2024. Through this protest, they cornered the government on several issues , including unemployment, MSP for farmers, and drug addiction. The police brigade had to use sticks and water cannons to control the crowd moving towards the official residence of Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma.
Congress leader Sachin Pilot also participated in this demonstration. We found another video of this protest, in which he could be seen stepping out of the crowd of protesters.
According to reports , police detained around 40 people, including Rajasthan Youth Congress state president and Sangaria MLA Abhimanyu Poonia, following a scuffle during this protest that left several police officers and protesters injured.
While it is true that protests are taking place regarding the Mahabodhi temple dispute in Bihar, the viral clip of a scuffle between protesters and police has nothing to do with it. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Mar 27, 2025 20:06 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of a mob setting vehicles on fire is NOT from West Bengal's Malda
content:
The video is from Bangladesh's Sylhet and shows vandalism during a protest on November 26, 2023.
Police brought an unruly mob that vandalised shops and vehicles under control in West Bengal's Malda on March 27. The incident reportedly took place during a protest against bursting firecrackers in front of a mosque in Malda's Mothabari area. The incident prompted West Bengal's Leader of the Opposition, Suvendu Adhikari, to write to Governor CV Ananda Bose, requesting immediate deployment of paramilitary forces in the area.
A video allegedly showing the incident is now viral on social media. In it, men can be seen setting fire to vehicles on a street. Sharing the video, one person wrote on Facebook , "As Mamata is in UK, horrific video showing radical mob on a rampage, attacking Hindu shops and burning properties in Malda's Mothabari dist of WB has gone viral on SM."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from Bangladesh's Sylhet and shows vandalism during a protest on November 26, 2023.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to its longer version shared on YouTube on November 27, 2023, by Prothom Alo, a news outlet from Bangladesh. The video's description in Bangla read: "Torchlight procession and vehicle vandalism in support of the blockade in Sylhet."
We found multiple news reports about this incident. Widespread vandalism and arson took place on November 26, 2023, during a 48-hour blockade in Sylhet. The Bangladesh Nationalist Party and its allies called for a blockade against Sheikh Hasina's Awami League government. During it, mobs torched vehicles in Sylhet's Subid Bazar. The miscreants were part of the torchlight procession from the Pathantula area marching in support of the blockade.
Per reports , a CNG-powered auto-rickshaw and an ambulance were among the vehicles set on fire in Subid Bazar. The incident caused panic, leading several local businessmen to shut their shops. However, the parties leading the protest accused the ruling party of causing the incident to defame the opposition.
We also found an X post from the official account of the West Bengal Police about the viral video. The post stated that the video had no links to the Malda incident and that the situation in Malda was under control. The attached video of arson and vandalism is being circulated on social media from certain quarters as an incident of Malda district. This claim is completely FAKE. This video captures events of November, 2023 in Sylhet region of Bangladesh and has no connection whatsoever with pic.twitter.com/5IlmqcFUWO — West Bengal Police (@WBPolice) March 28, 2025
The attached video of arson and vandalism is being circulated on social media from certain quarters as an incident of Malda district. This claim is completely FAKE. This video captures events of November, 2023 in Sylhet region of Bangladesh and has no connection whatsoever with pic.twitter.com/5IlmqcFUWO — West Bengal Police (@WBPolice) March 28, 2025
It is thus clear that a 2023 video from Bangladesh was falsely linked to vandalism in Malda. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Mar 28, 2025 15:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Sanjay Nirupam call Eknath Shinde a traitor? Viral clip edited
content:
This video is clipped. In the original video, Nirupam was attributing this statement to Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Priyanka Chaturvedi
Amid the outrage surrounding Kunal Kamra's controversial stand-up comedy set, two videos featuring Shiv Sena (Eknath Shinde) leader Sanjay Nirupam have gone viral.
Those sharing the videos claimed that while Nirupam was in Congress, he said Eknath Shinde's son should have "My father is a traitor" written on his forehead, but after switching sides, he defended Shinde, saying that calling someone a traitor wasn't a joke.
The first video is in Marathi. Hindi text in it reads, "After falling to the feet of Eknath Shinde," and, "To call somebody a traitor is not a joke". The text in the second video said, "When he was away from the feet of Eknath Shinde," and "It should be written on Eknath Shinde's son's forehead that his father is a traitor".
An X user shared the second video and wrote, "He is Sanjay Nirupam, angry with Kunal Kamra. 2 yrs ago, he called Eknath Shinde a Gaddar. Now he is in Shinde party". Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the second video has been shared out of context. Originally from May 2024, it shows Nirupam reacting to a remark made by Shiv Sena (Uddhav Tackeray) MP Priyanka Chaturvedi, who said the phrase "My father is a traitor" should be written on Eknath Shinde's son's forehead. WHAT DID SANJAY NIRUPAM SAY IN THE FIRST VIDEO?
In the Marathi-language video, Sanjay Nirupam said, "Satire of political leaders is normal. We tolerate such things. But calling someone a traitor is not satire."
He said this on March 24 during a media interaction about the controversy surrounding comedian Kunal Kamra's stand-up set, in which he implied Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde was a traitor. Nirupam emphasised that branding someone a traitor is a serious allegation, not a joke. His complete statement can be seen here . THE TRUTH BEHIND THE SECOND VIDEO
A quick reverse search of the keyframes of this video led us to a May 10, 2024, video report by News 24. This report was about Sanjay Nirupam's reaction to a statement by Shiv Sena (Uddhav Tackeray) MP Priyanka Chaturvedi.
In this video, Nirupam said, "Look, This is a reaction to someone's misbehaviour. Shiv Sena (UBT)'s female MP said that it should be written on the forehead of Eknath Shinde's son that 'My father is a traitor'. His son Shreekant Shinde is the Mahayuti candidate from the Kalyan Lok Sabha seat. I want to respond to her that the real traitor is Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray. Uddhav Thackrey is a traitor. He cheated the voters. He cheated the BJP. And he cheated Balasaheb Thackrey. Balasaheb Thackrey never wanted an alliance with the Congress".
At the time, Priyanka Chaturvedi had said while addressing an election rally that in the Bollywood movie "Deewar", the words"My father is a thief" was written on a child's hand. Similarly, "My father is a traitor" should be written on Eknath Shinde's son's forehead.
This statement sparked a major political controversy, and Nirupam's comments were a direct reaction to it.
Thus, it's clear that a small clip of Sanjay Nirupam's old statement is being circulated with a false context. - Ends With inputs from Praveen Thakare Published By: Vivek Published On: Mar 29, 2025 17:31 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Myanmar earthquake! Video of biker swaying on bridge amid tremors is from Taiwan
content:
This video is from April 2024 and shows the Meilun River bridge swaying from tremors in Taiwan's Hualien City.
The 7.7 magnitude earthquake that rocked Myanmar on March 28 has killed at least 2,700. A video now going viral allegedly shows a biker losing balance and swaying as a bridge shakes during the same tremors.
Many shared the clip with captions such as, "The intensity of the earthquake can be seen through this video, look at the biker," along with hashtags about Myanmar and Bangkok.
India Today Fact Check found that this video was not from Myanmar or Thailand. It is from a 2024 earthquake in Taiwan.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post from February 21. It stated that the viral video was from April 3, 2024, when a 7.4 magnitude earthquake shook a bridge in Taiwan.
We then found multiple social media posts from 2024 featuring the video in question , making it clear that the video predates the Myanmar earthquake.
Responding to one such post, a person shared the coordinates of the location where the video was shot. It was the Meilun River bridge on Shiliugu Boulevard in Taiwan's Hualien City. We checked the Google Street View of this location and found that it matched the viral video. We also found a news report about the earthquake causing damage to this bridge, published in Mandarin. Per reports , at least nine people died in Taiwan after a 7.4-magnitude earthquake, the strongest in 25 years, struck the east coast of Taiwan on April 3, 2024. It is thus clear that a 2024 video from Taiwan was falsely linked to the Myanmar earthquake. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 1, 2025 20:10 IST

title: Fact Check: Myanmar quake videos are quite horrifying. Yet fake AI clips have flooded social media
content:
All these clips are AI-generated.
More than 2,700 people have so far lost their lives in the most powerful earthquake to hit Myanmar in over a century. Thousands more are injured and missing. The 7.7-magnitude tremors devastated several parts of Myanmar and neighbouring Thailand, where an unfinished high-rise building collapsed.
And while the destruction caused by the earthquake has been thoroughly documented, many are sharing AI-generated videos of the quake's effects. Let's look at three such videos. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story A leaning tower Many shared a video of a half-destroyed high-rise. The building's base appeared fully damaged, causing it to lean. Fire trucks could be seen on the road. This video is AI-generated. If you look closely, most responders in the video appear to be standing still. The vehicles look oddly shaped. At the very bottom of the screen, you can also see a man walking through a vehicle like a ghost.
Many shared a video of a half-destroyed high-rise. The building's base appeared fully damaged, causing it to lean. Fire trucks could be seen on the road.
This video is AI-generated. If you look closely, most responders in the video appear to be standing still. The vehicles look oddly shaped. At the very bottom of the screen, you can also see a man walking through a vehicle like a ghost.
It's worth noting that the building somewhat resembles the unfinished headquarters for the auditor-general's office in Bangkok's Chatuchak district, the only skyscraper in Thailand that collapsed because of the quake. The building's dramatic collapse was captured on various videos. View this post on Instagram A post shared by ThePrint (@theprintindia) Volcanic wave Titled "Shocking Bangkok Earthquake Footage Caught on Camera", a video of an unnaturally huge tidal wave was shared online. The video contains glaring discrepancies. For starters, the wave, despite looming over the row of houses, never really reaches them. The wave also starts abruptly and shoots in odd directions — making it look more like an explosion. Shocking Bangkok Earthquake Footage Caught on Camera #bankok #Earthquake #massiveearthquake #video #viralvideo #BangkokEarthquake #ThailandQuake #DisasterResponse #ThailandNews #Emergencyalert #BangkokDisaster pic.twitter.com/5RNunyrwdO — Asian News Bharat (@Asian_newsBH) March 29, 2025 Reverse-searching the video's keyframes led us to an Instagram post dated January 8 from an account called Status AI. The video was captioned, "Volcanic Eruption off the Coast of Italy." The account is full of AI-generated clips of large tidal waves. Bridge over the River AI Another video making the rounds online features various scenes of devastation: a destroyed bridge, a city that looks bombed out with collapsed skyscrapers and rubble all around, and roads full of deep fissures. The video was shared with the claim, "Pray for Myanmar. A powerful 7.7 magnitude Earthquake March 28, 2025." Pray for Myanmar A powerful 7.7 magnitude Earthquake March 28, 2025 #earthquake # #ViratKohli pic.twitter.com/rob8Mim7N9 — Rajak Shaikh (@rajak_sahil1) March 29, 2025 Again, this video has many telltale signs of being AI-generated. The video looks very glossy. The people in it are mostly standing still. In one shot, a person can be seen walking on muddy water without creating any splashes. The video also featured the watermark for Runway in various frames. Runway is an American AI company that offers a suite of AI video tools, including video-generating models. advertisement Incidentally, a bridge in Mandalay, Myanmar, did collapse because of the quake. The Ava Bridge , reportedly built about 90 years ago during British colonial rule, was among the many structures that collapsed. Thus, it's clear that all three videos are AI-generated. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Apr 2, 2025 11:48 IST

title: Fact Check: Superstar Singer 3 winner Avirbhav S is NOT dead, viral rumours false!
content:
Talent Next, the agency that manages Avirbhav S, confirmed that he is alive and well.
A garlanded photo of Kerala child singer Avirbhav S has been widely shared with the claim that he has died. Some shared photos allegedly showing his cremation, along with pictures of singer Neha Kakkar crying. At the time of writing this story, one such post had around three million views.
This rumour is false. The company that manages Avirbhav S confirmed to India Today Fact Check that the child singer is alive and well. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story OUR PROBE Avirbhav S from Kerala and Atharva Bakshi from Jharkhand jointly won the third season of the singing reality show "Superstar Singer" in August 2024. Avirbhav, a native of Kerala's Idukki, became an overnight sensation. His death would have been covered by local and national news outlets. However, we did not find any reports about Avirbhav's death or even ill health.
Avirbhav S from Kerala and Atharva Bakshi from Jharkhand jointly won the third season of the singing reality show "Superstar Singer" in August 2024. Avirbhav, a native of Kerala's Idukki, became an overnight sensation. His death would have been covered by local and national news outlets. However, we did not find any reports about Avirbhav's death or even ill health.
We checked his social media and found that he shared a video singing the popular Tamil song "Unnai Kaanadhu Naan" with his sister Aniirvinhya on Instagram on March 31.
We contacted Suraj Rosario from Talent Next, the agency that manages Avirbhav S. He told us that Avirbhav is healthy and preparing for a US and Canada tour in June and July. NOT A CREMATION
Many of these posts shared photos allegedly showing Avirbhav's cremation. One such photo showed a large gathering of people wearing white clothes standing around a massive fire. It shows the celebration of a festival called Meskel.
Some of the posts claiming Avirbhav's death have links to reports in which they have clarified that this is just a rumour. However, in the social media posts, they have used clickbait headlines suggesting that he died. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Apr 3, 2025 15:33 IST

title: Fact Check: Asaduddin Owaisi crying over Waqf Bill in Lok Sabha? No, this video is from last year
content:
This video dates back to August 7, 2024, and does not show Owaisi crying. He was just rubbing his eyes and forehead. And it has nothing to do with the Waqf Bill.
Since the Waqf Bill was passed in the Lok Sabha, a video of AIMIM MP Asaduddin Owaisi rubbing his eyes has gone viral. Those sharing this clip claimed that Owaisi was crying in Parliament after the Bill was passed.
One such Facebook post read, "Saw Asaduddin Owaisi crying in Parliament today. My heart shattered into pieces. His tears carried the pain of millions, a scream for justice that echoes in my soul." It was shared with hashtags like #WaqfBoard and #Owaisi. Similar posts were shared on X as well. Saw Asaduddin Owaisi crying in Parliament today My heart shattered into pieces His tears carried the pain of millions, a scream for justice that echoes in my soul. #WaqfBoard #Owaisi pic.twitter.com/sreJjkD9lp — Er. Dervinova (@Dervinova) April 2, 2025
Saw Asaduddin Owaisi crying in Parliament today My heart shattered into pieces His tears carried the pain of millions, a scream for justice that echoes in my soul. #WaqfBoard #Owaisi pic.twitter.com/sreJjkD9lp — Er. Dervinova (@Dervinova) April 2, 2025
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from August 2024 and, therefore, predates the Waqf Bill debate.
A search with keywords about Owaisi breaking down during the Waqf Bill debate yielded no credible news results. A reverse search of keyframes from the viral clip took us to a video posted by the AIMIM Instagram account on August 7, 2024. In it, Owaisi was wearing an outfit identical to the one in the viral video, suggesting the video was from last year. View this post on Instagram A post shared by AIMIM (@majlis_official)
A post shared by AIMIM (@majlis_official)
The post's caption said that Owaisi was speaking about the taxation on lower and middle-income families. However, in the viral video, Owaisi was seated while someone else was delivering a speech in the row in front of him.
On Sansad TV's YouTube channel , we found the viral clip shared on August 07, 2024 — the same day as the Instagram post.
The person speaking while Owaisi was seated was Pappu Yadav, the independent MP from Purnia, Bihar. He was delivering a speech at the Lok Sabha when Owaisi rubbed his eyes. This can be seen at the 4-minute 34-second mark in this video.
Watching the full video makes it clear that the AIMIM MP removed his glasses, rubbed his eyes and forehead, and then put his glasses back on. This suggests that Owaisi was likely just rubbing his eyes and not crying. Regardless of what his action meant, however, it's clear that the video is unrelated to the Waqf Bill. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 4, 2025 15:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Manipuri women protesting with torches is NOT recent. It's from 2024
content:
The Viral video is from September 2024, when women in Imphal, Manipur, protested the continued violence in the state.
The Rajya Sabha adopted a statutory resolution on April 4 approving the imposition of President's Rule in Manipur, a day after the same was passed in the Lok Sabha. President's Rule was imposed after N Biren Singh tendered his resignation as chief minister on February 9. Speaking in Parliament, Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated there has been no violence in Manipur for the last four months, adding that talks were on with the Meitei and Kuki communities for a peaceful solution.
Amid this, a video of Manipuri women protesting on the streets with torches in their hands went viral on social media. "This is Manipur, India. People are on the streets against the #state and have declared independence," read the caption of one such post .
India Today Fact Check found that the video in question is from September 2024, when women in Imphal protested the government's inaction on the violence in the state.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the video led us to a post dated September 10, 2024, shared on Facebook by Licypriya Kangujam, an environmental activist from Manipur. At the time , many shared the video in question, with one person posting a longer version as well. This rules out the possibility of this protest being recent.
According to news reports from the time , Meira Paibis, a Meitei women's social movement in Manipur, organised a torch rally on September 9, 2024, in Thangmeiband, Imphal.
They were protesting the government's inaction in resolving the conflict going on in Manipur for more than 16 months. The incident came days after a fresh wave of violence, with multiple attacks reported across several districts. The protesters called for unity in Manipur, urging the government to restore peace. The Press Trust of India also shared the video of the protest, shot from a different angle, on September 9, 2024. VIDEO | Manipur: Women hold a protest rally in Imphal's Thangmeiband over continued violence in the state. (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvqRQz ) pic.twitter.com/lJNvd78970 — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) September 9, 2024
VIDEO | Manipur: Women hold a protest rally in Imphal's Thangmeiband over continued violence in the state. (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvqRQz ) pic.twitter.com/lJNvd78970 — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) September 9, 2024
India Today NE correspondent Keny Phurailatpam also confirmed to us that no such torch rally had taken place in Manipur since the imposition of the President's Rule in the state. Per reports , however, people in Manipur and Nagaland recently took to the streets against the Centre's move to fence the India-Myanmar border. Another protest saw nearly 60 women protesting the frequent transfers of Kakching SP Priyadarshini Laishram.
Thus, it is more than clear that the viral video is not recent, and no such protests against the Centre have recently taken place in Manipur. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Apr 4, 2025 20:34 IST

title: Fact Check: Owaisi, others celebrate passing of Waqf Bill? NO! Here is the truth
content:
This video is not recent, but from January 29, after the Joint Parliamentary Committee meeting to scrutinize the Waqf Amendment Bill concluded.
AIMIM president and Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi challenged the Waqf (Amendment) Bill in the Supreme Court , hours after it was cleared by the Parliament on April 4. Owaisi's petition claims that the amendment violates minority rights and undermines waqf autonomy.
But, amid this sharp criticism, was Owaisi spotted celebrating the passing of the bill with the Joint Parliamentary Committee members and fellow leaders in the Parliament? Many on social media , including some news outlets , claimed so by sharing a video featuring Owaisi having tea and laughing with leaders seated together.
Sharing the clip on X , one person wrote, "So-called protectors of Muslims are enjoying behind the scenes with joy after the passage of the Waqf Amendment Bill. Owaisi is laughing heartily, but because of people like him, Abdul from the Seelampur slum is ready to shed his blood and have his house demolished by a bulldozer."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the video in question is from January 29, after the Joint Parliamentary Committee meeting to scrutinise the Waqf Amendment Bill had concluded.
Reverse searching keyframes from the video led us to a Facebook post of the Bharatiya Janta Party MP Brij Lal . Sharing the video in question, he wrote that leaders of the ruling party and the opposition shared light moments over tea after the JPC on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill adopted amendments on January 29, 2025. We then found some news reports about the viral video. According to them , Parliament's Joint Committee on Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 adopted the draft report and the amended revised bill on January 29. These reports also carried photos of JPC Chairman Jagdambika Pal having tea with fellow JPC members and other leaders, including Owaisi. On January 29, the draft report was adopted by 14 to 11 votes , clearing the way for the government to move the bill to Parliament. Opposition members were given time until 4 pm that day to register their dissent. The JPC approved 14 amendments proposed by the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and rejected all 44 changes submitted by the Opposition MPs. VIDEO | Members of the Joint Parliamentary Committee scrutinising the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, meet over tea after it adopted the draft report. #WaqfAmendmentBill2024 (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/n147TvrpG7 ) pic.twitter.com/wLbjBOXZoA — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) January 29, 2025 Per reports , 11 Opposition members moved dissent notes on the bill, including AIMIM's Asaddudin Owaisi, who filed a 231-page dissent note. We also found a video report by the Indian Express from January 29, featuring Owaisi slamming the "hasty" process of JPC and stating that he had submitted his dissent note. In the clip, Owaisi claimed that the 655-page JPC report was handed to MPs late at night, calling it an attempt to push the bill without thorough discussion. In a dramatic protest, AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi symbolically "tore" a copy of the Waqf Bill at the end of his speech in Lok Sabha on April 2. He had also joined in the "black band" protest against the bill , by wearing a black arm band while offering prayers on March 28 in Hyderabad. It is thus, clear that the viral video of Owaisi laughing with fellow leaders predates the passing of the Waqf Amendment Bill in the Parliament. - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Apr 5, 2025 16:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Jumbo lies. These viral elephant clips are NOT from Kancha Gachibowli
content:
This video showed Rhandzekile, an elephant from the Kruger National Park of South Africa, who was born with a large cavity in its head.
Amid the ongoing dispute over 400 forest acres of land in Kancha Gachibowli that borders the Hyderabad Central University campus, multiple videos of elephants there allegedly struggling due to deforestation have gone viral. Here are three such videos that are wholly unrelated to the row. On the Nose
One video features an elephant with a deep wound just above its trunk, between its eyes. Allegedly, the beast was wounded by a bulldozer in Kancha Gachibowli.
This video has nothing to do with Hyderabad or even India. The clip shows Rhandzekile, an elephant from the Kruger National Park in South Africa. Moreover, what appears to be a wound actually isn't.
Per reports , Rhandzekile was born with a huge cavity in her head. Her condition was found to be stable as her eating and drinking habits had adapted to the cavity. Rhandzekile even gave birth to a healthy calf.
We found multiple videos of the elephant roaming around the forests , shared by people across the years . Bulldozer vs Big Guy
Another viral video shows an elephant ramming headfirst into a bulldozer as people watch from a distance. Again, many claimed this was from Hyderabad.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to multiple news reports about the video. According to them, this video is from February 1 and shows an incident from West Bengal's Jalpaiguri.
A person reportedly provoked a wild tusker by chasing it with a bulldozer. The elephant consequently attacked a multi-level watchtower and lifted the bulldozer with its trunk. Local police in Mal Bazar, Jalpaiguri, arrested the man who allegedly provoked the animal, which was injured in the process. Aid, NOT attack
This video, again allegedly from Hyderabad, shows a bulldozer trying to move a fallen elephant . Those sharing it criticised the authorities for being cruel to the helpless animal.
We found a longer version of the video on a YouTube channel named CP Wild Lanka. According to it, this video, from August 2018, showed a team of wildlife officers in Horowpothana in Sri Lanka.
This elephant was reportedly attacked by another elephant. Forest authorities, as seen in the video, tried to lift it to treat the animal. Unfortunately, however, the elephant succumbed to its injuries.
It is thus clear that old videos of injured elephants from various parts of the world were falsely linked to the Kancha Gachibowli row. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 8, 2025 21:19 IST

title: Fact Check: Madrasas sealed in UP under the Waqf Act? Here are the facts
content:
The viral video shows authorities sealing alleged illegal madrasas in Uttrakhand before the Waqf Act was passed.
The Waqf (Amendment) Act came into effect on April 8. Following that, a video of a madrasa in Uttar Pradesh being sealed by the government under the Act was widely shared. The video shows police officers and a government official telling an old Muslim man that they are sealing the madrasa.
One person wrote alongside the video on Facebook , "Trends have started coming after the Waqf bill was passed. Madrasa activities have started in UP. This video is a lesson for those who thought that nothing will happen with the Waqf bill." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is not from Uttar Pradesh but Uttrakhand. Also, the video was shot before the Waqf Act was implemented and shows authorities sealing alleged illegal madrasas in the state. Our Probe
We observed the badge of the Uttarakhand Police on the shoulder of a policeman in the video, which hinted that it was likely from Uttarakhand. With the help of a keyword search, we found the viral video in a Facebook post from March 24. Its caption suggested that the administration inspected madrasas in the Bhagwanpur Tehsil and that those not registered with the Madrasa Board were sealed.
This clarifies that the incident has nothing to do with the Waqf Act as it was not passed at that time. The Bill was cleared by Parliament on April 4.
We found news reports regarding the sealing of madrasas by the Uttarakhand administration. A video report by News Nation , dated March 24, said that the administration sealed several madrasas in Haridwar and nearby areas like Bhagwanpur and Laksar. The administration had banned over 110 madrasas by labelling them illegal.
At that time, DD News Uttarakhand also reported this government action. Its video report features the same officials seen in the viral video.
We also found several other videos of officials sealing madrasas in Uttrakhand.
Thus, it's clear that the viral video is neither from Uttar Pradesh nor has anything to do with the Waqf Act. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 9, 2025 20:31 IST

title: Fact Check: AI, not Mumbai. This 'Marathi imposition' protest video is fake
content:
This video does not show a real protest. It's AI-generated.
On Gudi Padwa, the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena's Raj Thackeray announced the "Mi Marathi" campaign and urged his supporters to "not hesitate and slap those refusing to speak Marathi in the state". In its aftermath, MNS workers have assaulted several people for the same, from bank workers to security guards. They've also blackened non-Marathi signboards .
While Thackeray later instructed party workers to pause the ongoing agitation, a video allegedly showing a large protest against the imposition of Marathi in front of the Gateway of India in Mumbai went viral on social media. Placards and banners in the hands of these people declared: "I don't speak Marathi. Please don't label us as traitors."
The caption of one such post read, "Opposition to Marathi while living in Maharashtra? Locals outraged. Despite living in Maharashtra, benefiting from its resources, opportunities, and lifestyle, some individuals are openly opposing the Marathi language, sparking widespread outrage among locals," adding that locals questioned the attitude of these protesters.
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video does not show a real protest; it was generated using AI. Our Probe
We could not find any credible news report about a massive protest against "Marathi imposition" in front of the Gateway of India.
We then looked closely at the video and noticed several irregularities. In the beginning, a woman in a red-black outfit had two right arms. The legs of another man and a woman from the crowd appeared jumbled up. There were many more such oddities.
We then reverse-searched keyframes from the viral video and found an Instagram post dated April 9. Its caption stated that the video in question was generated using AI.
It said: "India is a highly linguistically diverse country, with 22 officially recognised languages under the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, and a total of 121 languages and 270 mother tongues. Respect all languages. Disclaimer: Entire content in this video is AI-generated." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Manab Gogoi (@paribhraman)
A post shared by Manab Gogoi (@paribhraman)
According to the bio, this account belongs to Manab Gogoi , an Assamese digital creator. We found several other videos of protests , natural disasters , statues of deities — all seemingly made using AI. The bio of another Instagram account linked to this account states that Gogoi is an "AI Artist". View this post on Instagram A post shared by Manab Gogoi (@paribhraman)
A post shared by Manab Gogoi (@paribhraman)
We reached out to Manab Gogoi for his comments. This article will be updated if and when we receive a response.
Thus, it's clear that this video of a protest against the imposition of Marathi in Maharashtra is not real and was created using AI. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 10, 2025 18:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of Priyanka Gandhi sitting in protest FALSELY linked to Waqf Act
content:
This video has nothing to do with the Waqf Act. It's from August 2022 when Priyanka Gandhi protested price rise and unemployment.
The Indian National Congress and other opposition parties moved the Supreme Court against the newly enacted Waqf Act. Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi also slammed the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Centre over the Waqf legislation, calling it an attack on freedom of religion and the Indian Constitution.
Now, a video of Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra protesting while sitting on a road with others has gone viral. Policewomen can be seen struggling to control the crowd. Those sharing the video claimed that Priyanka Gandhi was protesting the Waqf Act/Bill. Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video has nothing to do with the Waqf Act. It's from August 2022, when Priyanka Gandhi protested inflation and unemployment.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the video led us to a similar video shared by The Times of India on X on August 5, 2022. The post said that Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was sitting in protest with other Congress party leaders and workers outside the All India Congress Committee headquarters. Hindustan Times also shared the same video at the time. #WATCH | #Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra sits on a protest with other leaders and workers of the party outside the AICC HQ pic.twitter.com/VNfjXXxlyQ — The Times Of India (@timesofindia) August 5, 2022
#WATCH | #Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra sits on a protest with other leaders and workers of the party outside the AICC HQ pic.twitter.com/VNfjXXxlyQ — The Times Of India (@timesofindia) August 5, 2022
Another report in The Times of India, published on August 5, 2022, said that several Congress leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, and Priyanka Gandhi, wore black outfits to protest the Centre's handling of issues like inflation and unemployment.
They were stopped by the Delhi Police and not allowed to proceed towards the Rashtrapati Bhawan. The police detained over 200 Congress members during the protest. Priyanka Gandhi was also forcibly put in a vehicle by police and taken away, said the report.
Thus, it's clear that the video is almost three years old and unrelated to the Waqf Act. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Apr 10, 2025 21:17 IST

title: Fact Check: Spectacular arch bridge from China FALSELY shared as Delhi-Srinagar Highway
content:
This video shows the Dafaqu Grand Bridge in China's Guizhou province. It has nothing to do with India.
With a slew of infrastructure projects underway in Jammu and Kashmir, many on social media shared a video of a spectacular arch bridge connecting two mountains, claiming it was the Srinagar-Delhi National Highway 44. Sharing this video, an Instagram user wrote , "Srinagar to Delhi NH44 Complete."
India Today Fact Check found that this video shows the Dafaqu Grand Bridge in China's Guizhou Province and has nothing to do with India. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story OUR PROBE Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to a similar video in an Instagram post from October 2, 2024. The post's caption stated, "The Dafaqu Grand Bridge is a super engineering project in China." View this post on Instagram A post shared by BeautifulChina (@amazingbeautifulchina)
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to a similar video in an Instagram post from October 2, 2024. The post's caption stated, "The Dafaqu Grand Bridge is a super engineering project in China." View this post on Instagram A post shared by BeautifulChina (@amazingbeautifulchina)
A post shared by BeautifulChina (@amazingbeautifulchina)
Subsequent keyword searches led us to a Facebook post shared by China News dated October 24, 2024. The post had several photos of the Dafaqu Grand Bridge. The caption read: "The 1,427-metre Dafaqu Grand Bridge, located in Zunyi, southwest China's Guizhou Province, is a large-span concrete-filled steel tube arch bridge. As one of the key projects along the Renhuai-Zunyi expressway, the bridge closes the distance between Zunyi and Renhuai. It was praised as an engineering marvel created by Guizhou construction engineers."
We then compared the viral video with the Dafaqu Grand Bridge and found many similarities between the two bridges.
We also found several Chinese news reports on this iconic arch bridge in the mountains. As per the Global Times , the Dafaqu Grand Bridge is in China's southwestern province of Guizhou and connects Renhuai city to Zunyi. The photos in the reports are similar to the bridge seen in the viral video.
Notably, the Chenab Rail Bridge between Delhi and Jammu and Kashmir is an arch rail bridge. However, it has not been opened to public use, and it looks very different from the bridge in the viral video.
In the past, videos of Chinese and South Korean bridges have been shared several times, with those sharing them claiming they are from Jammu and Kashmir, which we fact-checked. You can read them here and here .
Thus, it is clear that a video of China's Dafaqu Grand Bridge was falsely shared as a bridge connecting Jammu and Kashmir to Delhi. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 14, 2025 20:10 IST

title: Fact Check: Woman being publicly stoned in Bangladesh? It is not what it seems
content:
This video has been on the internet at least since March 2023, a year before Yunus came to power.
A dramatic video of a woman, buried up to her waist in sand, while a crowd throws stones at her, is being widely shared on social media, claiming it depicts how women are currently being treated in Bangladesh.
We can hear people speaking Bengali in the background.
A Facebook user shared the video with the caption, "A woman is being stoned in Bangladesh. This is the new Bangladesh that the deep state under the Biden administration brought to power."
An archived version of this post can be seen here.
Some X users have reacted sarcastically to the video, suggesting that the situation of women in Bangladesh under Md. Yunus' regime is worse than that in Pakistan.
However, India Today Fact Check found that this video has been present on the internet even before the Muhammad Yunus-led interim government came to power in August 2024. OUR PROBE
At approximately16 seconds into the video, someone can be heard shouting, "Action!" This suggested the footage might be part of a filming sequence.
We then found Shohanur Rahman, a journalist from Bangladesh, who mentioned the same video on X, saying that it was over two years old. He also clarified that this was actually a shooting sequence and not an actual event.
Rahman also noted that what was being thrown at the women during the shooting were not actual stones.
Following this lead, we found a longer version of this video on a YouTube channel named "SHAMIM AHMED CIP." It was uploaded on March 19, 2023 - more than a year before Yunus came to power.
Archived version can be accessed here.
This confirms the video existed on the internet more than a year before the current government took power.
In the longer version of the video, at around the 8-second mark, a man holding a camera is visible, further confirming that this is likely a dramatised scene. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Apr 16, 2025 20:40 IST

title: Fact check: This isn't a Trinamool leader threatening a female officer in Bengal
content:
This video from Tripura shows Congress leader Badruj Jaman arguing with Unakoti SP Sudhambika R on April 12.
Following the violence over the Waqf Amendment Act in West Bengal's Murshidabad, a video of a man and a woman police officer arguing began making the rounds on social media. In it, the police officer blamed the man for gathering a huge crowd and breaking the law by injuring a police officer. She said legal action would be taken against the protesters. In retaliation, the man blamed the officer for giving the police a free hand and threatening people against exercising their right to protest.
Those sharing the clip claimed that the video showed a Trinamool Congress leader threatening a woman DIG in West Bengal. One such post read, "The zahil leader of TMC is threatening to show a woman IPS (DIG) rank officer in West Bengal and is grabbing from bullying. This is the law and order of West Bengal. I claim that DIG is a big thing. It could not talk to a constable in UP even in this tone. Hey sir, leave the constable too. It would not be able to talk to a home guard of UP by showing a finger. If it did, then its finger would have been put in its backyard and so much on its backyard, it would have been so on the back of it".
India Today Fact Check found that the video is not from Bengal at all. It is from Tripura and shows Congress leader Badruj Jaman arguing with Unakoti SP Sudhambika R on April 12.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the clip led us to the same video shared by the YouTube channel of Sangbad365Din, a Tripura-based news website, on April 12. The description stated that the exchange of words happened between the superintendent of police and the district Congress president following an incident in Kailashahar, in the Unakoti district of Tripura.
We found multiple news reports about this incident. Tensions prevailed in Unakoti's Kailashahar after a protest turned violent on April 12. Protesters were demanding the immediate withdrawal of the recently passed Waqf Amendment Act.
Protests reportedly began peacefully in Tillabazar. At the Kubjhar village in Unakoti, things turned violent when some demonstrators began marching towards the Kailashahar town without permission.
Police had set up barricades to prevent escalation, but protesters and policemen clashed. In the process, protesters allegedly hurled bricks at the police, leaving some officers injured. The Tripura Police reportedly detained eight people involved in the incident.
As per reports , Unakoti district superintendent of police Sudhambika R and DIG (Northern Range) Rati Ranjan Debnath rushed to assess the situation. Congress Unakoti district president Badruj Jaman , who was leading the rally, blamed the police for instigating the violence. Jaman was also seen arguing with SP Sudhambika. We also found other videos of the argument seen in the viral clip.
It is thus clear that this video does not show a TMC leader threatening a female officer in West Bengal. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Apr 17, 2025 19:32 IST

title: Murshidabad violence — Ghibli style. How cartoons turned into weapons of hatred
content:
What comes to your mind when you read the word "Ghibli"? People creating soft, warm, cartoon versions of themselves, their pets and their families to share on social media.
Yet, barely a month after ChatGPT launched its new image generator, social media was suddenly full of Ghibli-style photos related to the horrific communal violence in Murshidabad. The violence erupted there after the passing of the Waqf (Amendment) Act.
India Today Fact Check found several such photos being shared online: of people holding religious flags, weapons, and sometimes delivering inflammatory messages, all in the form of adorable cartoon. The intent seems twofold: First, to bypass content moderation systems of social media platforms, and second, to exploit the visual appeal of the trend to influence more people. STICK AND STONES
One common theme was religious processions featuring individuals holding swords and saffron flags. Some images explicitly encouraged people to acquire weapons such as swords and machetes, and to stockpile stones.
Ghibli-style illustrations of Gopal Mukherjee, also known as Gopal Patha, have been widely shared with provocative captions.
Patha was a controversial figure in the Great Calcutta Killings of 1946, when the city was plunged into horrific communal riots that lasted four days and claimed close to 10,000 lives. As per reports , Gopal Patha led the Hindu resistance during the violence.
Illustrations now being circulated in the context of the Murshidabad unrest show Gopal Patha brandishing weapons. One such post on X calls for the creation of "mini militias" to protect Hindu women and children from Islamic violence.
Ghibli-style images of Hindu nationalist leaders from West Bengal are also being widely shared in an attempt to influence people. These include cartoons of Tapan Ghosh , the founder of the far-right group Hindu Samhati.
This image was posted on Facebook on April 9, a day after the Murshidabad violence began. It shows Tapan Ghosh seemingly addressing a public gathering. Alongside one of the images of this collage, it was written, "Who is ready to be Gopal Mukherjee to protect their religion? Now make up your mind". This was from Ghosh's speech in Kolkata on February 14, 2016. MAMATA TARGETED This style is also being widely used to target political leaders. For instance, the West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party portrayed Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee as Adolf Hitler. In another , she was shown playing the flute while surrounded by flames — supposedly West Bengal on fire. HINDU VICTIMS Some illustrations depict the migration of the Hindus in Bengal during the Murshidabad violence. A widely talked about incident in which a bus driver was allegedly asked to remove a saffron flag was also depicted in the Ghibli style. advertisement COMMUNITY GUIDELINES? As per safety guidelines on X , one may share graphic media if it is "properly labelled, not prominently displayed, and is not excessively gory or depicting sexual violence. But "explicitly threatening, inciting, glorifying, or expressing desire for violence" is not allowed." However, we found Ghibli-style content inciting violence being widely shared on X and, at least for now, it seems they are able to slip through the filters in place. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Apr 17, 2025 20:57 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Pahalgam massacre! This video of child sitting on dead body is from 2020
content:
This 2020 video from Kashmir's Sopore shows the corpse of Bashir Ahmad Khan, who was reportedly caught in a crossfire between militants and security forces.
Blood stained the picturesque Baisaran meadow in Kashmir's Pahalgam — popularly known as a "mini Switzerland" — when terrorists shot and killed 28 people, most of them tourists, on April 22. The Resistance Front, a proxy of the Pakistan-based terror group Lashkar-e-Taiba, claimed responsibility for the heinous attack.
One video allegedly from the scene of this violent attack shows a child sitting atop the corpse of a man. The video then cuts to the same child in a vehicle, crying inconsolably, as a woman tries to mollify him with the promise of biscuits and chocolates.
One such post was captioned: "The only fault of this child is that he is a Hindu that is why he lost his father." It was shared with hashtags like "Pahalgam Terrorist Attack" and "Pahalgam Attack".
But is this video from the April 22 attack? India Today Fact Check found that while the video is from Kashmir, it's five years old and shows a Muslim man who died in a crossfire. OUR PROBE
Reverse-searching keyframes from the video led us to a National Herald report from July 2020. The report said that a man called Bashir Ahmad Khan was driving with his three-year-old grandson on the morning of July 1, 2020, when they were caught in crossfire between militants and security forces in Kashmir's Sopore. Khan was killed, but his grandson remained unharmed. A CRPF officer was killed, and three others were injured during the altercation.
An India Today magazine report from July 3, 2020, noted that Khan's family alleged the 65-year-old man was dragged out of his car and killed by the security forces. The Jammu and Kashmir police and the CRPF, however, denied this charge. According to the police, at about 8 am on July 1, 2020, CRPF soldiers were disembarking for deployment when they were ambushed by militants, who opened fire on them.
We also found a Hindustan Times video report on its YouTube channel that showed the young child crying inside a police vehicle. The video from July 1, 2020, relayed the same information.
Thus, it's clear that while this video does show the victim of a militant attack in Kashmir, it has nothing to do with the Pahalgam massacre of April 22. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 23, 2025 18:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Military retaliation after Pahalgam terror attack? No, this clip is old!
content:
This video is at least four years old and therefore unrelated to Pahalgam.
The Indian government, alleging Pakistan's role in the Pahalgam terror attack, announced a slew of diplomatic measures against the country. These include suspending the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 and closing the Integrated Check Post in Punjab's Attari.
And now a video making the rounds on social media claims to show military retaliation against Pakistan as well. In it, a soldier, allegedly from the Indian Army, can be seen firing at bodies lying in a snow-covered mountainous area.
The person recording the video can be heard saying in Hindi that the man shooting the bodies was an Indian Army commander.
The video was shared with captions like "Revenge Mission Started" and hashtags like "Indian Army", "Terror Attack", and "Pahalgam".
India Today Fact Check found that this video is at least four years old and therefore unrelated to Pahalgam.
Using Google Lens, we found the extended version of the video on a website called BestGore.fun . The video was uploaded there on August 16, 2022, with the title, "Indian army executes Kashmiri militants."
Apart from this, a Facebook page called "Indian Military Images" also uploaded a part of the viral clip in December 2020.
We couldn't independently verify the location and date of the video, but it's more than clear that it's old and has nothing to do with the Pahalgam attack.
On April 23, the Cabinet Committee on Security, under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, took several steps against Pakistan in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack. These included the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 and the closing of the Attari check post on the India-Pakistan border in Punjab.
The committee also said no visas for Pakistani nationals under the SAARC Visa Exemption Scheme would be issued any more, existing ones are now deemed cancelled, and any Pakistani national currently in India under these visas would have to leave India within 48 hours.
The committee also declared military, naval and air advisors at the Pakistani High Commission in New Delhi as Persona Non Grata, asking them to leave India in a week. India will also withdraw their counterparts from the Indian High Commission in Islamabad. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 24, 2025 17:58 IST

title: Fact Check: Alia Bhatt, Priyanka Chopra, others FALSELY accused of ignoring Pahalgam attack
content:
All these actors have condemned the Pahalgam massacre on social media.
Following the attack in Kashmir's Pahalgam on April 22, where terrorists shot and killed tourists, condolences poured in from all over the world. Celebrities and world leaders condemned the heinous attack, calling for strict action against the perpetrators.
Meanwhile, a video featuring Instagram stories of Bollywood actors Varun Dhawan, Priyanka Chopra, Alia Bhatt, Dia Mirza, Nora Fatehi, and Sonakshi Sinha has been widely shared. The post claims these actors, who had condemned the Israeli air strike on the Palestinian city of Rafah back in May 2024, were now silent on the Pahalgam massacre. View this post on Instagram A post shared by M O H A K B H A N G A L E (@mok_v_b)
A post shared by M O H A K B H A N G A L E (@mok_v_b)
The video showed their stories about Rafah, and juxtaposed it against their recent stories, which allegedly did not feature any mention of the Pahalgam violence. The video was shared with captions like, "Bollywood on Rafah attack vs now." Many on X shared this video with hashtags like "Boycott Bollywood". The archive of such a post can be seen here .
India Today found that all the actors mentioned in this post have condemned the Pahalgam terror attack through social media.
We scanned the social media accounts of all the actors mentioned in the viral post. We found that actor Alia Bhatt penned a detailed note on the Pahalgam massacre, part of which reads, "The news from Pahalgam is heartbreaking. Innocent lives lost. Tourists, families, people who were just...living. Seeking beauty. Seeking peace. And now there's only grief. And the unbearable weight of it." People were there on vacations, honeymoons, celebrating with their families. Just taking in the beauty of Kashmir. So many innocent lives were caught in a storm they never asked for. The pain we share must fuel our collective resolve—to stand united, to speak louder for peace, and to act against hate in all its forms.
