We will not be silent." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dia Mirza Rekhi (@diamirzaofficial) Sonakshi Sinha and Nora Fatehi posted emotional notes as Instagram stories. And actor Varun Dhawan shared the viral image of Himanshi Narwal sitting by the dead body of her husband, Lieutenant Vinay Narwal, who was slain during the attack. advertisement Besides, other actors like Shah Rukh Khan , Salman Khan , and Akshay Kumar took to social media to express solidarity with the families of the Pahalgam attack victims. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 24, 2025 18:42 IST

title: Fact Check: Chinese diplomat DIDN'T threaten India over Indus treaty suspension after Pahalgam attack
content:
The viral screenshot of Zhao Lijian's X post is fake. Moreover, China has condemned the terrorist attack on tourists in Pahalgam.
Following the massacre of tourists in Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam, the Indian government suspended the Indus Waters Treaty, shut the Attari-Wagah border, and cancelled visas issued to Pakistani nationals, downgrading diplomatic relations with Pakistan.
Now, a screenshot of an X post , allegedly made by Chinese diplomat Zhao Lijian, has begun making the rounds online. In it, he's seemingly threatening India over pausing the Indus treaty. Lijian is the Deputy Director-General of the Department of Boundary and Ocean Affairs of China and a former spokesperson for the Chinese foreign ministry.
The post whose screenshot is being shared reads: "China will block the Brahmaputra and Sutlej rivers flowing into India if it didn't restore the Indus Water Treaty." Sharing the screenshot , many shared their opinions on the issue.
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the viral post was fake. Lijian has not made any such post regarding the incident. Our Probe
We first checked the X account of Zhao Lijian but found no such post on the account. Lijian's last post on the platform, at the time of writing this, was on August 12, 2024. Since 2023, he hasn't posted anything on Instagram either.
We also checked Zhao Lijian's account on the Chinese social media site Weibo . Lijian has made a total of four posts since April 22, the day of the Pahalgam terror attack, and none of them are about the attack or the Indus Water Treaty. Discrepancies in the viral screenshot The X post featured in the viral screenshot has several discrepancies. Firstly, it states the number of retweets and quote-tweets for the post. The current interface of X, however, does not have these labels. Retweets are now called reposts, and quote tweets are now simply called quotes. We then compared the viral screenshot with one of Lijian's actual posts. It featured a verification badge next to the username, the number of views on the post, and the number of bookmarks — all missing in the viral screenshot. A comparison can be seen below. Several online tools can generate fake X posts in the name of anyone within a few seconds. We used one such tool called Tweetgen and created a similar X post for Lijian's account. The appearance and elements in this fake X post matched the viral one. It is possible that this tool or other similar ones were used to create the viral X post. China on the Pahalgam terror attack China's foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun strongly condemned the April 22 terror attack and mourned the victims. The Chinese ambassador to India, Xu Feihong, similarly expressed shock over the massacre and offered condolences to the bereaved families. China and Pakistan advertisement China has solidified its role as Pakistan's biggest arms supplier , making up 81 per cent of Pakistan's weapons imports in the past five years. The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor is one of the most significant infrastructure projects, aimed at connecting western China to Pakistan's Gwadar Port through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. In 2021, China reiterated its support for Pakistan over the Kashmir issue. It is, thus, clear that the viral screenshot is fake and does not reflect Beijing's official stance on the issue so far. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Apr 24, 2025 19:30 IST

title: Fact Check: This video does NOT show Indian army's attack along the LOC, it's from 2023
content:
Viral video is from May 2023, when Islamabad police used tear gas at people protesting against the arrest of Imran Khan.
The situation along the Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir remains tense, as Pakistani troops resorted to unprovoked firing yet again, prompting a response from the Indian Army. Relations between the two countries soured following the massacre of tourists in Pahalgam, to which India responded with punitive measures like suspension of the Indus treaty, closure of the Attari-Wagah border, and cancellation of visas to Pakistani nationals.
Amid this, a video making the rounds on social media purportedly showed the Indian army's offensive across the LOC, resulting in heavy losses on the Pakistani side. The video showed a huge crowd of people running away as smoke billowed from a distance. Among the crowd, some could be heard sloganeering and asking people to gather stones to pelt at the attackers.
Sharing the video one person wrote, "Pakistan faced heavy losses at the LOC with multiple posts being dismantled across various locations. Indian Army is in no mood to show mercy on these terrorist nation (sic)."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the video in question is from May 2023, and has nothing to do with the aftermath of the Pahalgam attack.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an X post dated May 11, 2023. Sharing the viral video, the post called for the banning of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.
The same video was shared by some other social media accounts as well at the time. The caption of one such post read: "Scenes of state oppression on PTI protesters at H11 Highway Islamabad. They are literally attacking their own citizens right now, incredibly disgusting. Pakistanis are brave soldiers of a strong-nerved leader Imran Khan."
It is hereby, clear that the viral video predates the Pahalgam attack by more than two years.
We then found multiple news reports about this incident. According to a report by Dawn , the PTI supporters in Islamabad and Rawalpindi took to the streets on May 9, 2023, to protest the arrest of party chairman Imran Khan. The police had to fire tear gas shells to disperse the protesters, who blocked multiple roads and highways.
Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was arrested by paramilitary troops from the Islamabad High Court, where he appeared seeking bail in multiple corruption cases on May 9, 2023 . This was followed by violent protests from PTI workers and supporters of Imran Khan across the country.
We also found several other videos of a protest , similar to the viral video, shared on X on the night of May 10, 2023, by journalists . #EXCLUSIVE : @ICT_Police operation underway with heavy teargas shelling in #Islamabad on Sirinagar highway and expressway to open/clear roads blocked by #PTI workers. pic.twitter.com/hjOlZxMAA1 — Asad Ali Toor (@AsadAToor) May 10, 2023
#EXCLUSIVE : @ICT_Police operation underway with heavy teargas shelling in #Islamabad on Sirinagar highway and expressway to open/clear roads blocked by #PTI workers. pic.twitter.com/hjOlZxMAA1 — Asad Ali Toor (@AsadAToor) May 10, 2023
It is thus, clear that a 2023 video was falsely shared as an attack by the Indian army along the LOC after the Pahalgam attack. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Apr 27, 2025 15:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Pak-based users share old, unrelated video to push propaganda against Indian Army
content:
This March 2025 video has nothing to do with Pakistan. It shows a press conference related to the Colonel Pushpinder Singh Bath assault incident.
Following the Pahalgam terror attack, a video circulating online claims to show Indian Army officials walking out of a meeting, expressing their desire to not go to war against Pakistan.
The video likely shows a press conference. Several men in uniform can be seen leaving the room, after which a man can be heard saying, "What is the army afraid of? Why are they running away like this?" Many Pakistan-based accounts shared this video.
Sharing the video, a Facebook user wrote , "Breaking News: Indian Army Generals walked out of the meeting, they said we are not capable of fighting a war against Pakistan. Modi still wants war, but his army isn't capable of fighting!" The archived version of a similar post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this March 2025 video has nothing to do with Pakistan. It shows a press conference related to the Colonel Pushpinder Singh Bath assault incident.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the clip led us to the same video shared by Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia on his Instagram account on March 25. He praised journalist Man Aman Singh Chhina for "persistently asking questions to ensure justice for Col. Pushpinder Singh Bath and his family".
Notably, Indian Army Colonel Pushpinder Singh Bath and his son Angad were allegedly assaulted by Punjab Police personnel over a parking dispute outside a Patiala dhaba in March 2025. A Special Investigation Team led by Chandigarh Police SP Manjeet Sheoran is probing the case. In connection with the incident, four officers have been suspended and transferred.
On Chhina's social media profile, he had shared the same video and wrote, "Chief of Staff Western Command Lt Gen Mohit Wadhwa just scooted away with his senior officers after reading out a statement on the Patiala Colonel without taking any questions. The DGP also read out a statement and left but at least he has answered questions of media in recent days. What is the Army afraid of?" Chief of Staff Western Command Lt Gen Mohit Wadhwa just scooted away with his senior officers after reading out a statement on the Patiala Colonel without taking any questions. The DGP also read out a statement and left but at least he has answered questions of media in recent pic.twitter.com/86Ytgee0sz — Man Aman Singh Chhina (@manaman_chhina) March 25, 2025
Chief of Staff Western Command Lt Gen Mohit Wadhwa just scooted away with his senior officers after reading out a statement on the Patiala Colonel without taking any questions. The DGP also read out a statement and left but at least he has answered questions of media in recent pic.twitter.com/86Ytgee0sz — Man Aman Singh Chhina (@manaman_chhina) March 25, 2025
In a joint press conference held on March 25 , Gaurav Yadav, DGP of Punjab Police, and Lieutenant General Mohit Wadhwa, Chief of Staff, HQ Western Command, issued a joint statement on the assault of serving Colonel Bath. The viral clip shows the same press conference, where Chhina criticised Army officials for not taking questions from the media.
In the conference, General Mohit Wadhwa called for a fair and honest investigation ( https://www.hindustantimes. com/india-news/col-assault- incident-army-calls-for-fair- probe-highest-respect-for- army-says-punjab-dgp- 101742903225678.html ) to be conducted transparently and within a set timeframe, to punish those responsible for the assault on Colonel Bath.
Thus, it is evident that an old and unrelated clip from a press conference regarding the Pushpinder Singh Bath assault incident is being shared with wrongful claims. - Ends Written by Abhishek Pathak Published By: Harshita Das Published On: Apr 27, 2025 22:32 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Akshay Kumar hasn't asked for donations to buy weapons for the Indian Army!
content:
This fund was started back in 2016 and it is used to provide financial assistance to the families of soldiers who get grievously injured or sacrifice their lives during operations.
As tensions rise between India and Pakistan in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack, many fear war is on the horizon. And a message going viral right now purports to show how you can chip in and do your part to help the Indian Army.
The message informs us about a bank account to which people can donate money to modernise the Indian Army. Per the message, Prime Minister Narendra Modi started this programme at the suggestion of Bollywood actor Akshay Kumar.
One such post read : "Another good decision by Modi Govt as suggested by Super Star Akshay Kumar. Only one rupee per day, that too for Indian army. In yesterday's cabinet meeting, the Modi government opened a bank account for the modernisation of the Indian Army and for soldiers who are injured or martyred in the war zone. In which every Indian can contribute any amount as per his/her own choice. It starts from Rs.1 and is unlimited. This money will also be used to purchase weapons for the army and paramilitary forces."
The post then provided the details of the Army Welfare Fund Battle Casualty Fund account in the Canara Bank. These details included the bank account, the Indian Financial System Code or the IFSC, and the name of the bank branch - the South Extension Branch in New Delhi.
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the viral message is misleading. Donations to the Army Welfare Fund Battle Casualty Fund or the AFBCWF are not meant for purchasing weapons for the Army. It's to provide financial assistance to the families of soldiers who get grievously injured or sacrifice their lives in military operations. WHAT IS THE AFBCWF?
On the website of the Indian Army, we found the details of two bank accounts where people can donate money: The Army Central Welfare Fund and the Armed Forces Battle Casualties Welfare Fund. Donations received through these funds are used to give financial assistance "to widows of soldiers, their next of kin, dependents, and needy ex-servicemen as a welfare measure".
The website stated that the fund is maintained by the Indian Army on behalf of the Ministry of Defence for families of battle casualties from the Army, the Navy, and the Air Force. The website also shared the account number, the IFSC, and other details of both the bank accounts.
Notably, however, while the account number mentioned in the viral posts are correct, the IFSC and the branch details don't match.
According to an October 2019 Ministry of Defence press release on the Press Information Bureau website , the fund was set up by the Ministry of Defence after a large number of people offered to provide monetary assistance to the families of battle casualties following the February 2016 Siachen incident, in which 10 soldiers were buried in an avalanche.
On April 27, the Press Information Bureau's Fact-Check account also debunked the viral claim. The post called the viral posts misleading and wrote: "Armed Forces Battle Casualties Welfare Fund (AFBCWF) was created to provide immediate financial assistance to the families of soldiers who have sacrificed their lives or were injured during military operations." A WhatsApp message is going around claiming that government has opened a bank account for the modernization of the Indian Army. #PIBFactCheck This claim is MISLEADING The bank account mentioned in the message is NOT meant for modernization of Indian Army or for purchase pic.twitter.com/flm2vGe22G — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) April 27, 2025
A WhatsApp message is going around claiming that government has opened a bank account for the modernization of the Indian Army. #PIBFactCheck This claim is MISLEADING The bank account mentioned in the message is NOT meant for modernization of Indian Army or for purchase pic.twitter.com/flm2vGe22G — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) April 27, 2025
The post is linked to another Ministry of Defence press release from December 2022. It said a website called "Maa Bharati Ke Sapoot" was launched by Rajnath Singh to contribute towards the Armed Forces Battle Casualties Welfare Fund. It also noted that the fund in question has been in existence since 2016. advertisement AKSHAY KUMAR'S DIFFERENT INITIATIVE In 2017, Akshay Kumar urged Indians to contribute a rupee every month for the Army via a web portal called "Bharat Ke Veer". The portal was launched by Kumar in association with the Ministry of Home Affairs. Such an Honour to Garland the sacred soil of the Sardar Post on #ValourDay . Launching my dream, #BharatKeVeer as we speak!! Jai Hind pic.twitter.com/JbJUoNbq5i — Akshay Kumar (@akshaykumar) April 9, 2017 In a 2017 interview with India Today , the actor said: "The Government is doing a lot for our martyrs but being a civilian, it's our duty too to contribute. It doesn't matter if it is Rs 5 or Rs 10 or Rs 1 lac. The idea is to get people to collect money and directly send it to the person who has lost their loved ones." He added, "This was just an idea, and has worked very well. You will be happy to know that within two-and- a-half months, we have collected about Rs 13-14 crore. This shows people of India care, and I request you to keep on caring." advertisement This contribution is also meant to help the next kin of slain soldiers, and not to purchase weapons. The State Bank of India also created a UPI ID for contribution to the "Bharat Ke Veer" initiative. The State Bank of India @TheOfficialSBI has created a UPI for #BharatKeVeer initiative. You can now help the families of India's bravehearts by contributing through UPI using VPA- bharatkeveer@sbi pic.twitter.com/HoXfODhoYK — Bharat Ke Veer (@BharatKeVeer) February 16, 2019 It is thus clear that the Armed Forces Battle Casualties Welfare Fund is neither new nor meant for purchasing weapons - it's there to provide financial assistance to families of injured or slain soldiers. - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Apr 28, 2025 12:15 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of Hyderabad hospital fire FALSELY shared as Houthi strike on Mossad HQ
content:
This December 2023 video shows a massive fire at the Ankura Hospital in Hyderabad, India.
Amid the ongoing conflict between Israel and Yemen's Houthi rebels, a video circulating online claims to show Yemen striking the headquarters of Israel's intelligence agency Mossad in Tel Aviv. The video shows a massive fire in a building. A plume of black smoke can be seen in the sky.
The Arabic text in the video also said that the building was the Mossad headquarters and that Yemen's hypersonic missiles targeted it. Sharing the video on Facebook , one person wrote, "Yemen strikes Israel's Mossad headquarters in Tel Aviv! That's what I'm talking about! Amazing! Go Yemen."
India Today Fact Check found that this December 2023 video actually shows a massive fire at the Ankura Hospital in Hyderabad, India.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to a December 2023 post featuring a photo of the same building featured in the viral video. The post claimed that the building was a hospital in Hyderabad.
We then found several news reports featuring the same building's photo. As per an India TV report , a massive fire was reported at the Ankura Hospital near Gudimalkapur in Hyderabad on December 23, 2023. As per the officials, a flex board on the building caught fire because of a suspected short circuit. There were no casualties or injuries reported. View this post on Instagram A post shared by NDTV (@ndtv) As per news reports , Yemen's Houthi rebels fired a missile toward Israel last Sunday. Israel, however, claimed that it intercepted the missile before it entered its territory. Meanwhile, the US is also targeting the Houthis due to the Red Sea blockade. On Monday, the Houthis claimed that a US airstrike hit a prison where African migrants were being held. The strike killed at least 68 people and injured 47 others. Thus, it is evident that an old video from 2023, showing a fire at a Hyderabad hospital, is being falsely shared as Yemen's strike on the Mossad headquarters. (Written by Abhishek Pathak) - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 28, 2025 17:47 IST

title: Fact Check: 2023 video from Gaza VIRAL as India's revenge on Pakistan after Pahalgam attack
content:
The video is from November 2023, when Israel dropped bombs near a hospital in the Gaza Strip.
On the night of April 28-29, the Pakistan Army resorted to unprovoked firing across the Line of Control for the fifth consecutive time following the terror attack in Pahalgam. Pakistan's defence minister said on April 28 that "a military incursion" by India was imminent in the aftermath of the Pahalgam attack.
Now, a video of people running helter-skelter amid heavy bombardment at a distance is being widely shared online with the claim that India conducted this attack at the India-Pakistan border to avenge the Pahalgam massacre.
Sharing the video on Facebook , one person wrote, "Pakistan situation now. Bharat Mata Ki Jai. #Pahalgam Terror Attack."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video is from the Gaza Strip, and is more than a year old. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook post from November 10, 2023, by Omar Suleiman, an American Islamic scholar and civil rights activist. Its caption stated that Israel dropped bombs on the Indonesia Hospital outside the Jabalia Refugee Camp in Gaza.
We then found multiple news reports about this incident. According to them, people fled from a hospital in Beit Lahia in Gaza during an Israeli strike in a nearby street. An Al Jazeera video report about this featured the viral clip, along with some other footage from the attack.
Per reports , hundreds of people were injured in this Israeli airstrike near the Indonesia Hospital, which was opened in Beit Lahia in 2015. The hospital, built from donations raised by an NGO, was one of the last remaining hospitals in Gaza. A week before this attack, the Israeli military had claimed that Hamas was using this hospital "to hide an underground command and control center".
Back in October 2024, the same video was shared on social media as Israel's attack on Iran. We had debunked it at the time as well.
It is thus clear that a 2023 video from Gaza was falsely linked to the ongoing India-Pakistan tensions. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Apr 29, 2025 14:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Amid ceasefire violations, Pak accounts share OLD video as attack on Indian Army depot
content:
This 2022 video shows an explosion in Sialkot, Pakistan. It has no connection to the ongoing tensions between the two countries.
Amid Pakistan's repeated ceasefire violations following the Pahalgam terror attack, a video showing massive explosions has gone viral. Many Pakistan-based accounts on social media claimed these explosions occurred at a military ammunition depot in India and were carried out by the Pakistani army.
This 30-second-long video features several houses, indicating that the area was residential. At some distance, flames from the blasts were visible. Loud explosions could also be heard. A Pakistan-based account shared the video on X and wrote: "Massive explosions reported at the military ammunition depot in India's Lipa Valley after being targeted by Pakistani forces." Its archive can be seen here .
Some also claimed that the Indian Army caused these explosions in Pakistan. Notably, the Leepa Valley is part of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
India Today Fact Check found that this video has no connection to the ongoing tensions between the two countries. It's from 2022 and shows a massive explosion in Sialkot, Pakistan. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to a March 2022 post which contained the same video. This made it evident that the video is not related to the current tensions between the two countries that began after the Pahalgam massacre on April 22. The post said that the video was from Sialkot in Pakistan.
We found several news reports featuring the same visuals. According to a report by India.com , a massive explosion occurred in Sialkot, Pakistan, on March 20, 2022. The sound of the blast was reportedly heard near the cantonment area in the Punjab province of Pakistan.
According to reports , the explosions were caused by an accidental fire that broke out in an ammunition shed near the Sialkot Garrison due to a short circuit.
"Due to effective and timely response, the damages were immediately contained," the Pakistan Army's media wing said at the time, adding, "The fire has been extinguished." It also said there was no damage to property or loss of life.
Thus, it is evident that a 2022 video of explosions in Sialkot is being falsely shared in connection with the current tensions between India and Pakistan.
(Written by Abhishek Pathak) - Ends Published By: Anupriya Thakur Published On: Apr 29, 2025 17:48 IST

title: Fact Check: This army vehicle collision is from BEFORE the Pahalgam attack. No lives were lost in it
content:
This accident, caused by slippery roads in J&K's Baramulla, predates the Pahalgam terror attack. No lives were lost in it.
Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar claimed on April 30 that there is "credible information" about a possible Indian military strike against the nation in the next 24–36 hours. This came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi reportedly granted the Indian Army "complete operational freedom" to respond to the Pahalgam terror attack.
Now, some are sharing a video on social media, alleging that an Indian Army vehicle hurtling towards the Pakistan border claimed the lives of six Sikh women and children. The video shows soldiers coming out of an army vehicle surrounded by seemingly distressed people.
Sharing the video on Facebook, a Pakistan-based account wrote: "#BREAKING. Indian Army personnel killed six Sikh women and children after a convoy racing toward the Pakistan border struck them. A police investigation found that the Army driver was drunk."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this accident took place before the Pahalgam attack and no lives were lost in it. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a YouTube video dated April 17. Its description stated there was an accident at Rafiabad, a tehsil in the Baramulla district of Jammu and Kashmir. This makes it clear that this incident predates the Pahalgam attack.
We found several videos and photos of this accident , shared on social media platforms on April 16 . These posts stated that four people were injured after an army vehicle collided with a car and a motorcycle in the Hadipora region of Rafiabad in Baramulla . All four injured were reportedly taken to the Government Medical College in Baramulla for treatment . According to a news report , the accident took place near the Government Degree College in Hadipora and was caused by slippery roads. The authorities have launched an investigation into the accident. Sheikh Dawood Ahmad, India Today's correspondent from Baramulla, confirmed that this accident predates the Pahalgam attack and did not claim any lives. Two injured people were discharged immediately, while the other two — a woman named Fahmeeda and a man named Fazilka Qayoom — are currently being treated at a hospital and are expected to be discharged soon. It is thus clear that the video of an accident that took place before the Pahalgam attack was falsely linked to the ongoing tensions between India and Pakistan. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Apr 30, 2025 16:01 IST

title: Fact Check: One crash, many claims. How an old video went viral amid rising Ind-Pak tensions
content:
This video from June 2024 shows a Sukhoi fighter jet that crashed during testing in Nashik, Maharashtra.
In the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack, social media has turned into a digital battlefield, at least for Indians and Pakistanis. And misinformation is aplenty in this online war.
Take, for example, this video going viral right now. It shows flames raging in a field and plumes of black smoke wafting. Pakistan-based accounts claimed it showed the Indian Air Force's newly-inducted Rafale fighter jet shot down by Pakistan near the LoC.
Conversely, many Indian accounts claimed that this was a Pakistani F-16 Fighting Falcon , eliminated by the Indian Air Force near Sialkot. Multiple accounts on Facebook and X shared the video with these claims.
A simple reverse search tells the real story of the viral video. The video is from June 2024, when a Sukhoi fighter jet of the Indian Air Force crashed in Nashik, Maharashtra. Both pilots were ejected safely before the impact.
According to various news reports from June 2024 , a Sukhoi Su-30MKI fighter jet crashed in a field in a field near Nashik's Shirasgaon village. The aircraft took off from Ozar in the Nashik district and was on a test flight after being overhauled by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. The pilots reported a technical snag in the aircraft.
The deadly Pahalgam terror attack has escalated tensions between India and Pakistan. Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired a meeting with the military brass in New Delhi on April 29, and reportedly said that the armed forces have complete freedom to decide mode, targets, and timing of response to terrorism.
On the other hand, Pakistan's information minister, Attaullah Tarar, said on Wednesday that India intends to launch military action on Pakistan within the next 24 to 36 hours. As per reports , Pakistan also opened fire along the international border in Jammu and Kashmir's Pargwal sector last night, to which India responded. - Ends Published By: Atul Mishra Published On: Apr 30, 2025 18:51 IST

title: Fact Check: 2020 crash video FALSELY shared as Pak shooting down its own plane!
content:
The viral video is from May 2020. The crash was caused by human error. It wasn't shot down by the Pakistan Air Force.
Since the April 22 terror attack in Kashmir's Pahalgam, the Pakistani military has been on high alert , anticipating a possible Indian strike, leading to heightened tensions on the border.
Now, a video showing a residential area with plumes of smoke and flames is going viral on social media. This video allegedly shows a Pakistani passenger plane shot down by the country's own air force. An X user shared the clip and wrote, "A passenger plane shot down by @DGPR_PAF near Karachi airport. A plane hit a residential area, and almost 100 people were onboard."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from May 2020. The plane wasn't shot down — the crash happened because of "human error".
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a YouTube video dated May 22, 2020. The video's description stated that a Pakistan International Airlines plane, PK-8303, had crashed near Karachi's Jinnah International Airport. The flight was returning from Lahore and was about to land when it crashed near Model Colony in Malir, Karachi.
We found the viral video's screengrabs in several news reports published in May 2020. Reportedly, 101 people, including 99 passengers and flight crew members, lost their lives , while two passengers survived.
Per the New York Post , witnesses said the passenger plane appeared to have attempted to land several times before the crash in a residential area of Karachi. The plane first hit a mobile tower and crashed into houses, a witness said. The PIA said that the pilot made a mayday call saying he was experiencing a technical problem.
Four years after the incident, the final report was released by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Board in 2024. According to it, the crash was caused by "human error" due to a lack of coordination between the pilots of flight PK-8303 and the air traffic controller.
Notably, we did not find any news reports suggesting the Pakistani Air Force shot down a passenger plane in Karachi recently. Thus, it's clear that an old video of a plane crash was shared with false claims. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: May 1, 2025 19:48 IST

title: Fact Check: Hindu family attacked for posting anti-Pak content? No, this was a road rage case
content:
This was a road rage incident. Shoaib Umar Saiyyad and his associates beat up Harsh Keshwani in Pune for honking. They later allegedly assaulted his family as well.
As tensions between India and Pakistan heighten with every passing day, in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack, a video of a brawl was virally shared with shocking claims. A post alleged, "A Hindu family in Pune was attacked by a group after posting against Pakistan on social media."
Many shared the video on Facebook and wrote captions like: "In our own country, a Hindu family in Pune was brutally attacked just for speaking out against Pakistan. This is the harsh reality we face — silenced in our own home for voicing the truth."
India Today Fact Check found that the clash had nothing to do with an anti-Pakistani post on social media. It was a road rage incident.
Upon reverse-searching the viral clip's keyframes, we came across a news report published in My Pune Pulse on April 29, featuring screengrabs from that video. The incident occurred in the busy Bhawani Peth area of Pune. Reportedly, a two-wheeler rider honked at a pedestrian crossing the road, who then confronted the rider. This soon escalated into a brawl.
According to a Lokmat Times report, on Sunday, April 27, Harsh Keshwani honked his horn while passing through the narrow lane. Shoaib Umar Saiyyad, who had parked his auto-rickshaw on the road and was unloading goods, was angered by this. He allegedly abused Harsh and physically attacked him. When his brother Karan, his sister Nikita, and their grandfather Bharat arrived and confronted Shoaib, he and his associates attacked the family.
Shoaib allegedly hit Harsh on the head with a stone and threatened to kill him. Harsh was reportedly rushed to the hospital for treatment. The others were injured as well. They claimed that Shoaib also threatened to burn their house down. A Pune Mirror report also said the same.
According to a Punekar News report, the police detained the accused, Shoaib, and registered an attempt-to-murder case against him and other unidentified accomplices, following an FIR lodged by Karan Lalit Keshwani at Khadak Police Station.
India Today Fact Check reached out to Mahendra Kamble, the investigating officer in the case. He confirmed to us that no social media post led to this brawl — it was a road rage incident.
Therefore, it is abundantly clear that a video of a brawl was shared with a false story. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: May 2, 2025 18:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Kashmiri locals DIDN'T fight with Army after Pahalgam attack, this video is old
content:
This 2022 video from Srinagar in Kashmir long predates the Pahalgam terror attack. According to reports, a case was registered against the soldiers by the J&K Police.
Amid escalating tensions between India and Pakistan, a video began making the rounds on social media showing an Indian Army soldier beating a civilian with sticks. Those sharing the clip claimed that locals in Kashmir got into a fight with the Indian army following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack.
Sharing the clip on Instagram , one person wrote, "Kashmiri locals fighting with Indian Army. And yes it's April 2025 and after Pahalgam terrorist attack."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video predates the Pahalgam attack. The video is from August 2022, when Indian army personnel had beaten up a civilian in Srinagar. OUR PROBE
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a news report about this incident from August 22, 2022. According to it, Indian Army personnel hit a civilian with sticks at Nowgam Chowk in Srinagar. This makes it clear that the video predates the Pahalgam attack by almost three years.
We then found multiple news reports about this incident from 2022. As per reports, some uniformed soldiers beat up a civilian after they got into a minor fight in Srinagar . Following the incident, the Nowgam Police Station registered a case under sections 323, 341 of the IPC against the soldiers on August 18, 2022.
"On Monday afternoon, an incident came to notice wherein some Army personnel in uniform reportedly beat up a civilian, while other personnel present also got involved in a minor fight at the Nowgam chowk," the Srinagar Police said in a statement . J&K police registers FIR after a video showing army men beating civilians at Nowgam area of Srinagar went viral. "On receipt of this information, cognisance of incident was taken and a case under FIR number 116/2022 under sections 323,341 of IPC was registered in nowgam PS." https://t.co/LauWTVWKZQ — Ieshan Wani (@Ieshan_W) August 22, 2022
J&K police registers FIR after a video showing army men beating civilians at Nowgam area of Srinagar went viral. "On receipt of this information, cognisance of incident was taken and a case under FIR number 116/2022 under sections 323,341 of IPC was registered in nowgam PS." https://t.co/LauWTVWKZQ — Ieshan Wani (@Ieshan_W) August 22, 2022
In the video, we can see two soldiers pulling out the driver of a load carrier and hitting his head with a stick . During the altercation, another civilian could be seen trying to rescue the person.
At the time, many had shared the video of the incident on social media platforms . In one such post , we found another video of the incident shot from a different angle.
It is thus clear that the video of soldiers beating up a civilian in Srinagar predates the Pahalgam attack, and is therefore unrelated to it. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: May 4, 2025 20:13 IST

title: Fact Check: Air Force jet crashes during drill? This video is over a decade old!
content:
This video has been online since 2013 and likely shows a 2010 crash. No Air Force plane crash has been reported in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22.
Amid rising tensions between India and Pakistan in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack, Pakistan- and Bangladesh-based social media users began sharing a video of a fighter jet catching fire right after taking off and subsequently crashing. They claimed it was an Indian Air Force fighter jet.
One Facebook post said, "An Indian Air Force fighter jet has crashed during a takeoff drill from a highway as part of a wartime exercise. This is the second crash of their fighter jet since the start of the three-day exercise. Very sad."
India Today Fact Check found that while the viral video shows an Air Force MiG-27 and the clip is more than a decade old.
A simple reverse search led us to a longer version of the viral video uploaded to YouTube on January 16, 2013. The video's description stated that the two fighter jets seen in the video were MiG-27. This made it clear that the video is not recent.
In the video's comments, many people said that it shows the February 2010 crash of an Indian Air Force's MiG-27 plane flown by Wing Commander Oswald de Abreu.
We found a 2024 Instagram post featuring the same video, which stated that it was from February 16, 2010. As per the post, Wing Commander Oswald de Abreu was tasked to carry out an operational mission. Within minutes of taking off, he reported an engine fire and crashed inside the airbase. Oswald did not survive the accident. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Officer's Mind (@officers_mind) A Hindustan Times report from the time said that the mishap happened at West Bengal's Hasimara IAF base, where a fighter squadron is based. The wing commander was reportedly doing a sortie to Bagdogra. Following the incident, the Eastern Air Command headquarters in Shillong ordered a probe into the incident. HAS THERE BEEN A RECENT ACCIDENT? The Air Force on May 2 conducted a flypast and landing exercise drill on Uttar Pradesh's Ganga Expressway. However, no plane crashes or accidents have been reported. We did not find any credible news reports of an Air Force plane crash after the terror attack in Pahalgam. The most recent Air Force plane crash occurred on April 2 when a Jaguar fighter jet went down in Gujarat. Thus, it's clear that an old video was falsely shared as recent. - Ends Published By: Prateek Chakraborty Published On: May 5, 2025 20:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Indian dam collapsed trying to stop Pak's water? No, this 2019 clip is from US
content:
This video is from 2019 and shows a spillway failure at Lake Dunlap in the US. It has nothing to do with India and Pakistan.
After suspending the Indus Waters Treaty — a consequence of the Pahalgam terror attack — India briefly stopped water flowing through the Baglihar dam on the Chenab River. Reportedly, the Centre is planning to do the same at the Kishanganga Dam in Jammu and Kashmir.
Now, many Pakistan-based social media users are sharing a video of an alleged Indian TV news report of the gates of a dam collapsing. They claimed this was the Kishanganga dam. A voiceover in the video says the same.
Sharing this video, an X user wrote , "Breaking: India's move to block water at the Kishanganga Dam has backfired. The dam gates could not withstand the pressure and collapsed."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from 2019 and shows a spillway failure at Lake Dunlap in the US. It has nothing to do with India and Pakistan at all. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a video uploaded to the US-based news channel CBS17's YouTube on May 16, 2019. Its description stated that a dam collapsed at Lake Dunlap in Texas, US.
The date of May 14, 2019, can be seen on the upper left side of the surveillance camera's footage. On the other side, the words "Guadalupe-Blanco River Authority" are written. In the viral video, both these are hidden by the on-screen graphics. The bottom right corner of the CBS17 video bears the watermark of "Dunlap_Dam". This part has been cropped out in the viral clip.
We found several May 2019 news reports about this incident, including by CNN and ABC News . Both reports featured the video.
According to these reports, this video is from Texas, where this incident happened in Lake Dunlap on May 14, 2019, due to a spillage failure. Per a report , authorities called this a "partial dam failure." The collapse caused the lake's water level to drop by almost three metres in the following hours. The dam is about 91 years old .
The Guadalupe-Blanco River Authority, a local water conservation authority, cited safety concerns as residents were warned to reduce their water consumption after this incident.
Notably, we did not find any credible news reports of the Kishanganga Dam gates collapsing due to excess water. Thus, it's clear that a 2019 video of a dam gate collapse in the US was falsely shared as India's Kishanganga Dam. - Ends Published By: Anupriya Thakur Published On: May 7, 2025 10:53 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of injured Indian soldiers in J&K? This was made with AI using 18-year-old photo
content:
The viral video has been seemingly created through AI, using a 2007 photo of Indian Army soldiers carrying the body of a rebel in Baramulla.
In the early hours of May 7, the Indian armed forces carried out Operation Sindoor , striking nine terror camps in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and reportedly killing over 80 terrorists. However, at least 15 Indians have also been killed as Pakistan resorted to firing and heavy shelling along the Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir.
Amid this, a video began making the rounds on social media, allegedly showing Indian Army casualties following Operation Sindoor. It showed soldiers carrying a person on a makeshift stretcher .
Sharing the clip on Facebook, one person wrote , "Massive Indian casualties at Indian Army Forward Sanghar Post opposite own Chirikot Sector. The post has been razed to the ground by Pak Army. Remember this is the same post where, on one hand, a white flag was raised, whereas, on the other hand, it was trying to target Pak Army troops."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video has been created using AI on a 2007 photo of Indian army soldiers carrying the body of a rebel in Jammu and Kashmir's Baramulla. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the stock photography website Alamy, which contained a photo of the same soldiers carrying a body on a stretcher. Prima facie, AI tools were used to generate a video using this photo.
According to the information on the website, this photo was uploaded to Alamy on August 2, 2007, and showed Indian Army soldiers carrying the bodies of rebels in Ganthmulla, a village located in Jammu and Kashmir's Baramulla district. The photograph was credited to Altaf Zargar, a photojournalist from Srinagar.
The description of the photo read, "Indian army soldiers carry the body of a rebel in Ganthmulla, 65 km (40 miles) west of Srinagar, the summer capital of Indian Kashmir, 02 August 2007. Eight suspected rebels and two army soldiers, including one officer, were killed in a two-day gun battle near the Line of Control in Uri sector, the army said."
We also found several other photos from the same day, showing Indian Army soldiers carrying the bodies of the rebels in Ganthmulla .
We also spoke to Altaf Zargar, who told India Today Fact Check that he had indeed shot these photos for Zuma Press, a US-based news agency, back in 2007.
It is noteworthy that there's no evidence to suggest that the Indian Army raised a white flag along the LoC in Jammu and Kashmir. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: May 7, 2025 21:03 IST

title: Fact Check: 2019 video of Pak soldiers waving white flag NOW being pushed as Indian troops!
content:
This 2019 video actually shows the opposite. It was the Pakistan Army waving a white flag to retrieve its dead soldiers!
The Indian Army successfully executed Operation Sindoor in the early hours of May 7, hitting nine terrorist infrastructure targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Following the Indian strikes, many Pakistani social media accounts began sharing old videos of Indian plane crashes and mishaps.
They also shared a video allegedly showing Indian soldiers holding white flags in a hilly area, while carrying dead bodies. Those sharing the video claimed Indian troops were retrieving the dead bodies of fellow soldiers from the Line of Control. One such post read: "At the Line of Control, the Indian Army is waving white flags to retrieve the bodies of their dead soldiers".
India Today Fact Check found that this 2019 video shows the Pakistan Army waving a white flag to retrieve their dead soldiers killed by India following ceasefire violations.
A reverse search led us to a longer version of the viral video in an ANI post dated September 14, 2019. It said: "Hajipur Sector: Indian Army killed two Pakistani soldiers in retaliation for unprovoked ceasefire violation by Pakistan. Pakistani soldiers retrieved the bodies of their killed personnel after showing a white flag. (10.9.19/11.9.19)." This made it clear that the viral video is not recent. #WATCH Hajipur Sector: Indian Army killed two Pakistani soldiers in retaliation to unprovoked ceasefire violation by Pakistan. Pakistani soldiers retrieved the bodies of their killed personnel after showing white flag. (10.9.19/11.9.19) pic.twitter.com/1AOnGalNkO — ANI (@ANI) September 14, 2019 Subsequent keyword searches led us to several September 2019 news reports containing the viral video. As per The Times of India , the video shows the Pakistani Army retrieving the dead bodies of two of its soldiers in the Haji Pir sector of Pakistan-occupied Kashmir under the cover of the white flag on September 13, 2019. A Pakistani Soldier, Sepoy Ghulam Rasool of the Pakistan Army, was killed in retaliatory firing by India on the intervening nights of September 10 and 11. Last week at the Hajipur Sector of Pakistan Occupied Kashmir (PoK), Indian troops killed a Pak soldier Sepoy Ghulam Rasool of Bahawalnagar, Punjab in retaliatory firing. In a rare occurrence, Pakistan Army requested for the mortal remains showing white flag. Video: @manishindiatv pic.twitter.com/9BO2nxzMsP — Aditya Raj Kaul (@AdityaRajKaul) September 14, 2019 Several reports suggest that initially, Pakistani soldiers tried to retrieve the body under the cover of intense firing. However, another Pakistani army soldier was killed in the process, forcing them to raise a white flag for a temporary cessation of firing. ANOTHER INDIAN WHITE FLAG VIDEO Another video of a white flag being hoisted at an alleged Indian check post on Chora Complex along the Line of Control was widely shared. Sharing this video, an X user wrote , "India has admitted its first defeat. After an intense night of combat, India has raised the white flag at the Chora complex". advertisement The video featured a tree and a white flag hoisted in a ruined place in a hilly area. We found no concrete evidence that this video was from India at the LoC. It's also not clear if the white object in the video is a flag at all. We did not find any credible Indian or international news reports (except on Pakistani news channels) about the Indian Army waving the white flag anywhere in Jammu and Kashmir along the LoC. Thus, it's clear that the viral claims are misleading. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: May 7, 2025 21:17 IST

title: Panic among Pakistani citizens lays bare how hollow is the Pak govt's brave front
content:
In the second phase of Operation Sindoor, the Indian Army launched a barrage of drone attacks on Lahore, Karachi, and other major cities of Pakistan, striking Pakistan's air defence systems on May 8. Pakistan's government put on a brave face with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif vowing to retaliate and claiming to have downed scores of drones and jets belonging to the Indian Army.
In the run-up to Operation Sindoor, Pakistanis laughed off military action and the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty, making self-deprecating jokes and memes.
We scanned through hundreds of social media posts from X to Facebook to Reddit to gauge the nation's mood right now. What we found betrays the panic behind the government's bravado.
We found that Pakistanis are accusing their own government of misleading them about India's strike near Rawalpindi Stadium.
Indian airstrikes in the last two days have sparked a discussion among Pakistanis on social media, especially Reddit, about stockpiling food , fearing more strikes.
While the Pakistani government claims to give "proportionate" replies and down Indian drones and jets, its citizens discuss the possibility of de-escalation , wondering when all of this will be over.
Citizens of Islamabad, in panic, asked if they should stay put or leave their homes as air raid warning sirens go off.
Expressing anger over Indian drones and rockets reaching major cities, Pakistanis also questioned the efficiency of its defence systems, the neutralising capabilities of which are otherwise boasted by the army.
Going a step further, one Pakistani Reddit user even suggested that Pakistan should move on instead of retaliating against the Indian Army's attacks for the sake of its people.
Another Pakistani citizen went ahead and praised the Indian army for precisely hitting the 22 targets that it had set out to, during Operation Sindoor.
Some citizens also discussed how the Pakistan Army assumed control of several routes, and listed out areas that the citizens must evacuate while carrying essential medications and their Computerised National Identity Cards with them.
Apart from a few districts bordering India, educational institutions across the country are reportedly functioning normally. However, several examinations were cancelled in Lahore , Punjab , and other locations across Pakistan owing to the ongoing tension, which became a talking point .
- Ends Published By: Harshita Das Published On: May 8, 2025 21:02 IST

title: Pak guy mocked Pakistan Army for failing to intercept India's missiles. Now his family's in trouble
content:
India neutralised a wave of missile and drone attacks launched by Pakistan on the night of May 8, targeting key military installations. Having failed once again at destroying Indian military assets, the Pakistani government is now reportedly cracking down on its citizens.
On May 8, a video of a Pakistani man named Aladeen lauding the Indian Army's Operation Sindoor and calling out the failure of Pakistan's defence system went viral on social media. A day later, reports from Pakistan say that the police took strong action against his family.
According to a post shared on May 9 by Sabir Shakir, a journalist at Pakistan's ARY News, the police went after Aladeen's family. They reportedly tortured his brother and vandalised his office. pic.twitter.com/EkhoY9NsRp — Sabir Shakir (@ARYSabirShakir) May 9, 2025
pic.twitter.com/EkhoY9NsRp — Sabir Shakir (@ARYSabirShakir) May 9, 2025
We also found a news report on the Pakistani website Siasat about the incident. It quoted Aladeen saying, "Today, my brother's office was attacked by agencies and police. People came in 4 to 5 vehicles without a warrant. The office was attacked. My two brothers were vandalised and tortured. After beating them, they took them away. Everything in the office was broken, and all the laptops and mobile phones were taken away. My parents have been harassed by the Special Branch Gujrat and the IS office in Kharian Cantt for the past two years." Notably, Gujrat here refers to the city in Pakistan, not the Indian state.
Aladeen's X account lists his location as Germany. Several of his posts questioned Pakistani journalists for letting people die in silence while playing to the tunes of the government.
One such post read: "This is what we are saying: hold the military trial later, pick up Shehr Bano's mother later, threaten my family later. At this time, nothing is more important than Pakistan's defense, survival, and future." https://t.co/pKxfQxJY2d — Aladeen (@Aladeen_Pro) May 8, 2025
https://t.co/pKxfQxJY2d — Aladeen (@Aladeen_Pro) May 8, 2025
Apart from Aladeen, other Pakistanis have also shared videos , calling out the police and authorities for deceiving people and lying about Indian drone attacks.
Due to the prevailing war-like situation between India and Pakistan, we were not able to speak directly to Aladeen. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: May 9, 2025 16:02 IST

title: This is how Pakistan targeted India on the internet
content:
With the announcement of a ceasefire between India and Pakistan, let's look at some of the key items in Pakistan's disinformation campaign in the run-up to the dtente. The campaign provides an insight into what might have been on Pakistan's agenda against India amid its slew of unsuccessful air raids. 1. Sowing discord
Pakistan-based accounts attempted to cause infighting in India through their disinformation campaign. They shared a video of many people gathered on a farm, and claimed that Sikhs in India had turned against the Indian Army in Amritsar.
The video , however, predates the recent India-Pakistan military escalations that began with India's Operation Sindoor on May 7. Of course, India's covert operation was in retaliation against the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack.
The video actually shows a clash between the police and protesters over a biogas plant in Ludhiana's Akhara village on April 26.
According to The Times of India , on April 26, the police resorted to lathi-charging protestors opposing the setting up of a biogas plant in Akhara. Villagers had reportedly been protesting it for over a year, citing health concerns. 2. Fabricating hostages
Pakistan-based accounts overwhelmingly spread lies about an Indian Air Force pilot called Shivangi Singh getting captured across the border.
Of course, that's untrue. For starters, the Press Information Bureau, while referring to a separate video shared with the claim, refuted this outright. It said that an Indian female Air Force pilot "has NOT been captured". Indian Female Air Force pilot has NOT been captured Pro-Pakistan social media handles claim that an Indian Female Air Force pilot, Squadron Leader Shivani Singh, has been captured in Pakistan. #PIBFactCheck This claim is FAKE! #IndiaFightsPropaganda @MIB_India pic.twitter.com/V8zovpSRYk — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) May 10, 2025 Second, the photo shared with the claim is also old. In June 2023, an IAF training jet crashed in Chamarajanagar near Karnataka's Bhogapura village. According to The Hindu , on June 1, 2023, an Indian Air Force trainer aircraft, Kiran, crashed — but not before both its pilots ejected safely. The pilots were identified by the local police as Tejpal and Bhumika. They both sustained some injuries and were taken to Bengaluru for treatment. 3. Fake wins — in video games "Even Bollywood can't deliver such action that the Pakistan Air Force did in real life to India," wrote Pakistan-based accounts , as they shared a video of a fighter jet doing some rather impressive flying. The video does feel like an action film sequence. Because it's most likely from a video game. Clips from the combat simulator ARMA 3 are often mistaken for real incidents — something we have seen in wars , time and again. This video also predates Operation Sindoor and the subsequent skirmishes between India and Pakistan. It was shared by a YouTube account on April 30. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: May 10, 2025 22:00 IST

title: Pak General has been lying blatantly. Here is evidence he can't deny
content:
Pakistani propaganda through proxy accounts to target India is now well-known. However, Pakistan has now taken the disinformation campaign to an entirely new level.
Even during a military conflict, one does not expect a top-ranking army officer in uniform to conduct an official press conference and present doctored clips to prove a point. You don't expect to hear "quotes" that have been manufactured by picking up random parts of a sentence in a manner that distorts its meaning.
But that's exactly what happened on Sunday night, May 11, when Ahmed Shareef Chaudhry, the Director General of the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the Pakistan Armed Forces media wing, addressed the press on its Operation Bunyan Marsoos.
During the presser, he played a clip of Wing Commander Vyomika Singh of the Indian Air Force, who, alongside Colonel Sofiya Qureshi of the Indian Army, became the face of Operation Sindoor. The clip was from a press briefing a day earlier on May 10.
Ahmed Shareef Chaudhry wanted to prove through the press conference that Pakistan only targeted military installations, not civilian areas. However, what he presented as evidence was a video of Vyomika Singh stitched together from various sentences. If you look carefully, you can see several jump-cuts throughout the video. Every time the continuity breaks, there's a jump-cut, suggesting editing.
Here are four instances which make it amply clear how heavily Vyomika Singh's statements were twisted and distorted. Tampering number 1
The Pakistan Army removed the words "civilian areas" from Vyomika Singh's statement to make it look like they attacked only military bases.
They removed the part where Vyomika Singh says the Pakistani attacks were neutralised.
They created a whole new sentence by picking up words from various sentences. They dropped all mention of the Pakistani armed forces targeting civilian areas, Pakistan's disinformation campaign, and targets hit by Indian armed forces.
They chose to omit the part where Vyomika Singh countered Pakistan's claims of destroying Indian airbases in Punjab and Rajasthan.
You can see the original Indian press conference right here . And you can see the Pakistani press conference here . - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: May 12, 2025 17:41 IST

title: Half clips, full lies: How Pak used doctored news videos to push their propaganda
content:
Showing the full story would have revealed the truth. So, the Pakistan Army chose to pick up news reports, including AajTak's, and carved out portions from them to present to the press and the international community. Shockingly, this was done by none other than Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, the Director General of Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).
In a press briefing on May 11, he explained how Operation Bunyan Marsoos met all the objectives set out by Pakistan. As evidence, he showed clips of national and international news reports about cross-border airstrikes by India and Pakistan. However, not only did the Pakistan Army clip these reports to paint a false picture of its military might, but it also omitted parts of the same reports that didn't suit its narrative.
Here are two such news reports that Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry twisted during the press conference: AajTak's news report clipped out of context
Chaudhry showed an AajTak clip , claiming the news anchor stated that Indians were panicking as their armed forces could not protect airbases from Pakistan's airstrikes. The anchor could be heard saying, "There is a visible sense of panic among people because all the airbases appear to be under attack, they look like they're engulfed in flames. The biggest concern being discussed is if you cannot protect your airbases, how will you protect the public?"
The original news report , however, showed quite the opposite. In it, a video shared by the Indian Army showing Pakistani airbases being targeted by India was first shown. The report begins with correspondent Jitendra Bahadur Singh explaining how India attacked Pakistan's launch pads, airbases, and critical military assets, while Pakistan used civilian flights as shields.
The news anchor, Shashi Tushar Sharma, then elaborated on how people in Pakistan were panicking amid these attacks, questioning how Pakistan would save its civilians when it couldn't save its airbases. You can see the original news broadcast below.
Al Jazeera journalist's quote twisted
Another such "evidence" used by the Pakistan Army was a news report by Al Jazeera , in which journalist Umar Mehraj stated that a series of loud explosions were heard across Jammu and Kashmir just after morning prayers on May 10.
In it, Mehraj said: "Just after morning prayers, there was a series of loud explosions heard across Jammu and Kashmir, including Uri, Nagrota, Jammu, Udhampur, as well as major areas of Srinagar and Jammu."
We found an Al Jazeera news report dated May 10, featuring Mehraj's bite. In it, he reported that a series of loud explosions were heard across Jammu and Kashmir, including in Jammu, Nagrota, Uri, and Srinagar. However, right after this, he added that whether these blasts were caused by a Pakistani airstrike or India's air defence systems intercepting the airstrikes remained unclear.
He also added how Pakistani shelling in Jammu Kashmir's Rajouri killed "a senior government official", referring to Additional District Development Commissioner Raj Kumar Thappa. The Pakistan Army, however, omitted these parts completely from the video shown at the presser.
If splicing media reports was not enough, the Pakistan Army also doctored Wing Commander Vyomika Singh's statement from the official Indian Armed Forces press briefing of May 10. A detailed report about it can be read here . - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: May 12, 2025 19:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Arrested and beaten up for saying 'Pak Zindabad' in India? Here's the truth
content:
The viral video shows a gangster's arrest by the Bhopal Police. It has nothing to do with 'Pakistan Zindabad' slogans.
On Saturday, May 10, India and Pakistan agreed to a US-mediated ceasefire. Amid an uneasy detente between the two nations, some took to social media to share a video of injured people in torn clothes being paraded by the police. Allegedly, they were beaten up because they raised "Pakistan Zindabad" slogans.
Sharing this video, an X user wrote , "Traitors supporting Pakistan and raising 'Pakistan Zindabad' slogans serviced and paraded by Bhopal Police."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video shows gangster Zubair Maulana's arrest by the Bhopal Police after he was seen using firearms in a public place.
Reverse-searching key frames from the viral video led us to a news report uploaded to YouTube on May 12. Per the report, notorious gangster Zubair Maulana and three of his associates were arrested by the Bhopal Police. Over 55 criminal cases have been registered against him. He was accused of vandalising vehicles and firing guns in public to create panic in Bhopal. The police recovered illegal firearms and other weapons from them.
We found several news reports about this incident. Per the Free Press Journal , the operation was carried out on May 8, jointly by police teams from Mangalwara, Tila Jamalpura, the Crime Branch, and Hanumanganj. Zubair Maulana had been absconding since October 2024. He was accused of triggering violence and shooting in public places to scare rivals in Bhopal's Mangalwara and Tila Jamalpura areas on May 6. We did not find any mention of Pakistan or "Pakistan Zindabad" slogans in any news report.
To confirm this, we contacted the SHO of Mangalwara police station, Ajay Kumar Soni. Speaking to India Today Fact Check, Soni refuted the viral claim that the police arrested these people for chanting "Pakistan Zindabad". He confirmed that the arrests were made on May 8, because he and his aides started firing guns in public.
Thus, it's clear that this video does not show people beaten up for saying "Pakistan Zindabad" in India. - Ends Published By: Harshita Das Published On: May 12, 2025 22:52 IST

title: Fact Check: International community DID NOT laud Pakistan. So they decide to cook it up
content:
This screenshot is fake. The Daily Telegraph has not published any such report.
In the aftermath of the India-Pakistan ceasefire, Pakistan-based social media accounts began sharing fake screenshots showing international praise for the Pakistani armed forces. These fabricated visuals falsely attribute reports to reputed global media houses like The Daily Telegraph and CNN.
One such screenshot was from the British newspaper, The Daily Telegraph, dubbing the Pakistan Air Force "the undisputed king of skies".
Another viral image was an infographic featuring the CNN logo, claiming India suffered significantly more military losses than Pakistan. It claimed that India lost six jets and 553 drones, while Pakistan lost zero jets and 78 drones. The archives of two such posts can be seen here and here .
India Today Fact Check found that both viral screenshots are fake. The Daily Telegraph and CNN did not publish these. THE DAILY TELEGRAPH
We did not find any Daily Telegraph report praising the Pakistan Air Force. In fact, upon close observation, we found there were many inconsistencies in the viral screenshot. The URL incorrectly said "telegraph.cuk" instead of "telegraph.co.uk". The subhead contained gibberish text.
The screenshot appears to be the front page of The Daily Telegraph edition published on May 10. But its epaper from that date did not feature any such headline.
We checked the official website and social media accounts of CNN but couldn't find any report claiming that India has suffered more losses than Pakistan in the skirmishes.
Desmond Chung, CNN's Asia Pacific director of public relations, told India Today Fact Check over email that CNN did not publish any such infographic.
Thus, it's clear that both screenshots are fake and don't reflect actual news reports and headlines. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: May 12, 2025 22:54 IST

title: Fact Check: Sebastian Stan putting up 'I Told Modi' poster? Nope, this video is edited
content:
