title: Fact Check: NOT Pak Army officer. The man standing in food line is an Indian actor!
content:
The man in the video is not a Pakistani Brigadier. He is an Indian actor named Sachin Sharma, and the video was shot on the sets of a web series about the India-Pakistan conflict.
During his visit to the US earlier this month, Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir reportedly declared that Pakistan, a nuclear nation, would "take half the world down" if faced with an "existential threat" from India.
Now, a video going viral on social media purports to show a man in a Pakistan Army uniform waiting in line for food. Those sharing the clip claimed it was a "Pakistan Army Brigadier Standing in the Food Line Amid Shortage."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the individual in the video is not a Pakistani brigadier. He is an Indian actor named Sachin Sharma, and the footage was shot on the sets of a web series.
Many elements in the viral video raise suspicions. In the video, the person in the Pakistani army uniform claimed to be a brigadier. However, upon closer examination, we noticed that the badge on his uniform showed the rank of lieutenant general.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip on Instagram by an account called Arjun Rao on June 29. The caption of that post did not provide any information about the video. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Arjun Rao (@actorarjunrao) Upon examining the Instagram account more closely, we realised that the man seen alongside the person dressed in a Pakistani Army uniform was Arjun Rao , a professional actor who has worked alongside Bollywood star Akshay Kumar and several other prominent actors in various films. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Arjun Rao (@actorarjunrao) We contacted Rao to inquire about the viral video. He confirmed to us that "the person seen with me in the video is not a Pakistani Brigadier. He's an Indian actor called Sachin Sharma. The video was filmed on the set of a web series focused on the India-Pakistan conflict. And I made this video purely for entertainment purposes and was not intended to hurt anyone." Thus, it is evident that the individual standing in the food line in the viral video is not a Pakistani brigadier but an Indian actor. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Aug 26, 2025 14:19 IST

title: Fact Check: 7 million people in Japan march for Palestine? This clip is AI
content:
This video is AI-generated. While there have been many pro-Palestine protests in Japan, none have been attended by 7 million people.
Aerial footage of a sea of people marching in a coastal city is being widely shared as a recent pro-Palestinian protest in Japan. In the video, people can be seen seemingly holding Palestinian flags and banners.
The video was shared with claims like, "All Israeli Media Shocked! On 20 Aug- 7M Japanese Protest For Palestine." People also shared this video with hashtags like "Gaza" and "Gaza Under Attack".
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is AI-generated. OUR PROBE
In some of the versions of the viral video , we observed the watermark for a TikTok account called @urika.huh.
We checked this account and found the video in question shared by it on August 21 with an AI disclaimer.
It is noteworthy that this account has shared multiple AI-generated videos with similar captions, implying millions of people in Japan, Korea, and China were protesting in support of Palestine.
We also sent the viral video to Deepfakes Analysis Unit, a consortium of Indian fact-checkers and academics debunking synthetic media. They tested the video using the tool WasitAI, which called the clip AI-generated.
PRO-PALESTINE PROTESTS IN JAPAN
There have been many protests in Japan in solidarity with Palestinians in the past few months. On August 18 , people in Tokyo gathered in front of the Prime Minister's office in response to the ongoing famine and genocide in Palestine. They banged pots and dishes and demanded that the Japanese government impose sanctions on Israel.
Visuals of recent pro-Palestine protests in Japan can be viewed in these news reports . Japan is one of the 28 countries which issued a joint statement in July demanding that the war in Gaza end.
Earlier this month, two more AI-generated videos were shared on social media as pro-Palestine protests in Japan. Our fact-check on these videos can be read here . - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Aug 26, 2025 23:20 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral clip of 'world's largest Ganesh idol in Chennai' is NOT real
content:
The viral video is fake and made using AI tools.
Amid Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations, a video of a giant Ganesh idol being built began circulating on social media. Sharing the video, a Facebook user wrote , "The world's largest Ganpati statue in Chennai."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is fake and was made using AI. OUR PROBE
We observed a watermark saying "HooHooCreations80" in the video. We found the account "HooHooCreations80" on Instagram, where the video was shared on August 23. The post's caption read: "Ganesh Chaturthi special." In the comments, several people pointed out that this was an AI-generated video. We also found many other similar AI-generated videos shared by the Instagram account.
In the viral video, the movements of the people involved in the making process look unrealistic and robotic. Additionally, we found several discrepancies on the workers' hands and legs — all telltale signs of AI-generated content. View this post on Instagram A post shared by HooHoo (@hoohoocreations80)
A post shared by HooHoo (@hoohoocreations80)
Additionally, HooHooCreations80's Instagram bio mentions that the account specialises in AI-generated content. Its YouTube channel said that HooHooCreations80 is "the home of unique AI-powered entertainment," adding, "We create fun and entertaining AI videos designed to make you smile, laugh, and feel happy. Our every video is made with one goal – to entertain you and spread joy through AI-powered content."
We also checked this video using the AI-detection tool Hive Moderation. It flagged the video as AI-generated.
Notably, however, a Ganesh idol was made using 7,500 books, including 5,000 copies of the Bhagavad Gita, in the Mannali area of Chennai . But it looks completely different from the idol in the viral video.
All of this proves that the viral clip does not show a real statue. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Aug 27, 2025 20:55 IST

title: First Dog Babu, now Tomy Jaiswal? Story behind the doggy Aadhaar card going viral
content:
Man's best friends are getting there. Slowly, but surely! A couple of months ago, an application was reportedly submitted through the government's Right to Public Services' portal under the name "Dog Babu" using an image of a dog in Bihar's Patna.
And now, in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior, an Aadhaar card was allegedly made for a pooch by the name of "Tomy Jaiswal".
This Aadhaar card, making the rounds online, was complete with an Aadhaar number and featured a photo of an Indie dog along with the name Tomy Jaiswal. The dog's address was listed as the Simiriya Tal area of Gwalior district's Dabra municipality. Tomy, per the Aadhaar card, is under the guardianship of Kailash Jaiswal.
So, did someone create an actual Aadhaar card for a dog? Of course not. Here's the rather tragic story behind this photo. THE NUMBER
We first verified that no actual person's Aadhaar card was photoshopped to create Tomy's ID. When we entered the listed UID number, 070001051580, on the official Aadhaar website, we received the message, "Please enter a valid Aadhaar number." This clearly indicates that the Aadhaar number is fake.
AajTak's Gwalior correspondent, Sarvesh Purohit, spoke to locals in Dabra and informed us that the fake Aadhaar number was created by adding zeros on both sides of a phone number. According to Truecaller, this number belongs to one Pawan Jaiswal from Madhya Pradesh.
When we called this number, a woman named Mamta Jaiswal answered. She revealed that the number belonged to her only son, Pawan, who died five months ago following a sudden illness. Pawan used to work at a liquor shop. She also said that her husband's name is Kailash Jaiswal, who runs a small grocery store.
Mamta told India Today Fact Check that the address mentioned on the card was indeed hers. And the dog in the photo was their pet of 10-12 years, who died two years ago.
"We are considering filing a police complaint about this, because this controversy is causing us a lot of trouble," Mamta told India Today Fact Check. "We are not even educated enough to make our own Aadhaar card. How could we edit and create an Aadhaar card for a dog?"
Gwalior District Collector Ruchika Chauhan told India Today Fact Check that the Aadhaar card was fake. She said that an investigation was underway to determine who created it, who made it viral, and what their motive was. - Ends Published By: Prateek Chakraborty Published On: Sep 2, 2025 19:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Not Pak minor with her newborn child! Video of Vietnam sisters VIRAL with nasty claim
content:
This video is from Vietnam. It shows a premature newborn lying on the stomach of her older sister.
A video of a young girl lying on a hospital bed with a newborn resting on her stomach has been widely shared online with a disturbing claim: that it shows a 12-year-old Pakistani girl who had just given birth.
An X user shared the video with the caption: "Islam is a Cult Religion. How sad. A shocking case has emerged in Pakistan where an 11-year-old girl. Married to 60 year 60-year-old man and when she's 12 born a baby...! Really Islam is s*xual child abuse religion..!" Its archive can be viewed here .
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video is not from Pakistan but from Vietnam. It shows a young girl lying on a hospital bed with her baby sister, who was born prematurely.
Many on social media pointed out that the language being spoken in the video was Vietnamese, hinting that the clip was likely from Vietnam.
A reverse search of the video's keyframes led us to the TikTok account @kenhkhuyenmai, which had shared the viral video on June 21 with the Vietnamese caption: "The older sister kept her premature baby sister warm so that the mother could rest a bit."
A subsequent keyword search led us to a Spanish-language video from July by Instagram user Aguirre Felicitos. Translating the video through NotebookLM, we found that he was addressing misinformation surrounding the video. People at the time had claimed that an eight-year-old Thai girl had been impregnated by her stepfather. He stated that the mother of both children in the video was a woman named Bo Ngc. He has also shared a screenshot of Bo's TikTok account: @baongoc._.93.
On this TikTok account, we found that she had posted the video in question on August 9, 2024. Its Vietnamese caption read, "The older sister weighs 700g and the younger sister weighs 900g. Mom's two lovely angels. The two have grown up now and understand their mother very well."
The post confirms that Bo is the mother of the girl and the newborn child. In the post, she also tagged a hospital located in Tan An city in Vietnam's Long An province.
She also shared several videos with her daughters where they can be seen wearing the same clothes from the viral video. And on August 11, 2024, she even shared a video clarifying that the video featured her two daughters. Her TikTok bio also mentions that she is a mother of two premature children who shares tips about their care.
Thus, it's clear that a video from Vietnam was shared with false claims.
(With inputs from Sanjana Saxena) - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Sep 3, 2025 15:16 IST

title: Fact Check: Stash of dollars unearthed in viral clip has NO LINKS to Punjab floods
content:
The viral video is not from Punjab. It's staged and predates the recent floods in the state.
Unrelenting floods in Punjab have hit more than 1,400 villages across the state, affecting over three lakh people. At least 37 people have died so far, forcing authorities to declare Punjab a disaster-affected state.
Amid hundreds of videos of the deluge and rescue efforts being shared on social media, one showed a person uncovering a stash of US dollars buried under leaves and dirt. In the video's voiceover, a person in Punjabi says this incident was from the Punjab floods.
Sharing this video, an X user wrote , "Punjab: A family kept a large amount of US dollars buried in their land. After the floods, all these US dollars got spoiled."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is staged, not from Punjab, and predates the recent floods. OUR PROBE
Below the viral post , several people pointed out that the video was not from Punjab and predated the recent floods. Reverse-searching the video's keyframes led us to a longer version of the same video posted to a TikTok account named Galaxy Restore (@ifound504) on July 29. The video was titled: "A pile of dollars. 690000$." The location mentioned in the post was Los Angeles in the US. In it, a woman could be heard speaking in English. This means the viral clip's audio was manipulated.
We also found other similar videos on the same TikTok account, in which money, expensive phones, and jewellery can often be seen being dug out. This appears to be the main gimmick of the account — staging videos of valuable items being unearthed.
Interestingly, the account's YouTube channel mentions its location as Singapore. We also found several videos similar to the viral clip on their YouTube channel. In the channel's bio, we found a link to its Facebook . There, the location mentioned was neither Los Angeles nor Singapore, but Chiang Mai, Thailand.
We found no recent credible news reports of a family burying a stash of US dollars in its land in Punjab. Thus, it is clear that the viral video has been shared with completely false claims. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Sep 4, 2025 03:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Electric piya? No, this video DOES NOT show jilted lover cutting village power line
content:
This story is baseless. The man in the video is Anwar Hussain, an electrician who was simply replacing faulty wires with new ones in Assam.
Did a man disrupt the electricity of an entire village after his girlfriend ignored his call? This bizarre story has gone viral on social media along with a video of a young man cutting wires with a pair of pliers atop an electric pole.
An Instagram user shared the video and wrote: "Youth cuts off electricity to entire village after girlfriend ignores his phone call." Its archive can be viewed here .
Some claimed this happened in Bihar while others said it was from Uttar Pradesh . Some even called it the "Saiyaara effect", referring to the Mohit Suri movie that recently became popular among Gen-Z audiences.
India Today Fact Check found that the story being shared with this video is totally baseless. The man seen in the video is an electrician named Anwar Hussain who was replacing old wires with new ones in Assam's Baksa district.
News outlets like ABP News , News-18 , and Mint did stories on the viral claim, believing it to be real. Aaj Tak also did a story, but later retracted it. Our Probe
A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes led us to a YouTube channel named "Technical Work", where the video was shared on July 17 with hashtags like "electrician" and "lineman".
We noticed that the YouTube channel, Technical Work, regularly posts videos related to electrical repair work. In many of the videos , technicians can be seen working atop electrical poles. In others, electricians can be seen repairing electrical transformers.
We contacted Jahidul Islam, the person operating the YouTube channel. He told India Today Fact Check that the person in the viral video is his friend Anwar and that the video was shot in the Nikashi village of Assam's Baksa district.
He said, "This video was shot in June when Anwar was replacing old wires with new ones. It is unfortunate that it somehow went viral with the fake girlfriend story." He explained that he and his electrician friends are contract workers with Assam Power Distribution Limited.
Jahidul shared Anwar's photo and a photo of his group of electrician friends with India Today.
We also spoke to Saquib, another friend of Anwar. He told us that Anwar was extremely depressed because of this controversy, and his marriage is on the verge of breaking up. Saquib also shared a video with us in which Anwar and two of his friends can be seen refuting the viral claim.
Thus, it's clear that a video of an electrician at work is being falsely shared with a fake story. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Sep 4, 2025 14:01 IST

title: Fact Check: Did people beat up a BJP MLA in Bihar? This video is from Bengal
content:
This video is from Jalpaiguri, West Bengal. On October 6, BJP MP Khagen Murmu and MLA Shankar Ghosh's convoy was attacked by an angry mob.
Ahead of the Bihar Assembly elections, a video of people attacking a car with a Bharatiya Janata Party sticker has been widely shared. In the video , a uniformed security person can be seen trying to safely escort the vehicle while an angry mob throws shoes, slippers, and stones. Those sharing the video claimed it was a recent incident from Bihar, where public anger erupted against a BJP MLA.
India Today Fact Check found that this video is not from Bihar, but from Jalpaiguri in West Bengal. OUR PROBE
Reverse-searching the video's keyframes led us to a Facebook user's profile , who had shared this video on October 10 with the caption, "People threw stones at Bengal's BJP PMLA Shankar Ghosh's car. If you are not happy with a politician, show him your strength by the injury of the vote. Attack on the BJP leader in the presence of security is condemnable."
The video featured the watermark of a news channel called RNF News. On this outlet's YouTube channel, we found the video uploaded on October 9.
Its description stated that this video of an attack on a BJP MP occurred in the Nagarakata area of Jalpaiguri on October 6. Comparing frames from the viral video and this YouTube video clearly shows they are from the same incident.
On October 6, the channel uploaded another video of the incident. Its description stated that amid floods in North Bengal, when BJP MP Khagen Murmu and MLA Shankar Ghosh went to the area for relief work, some people attacked them. Heavy rains in early October caused floods and landslides in Darjeeling and Jalpaiguri, resulting in at least 40 deaths so far.
Several news outlets reported this incident, including Amar Ujala , Live Hindustan , and Jagran . The Tribune also uploaded a video of the attack on its YouTube channel.
According to these reports, after the attack, BJP leader Amit Malviya accused the Trinamool Congress of orchestrating it. Both Khagen Murmu and Shankar Ghosh were admitted to the hospital. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee also visited Murmu in the hospital. Later, the Calcutta High Court sought a report from the West Bengal government about the attack.
Thus, it's clear that this video from West Bengal is being shared falsely as being from Bihar ahead of elections in the state. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Oct 16, 2025 15:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Patna metro GOAT-ed? Let's slaughter this viral claim
content:
This video has nothing to do with the Patna metro. It is from the Samastipur railway station in Bihar.
Reel-makers inconveniencing passengers and walls stained by guthka or chewing tobacco spit stains, the newly inaugurated Patna metro has already grabbed headlines for the wrong reasons. And now a video going viral shows a woman taking two goats with her on an escalator, allegedly at a Patna metro station.
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the video has nothing to do with the Patna metro. It is from the Samastipur railway station in Bihar.
Using Google Lens, we found that an Instagram user had shared the viral video on July 5. This proves that the video predates the inauguration of the Patna metro on October 6. The person also wrote in the caption that the video was from Samastipur railway station.
Using this as a clue, we checked videos and photos of Samastipur Junction railway station online and found the same place on a platform where the escalator seen in the viral video is installed. The same location can also be seen in YouTube vlogs about Samastipur Junction. Comparing these videos and images with the viral video confirms that the latter is from Samastipur.
Recently, a video from a Gurgaon metro station was falsely shared with the claim that people entered the Patna metro without tickets by sneaking under the turnstile. India Today also fact-checked this claim, which can be read here .
Thus, it is clear that the claim about the viral video is false. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Oct 16, 2025 21:24 IST

title: Fact Check: Kohli DID NOT sign a Pak flag - it was an RCB jersey!
content:
Ahead of India's three-match one-day international series against Australia, the Indian cricket team landed in Perth on October 16. The focus is on Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma, who have rejoined the India squad after a brief break from the game.
A picture now going viral shows Kohli signing a Pakistani flag for a fan. Some applauded this gesture as a symbol of sportsmanship amid India-Pakistan tensions, while others criticised it. A Facebook user wrote , "Virat Kohli giving autographs to a Pakistani in Perth, Australia."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral picture is edited. Kohli was actually signing a Royal Challengers Bengaluru jersey for a Pakistani fan in Perth.
Many people pointed out that the picture had been edited. An X user wrote , "It was an RCB shirt, not Pakistani, but the guy is from Karachi, Pakistan."
Reverse-searching the viral photo led us to an X post from October 16 that contained the same photo, but it showed Kohli signing a Royal Challengers Bengaluru jersey — not a Pakistani flag. Virat Kohli RCB pic.twitter.com/VM8zMGF0W3 — RCBIANS OFFICIAL (@RcbianOfficial) October 16, 2025
Virat Kohli RCB pic.twitter.com/VM8zMGF0W3 — RCBIANS OFFICIAL (@RcbianOfficial) October 16, 2025
Using a keyword search, we found a video of the incident shared on X by the account RevSportz Global on October 16. The video's caption reads: "A lucky fan of Virat Kohli from Karachi got his RCB jersey signed by the star batsman." A lucky fan of Virat Kohli from Karachi got his RCB jersey signed by the star batter. @rohitjuglan @ThumsUpOfficial #ViratKohli #TeamIndia #AUSvsIND #CricketFans pic.twitter.com/gujRTYbwee — RevSportz Global (@RevSportzGlobal) October 16, 2025 In the video, Kohli was loading his luggage onto a bus when a fan asked him for an autograph on his RCB jersey. Kohli signed the jersey and then walked away. The viral photo was captured during this time. Reportedly , Kohli was leaving for the training session scheduled for October 16, when he walked up to the fan to sign the jersey. The same fan also got Rohit Sharma to sign an Indian jersey. At the video's end, he introduced himself as Sahil from Karachi, Pakistan. He also displayed both autographed jerseys. He described himself as a Virat Kohli fan and wished him good luck for the upcoming matches against Australia. At no point in the video was the Pakistani flag visible. We did not find any credible news reports about Virat Kohli signing a Pakistani flag during the Australia tour. Thus, it is clear that the viral photo is doctored. Kohli was, in fact, signing an RCB jersey. - Ends Published By: Prateek Chakraborty Published On: Oct 17, 2025 22:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Mamata Banerjee cook Kali Puja bhog without the gas on?
content:
The viral video is AI-generated. In the actual video, the West Bengal CM can be seen cooking with the stove lit.
During Kali Puja, Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee organised the customary Shyama Puja at her residence — something she does every year. A video , now going viral, purports to show the CM cooking the puja's bhog without the stove's fire on.
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is AI-generated. OUR PROBE
Upon closely examining the roughly six-second-long viral video, we noticed many inconsistencies that are telltale signs of AI manipulation. In the first second, the utensil is seen filled with cooked bhog. However, by the end of the video, it appears half-empty.
News outlets like The Wall published videos showing the chief minister cooking bhog at her residence with a lit stove. Additionally, the official Facebook page of the All India Trinamool Congress also posted a video and photos of her cooking bhog, which clearly shows the stove lit.
Notably, the first frame of the viral video matches a photo posted in a Facebook album shared by the All India Trinamool Congress. Comparing them shows that the viral video was created using AI from this image.
We also analysed the viral video using AI verification tools like Hive Moderation, which confirmed that it was AI-generated.
In conclusion, the viral claim that Mamata Banerjee was cooking without fire is false. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Oct 21, 2025 17:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Here's how a communal twist is being given to the Jaisalmer bus fire
content:
Many Muslims were among the dead. While the bus belonged to KK Travels, owned by a man called Turab Ali, the owner of Jain Travels also owns the company that built the bus's body.
On October 14, a private air-conditioned sleeper bus travelling from Jaisalmer to Jodhpur caught fire just before it reached its destination. The death toll has now reportedly reached 26. The tragedy has now become the subject of a conspiracy theory, this being a Muslim plot to kill Hindus.
People shared an article from a newspaper called Dainik Navjyoti about the tragedy. Text in the image prominently stated: "In the Jaisalmer accident, the owner of Jain Travels' bus, Turab Ali, and driver Shaukat were arrested." This clipping was shared with captions like, "Seems to be a part of a new version of there [sic] J.i.h@d to k.i.l.l as many as possible k.a.f.i.r.s that too disguised under hindu or jain named businesses."
India Today Fact Check found that many Muslims were among the dead. The bus belonged to KK Travels, not Jain Travels. That being said, the owner was indeed a man called Turab Ali. Jain Travels is a different company, and its owner owns the company that built the bus's body.
We reviewed the e-paper of Dainik Navjyoti for October 15 regarding the incident from October 14, which made it clear that the line at the top of the photo, "In the Jaisalmer accident, the owner of Jain Travels' bus, Turab Ali, and driver Shaukat arrested," was added separately. Its font did not match that of the Dainik Navjyoti. The news item also did not state that the bus belonged to Jain Travels.
On October 16, the Jaisalmer Police issued a press release via their X account regarding the incident, which said that the AC sleeper bus belonged to KK Travels. The owner's name was Turab Ali, and the driver's name was Shaukat Khan. It also mentioned that an investigation was ongoing regarding the role of Manish Jain, the owner of the company that built the bus's body. , , @PoliceRajasthan @Igp_Jodhpur pic.twitter.com/w4riCiEYcH — Jaisalmer Police (@JaisalmerPolice) October 15, 2025 According to a Dainik Bhaskar report from October 18, Manish Jain was arrested in Jodhpur, whose company, Jainam Coach Crafts, built the bus's body. The same Manish Jain also runs a company named Jain Travels. According to reports , several safety standards were ignored during the bus's construction. Following the incident, the Transport Department seized 66 buses manufactured by Jainam Coach Crafts. Several Muslims among the deceased A Dainik Bhaskar report from October 18 listed the names and photos of the deceased. It included 14 Hindus and nine Muslims. Jaisalmer Superintendent of Police Abhishek Shivhare also told India Today Fact Check that a significant number of Muslims, along with Hindus, died in this incident. Why was 'Jain Travels' written on the bus? In some video reports related to the incident, "jaintravels.com" can be seen written on the back of the bus. However, most of the bus was burnt, making it impossible to figure out what was written on it. We reviewed some videos of KK Travels buses on social media, where "KK Travels" was written on the front windscreen and sides. According to reports , the bus had a separately installed AC and only one exit door, which got jammed after a short circuit. SP Abhishek Shivhare said, "The bus had 'Jain Travels' written on it because its body was made by a company owned by Manish Jain, who also owns Jain Travels." advertisement (With inputs from Vimal Bhatia) - Ends Published By: Sonali Verma Published On: Oct 22, 2025 22:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Police beating up woman in India? No, this video is staged
content:
This is not a real incident but a staged video. The people in it are acting.
A video going viral on social media purports to show police brutality in India. In the clip , a man in a police uniform can be seen grabbing a woman by the hair and punching her. Allegedly, the video was leaked footage from a police station.
India Today Fact Check found that this was not a real incident but a staged video. The individuals seen in it are acting. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story OUR PROBE Using Google Lens, we found a similar clip on an Instagram page called Haunted Guru Ji. According to its bio, this page is managed by another Instagram account, belonging to a person named Arjun Singh . Taking a look at Arjun Singh's profile makes it clear that he's a content creator.
Using Google Lens, we found a similar clip on an Instagram page called Haunted Guru Ji. According to its bio, this page is managed by another Instagram account, belonging to a person named Arjun Singh . Taking a look at Arjun Singh's profile makes it clear that he's a content creator.
The bio also included a link to a YouTube channel named Haunted Guru Ji. The longer version of the viral video was uploaded on this channel on September 6. The nearly 16-minute-long video, whose Hindi title translates roughly to: "Tankrit comes to devour the body of a sacrificed minor before the final rites." The viral segment appears at 7 minutes 45 seconds .
The video description includes a clear disclaimer stating that it was made for entertainment and awareness about paranormal activities. The video also confirms that the person shown being beaten was a man, not a woman.
This channel has several other fake police videos similar to the viral one.
In short, a staged video is being misrepresented online. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Oct 24, 2025 14:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video of Indian driver cooking inside truck before California crash is AI!
content:
The first clip of the viral video is AI-generated. The second one is the original footage of the crash that took place on October 21 in California.
Jashanpreet Singh, an Indian-origin Sikh man in the US, was arrested in Ontario, California, after he allegedly rammed his semi-truck into multiple vehicles, killing three and injuring others on October 21.
Reportedly, the 21-year-old truck driver was under the influence of drugs while driving. A video now going viral also purports to show Jashanpreet cooking in the truck right before the crash took place. The video shows a Sikh man driving a vehicle on a multi-lane highway while cooking curry in a pan. It then cuts to dashcam footage of a vehicle ramming into other cars.
Sharing the video on Instagram, one person wrote , "Illegal immigrant truck driver caught cooking curry at 90 mph before crash kills 3 on California highway".
But India Today Fact Check found that the first clip of the viral video is AI-generated. The second one is the original footage of the crash in question.
Multiple pieces of evidence prove that the video of the Sikh man cooking while driving is AI-generated.
1. The video contains the watermark of an X account "Vox_Oculi", which shared the video on October 23, and captioned it: "WILD FOOTAGE: A second dash cam video reveals illegal immigrant truck driver cooking curry at 90 mph before killing 3 in California highway crash." The account's bio features the words "satire" and "AI Wizard" in it. We also found that the account had shared many AI-generated videos .
2. The video also has many visual inconsistencies, like the reflection in the side view mirror of the vehicle remaining static, despite the vehicle moving steadily. The stirring ladle seen in the video is also unusual. And in one of the frames, we can see the ladle get distorted. Apart from this, a passing by car appears to have only a single unpartitioned window spanning across the front and back seats.
3. The face of the driver seen in the video doesn't match that of the accused, Jashanpreet Singh. A comparison can be seen below.
4. The US-based fact-checking organisation Lead Stories also debunked the viral claim. Attributing the California Highway Patrol Police, the news outlet wrote that the footage was not released by the law enforcement agency, and it was not related to the crash.
However, as per Lead Stories, the second clip (dash cam video) was released by the CHP, and it was indeed from the crash. Many news organisations also used it in their reports .
Hence, we concluded that the viral claim is false. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Oct 27, 2025 19:36 IST

title: Fact Check: Deadly pollution in Indian waters? This video is from Guatemala
content:
This video, dated June 2022, is not from India but from Guatemala.
A video of a beach completely covered in garbage is circulating on social media. Many shared the video of mounds of plastic waste floating on the water and claimed it was from India.
One such post was captioned: "You pay carbon taxes, sky-high energy bills, banned plastic straws, and carry useless paper bags that tear instantly. All to 'save the environment'. Meanwhile, in India..."
India Today Fact Check found that this three-year-old video is from Guatemala — not India!
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a June 2022 post by CBS News featuring the same video. Its caption said, "Mounds of plastic waste lapped onto the Caribbean shores of Guatemala from the Rio Motagua, considered one of the most polluted rivers in the world, according to environmentalists." Mounds of plastic waste lapped onto the Caribbean shores of Guatemala from the Rio Motagua, considered one of the most polluted rivers in the world, according to environmentalists. pic.twitter.com/3igEb1ozvN — CBS News (@CBSNews) June 22, 2022
Mounds of plastic waste lapped onto the Caribbean shores of Guatemala from the Rio Motagua, considered one of the most polluted rivers in the world, according to environmentalists. pic.twitter.com/3igEb1ozvN — CBS News (@CBSNews) June 22, 2022
A subsequent search led us to a Reuters report from June 9, 2022, featuring several other visuals of the Rio Motagua, where heaps of plastic waste were photographed. According to the report, the river that runs from the edge of the country's capital, Guatemala City, out to the Caribbean Sea, was getting choked with plastic waste. The reason behind this waste was a tributary of the Rio Matogua, named Rio Las Vacas.
The UK-based Telegraph , in its report from July 22 this year, noted that the tributary Rio Las Vacas, once ideal for fishing, was now the most plastic-polluted river in the world, accounting for two per cent of the global total of river-derived plastic waste that enters the oceans. Presently, 20,000 tonnes of plastic flow through the Rio Motagua into the Caribbean Sea every year.
An August 2024 report from CNN , however, noted that a US-based startup named 4Ocean has begun a mission to eradicate plastic from Motagua.
Thus, it is clear that the viral video is completely unrelated to India. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Oct 28, 2025 16:47 IST

title: Fact Check: BJP leader garlanded with shoes ahead of Bihar polls? No, this video is OLD

title: Fact Check: Used condoms found in Delhi girls' hostel drain? These claims are garbage
content:
This video is AI-generated. There are no recent reports of condoms being found in the drainage system of a Delhi girls' hostel.
Two videos allegedly showing the drainage system of a women's hostel in Delhi being found clogged by used condoms have gone viral.
The first video shows news reporters zooming their cameras on used condoms floating in a drain. A reporter says, "As you can see, this is the sewage chamber of the hostel. Yesterday, when the cleaning staff opened the cover of this sewage drain, a huge number of used condoms were revealed. These were found near the girls' hostel."
The second video also shows many used condoms inside and scattered near a drain. A Facebook user posted this video with the caption, "Shock in Delhi PG Hostel as thousands of used condoms were found during drainage cleaning. Locals have dubbed it the 'Condom Nala Scandal', raising serious hygiene and safety concerns." The archive of one such post can be viewed here .
News outlets like NDTV Marathi , the Orissa Post , and Sakal featured the second video in their reports, claiming it was from Delhi.
India Today Fact Check, however, found that while the first video is AI-generated, the second one is from Nigeria.
Let us talk about these videos one by one. AI-generated video
In the first video, we observed the logo "VN Creator". We found that it was originally shared by a Facebook page of the same name on October 27. We noticed that in this video, the "VN Creator" logo was used to hide the watermark of Sora, Open AI's video generation tool.
This page had also shared a video allegedly showing used condoms found in a Pune girls' and boys' hostel. In this video, the Sora watermark can be seen very clearly.
Thus, it's evident that this video is not real at all. Nigeria, not New Delhi
A quick reverse search of the second video's keyframes led us to a Facebook post , which mentioned that it was from Nigeria.
We then found that a Nigerian social media influencer had posted a longer version of this video on October 13 on Instagram. He mentioned in his post that this video was from Nigeria. In this version, one can hear a voiceover featuring the word "Nigeria" at least once. Nigerian news outlet Edo Online Television had also shared this video on October 13 with the caption: "#Nigeria".
Thus, it's clear that two unrelated videos are being shared as visuals from a women's hostel in New Delhi. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Oct 29, 2025 19:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Photos of a Bangladeshi actress shared with a fake 'love jihad' twist
content:
This story is bogus. The woman is Bangladeshi actress Jouty Islam. The video is part of a shoot, and the image is from a film poster.
Two photos are going viral on social media with the claim that a Hindu woman named Nandini Mandal, who allegedly converted to Islam after marrying her Muslim boyfriend Abdul Adil Khan, was later assaulted and thrown out by him.
The first image shows a man in a checkered shirt and a woman in a sari. The text on the image labels them as "Muslim" and "Hindu" respectively. The second image shows a woman with a burnt face , claimed to be the same person after the alleged assault. The archive of one such post can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that this story is entirely fabricated. While the second photo of the woman with the burnt face is from a shoot, the first one is a film poster. OUR PROBE
A quick reverse search of the image of the woman with the burnt face led us to an October 21 Facebook post by the Bangladeshi actress Jouty Islam. The post features a video showing her with burn marks, clearly a makeup effect. The second image in the viral post was taken from this video only.
In the post, Jouty Islam mentioned the word "shooting" in the caption and in reply to a comment, she clarified that this video was part of a shooting sequence. Responding to another comment, she said that the name of this film was "Ami Nusrat Bolchi". We looked further and found the first image of the viral post on her Instagram account . It is quite clear that this is actually a poster of a movie whose Bangla language title translates to "Widow Wife". We could not find any recent reports about a converted Muslim woman called Zara Islam being tortured by her husband. To sum up, images of a Bangladeshi actress are being falsely shared with a communal angle. - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Oct 31, 2025 16:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Illegal Bangladeshis protesting SIR in West Bengal? This isn't India at all
content:
This video from September 15 actually shows locals protesting in Bangladesh's Faridpur district against constituency demarcation.
Following the announcement of Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls in West Bengal ahead of Assembly elections, many illegal Bangladeshi migrants were reportedly arrested trying to cross the border out of India. Now, a video of hundreds of protesters on a road, with sticks and brooms in their hands, has gone viral on social media.
Those sharing this video claimed illegal Bangladeshi and Rohingya migrants are now protesting against the SIR in West Bengal. Captions of such posts read, "See how they have come out against SIR (Special Intensive Revision of Voters' List) in West Bengal. Illegal Bangladeshis and Rohingyas must be deported."
India Today Fact Check has found that the video is not from India at all. It is from the Faridpur district of Bangladesh and shows locals protesting against constituency demarcation.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip dated September 15, posted by a Facebook user named Biplob Biplob, who's profile lists his location as Faridpur, Bangladesh. The Bangla caption of this post translates to, "Video clip from today's protest."
This makes it evident that the video is unrelated to SIR in West Bengal, as the Election Commission announced the revision exercise on October 27 in West Bengal and 12 other states and Union Territories.
India Today Fact Check reached out to Biplob, who confirmed that the video is from the Bhanga area of Faridpur district in Bangladesh. He mentioned that a series of protests took place in the Bhanga upazila against the Election Commission's decision on constituency demarcation.
We also found several reports published in Bangladeshi outlets like The Business Standard , The Daily Star , and The Dhaka Tribune in September that said the Election Commission of Bangladesh issued a gazette notification redrawing the boundaries of 46 constituencies across the country. This decision led to widespread protests in several districts.
According to Biplob, "This decision has hurt the livelihood of the locals as the distance to the nearest administrative office has now become nearly 40 km. For the time being, we have paused our protest as a case has been registered against this demarcation in court."
Therefore, it is abundantly clear that the video is not from India and not related to the SIR in West Bengal. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 7, 2025 18:33 IST

title: Fact Check: No extra marks for attending PM rally. This Uttarakhand uni notice is FAKE
content:
This notice is doctored; no such circular was issued by the university.
Ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Uttarakhand on November 9 for the silver jubilee celebrations marking the state's formation, a notice allegedly issued by the Dev Bhoomi Uttarakhand University has gone viral. According to it, the university has directed a section of its students to participate in the prime minister's rally, promising 50 internal marks to them in return. The notice says that the event would be considered under the Bharatiya Gyan Parampara component.
Noted Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan shared a photo of the notice on X, writing, "Dev Bhumi Uttarakhand University to award 50 marks for attending Modi's rally! And how many for shouting Modi Modi?" Its archive can be viewed here .
India Today Fact Check found that this notice was forged. The university has confirmed that no such notice has been issued. OUR PROBE
A closer inspection of the viral notice immediately raises several red flags. First, the notice did not feature a date of issue, a common practice for university circulars. Further, the absence of an official signature, stamp, or seal strongly suggests that it was fake.
Next, we searched for recent circulars on the official website of the Dev Bhoomi Uttarakhand University and found a Diwali Holiday notice issued on September 22, which, unlike the viral circular, contained all the necessary official seals and dates.
A comparison between these two makes it evident that the viral one is not authentic.
Aman Bansal, the vice chairman of the University, confirmed to India Today Fact Check that the viral notice was forged. He also said that the university was in the process of filing an FIR with the police. Bansal also shared a copy of the written complaint sent to the police, which can be seen below.
The official Facebook page of the Dev Bhoomi Uttarakhand University also shared a post on the evening of November 8, publicly denouncing the notice as fake.
Thus, it's clear that the university in Uttarakhand had issued no such notice at all. - Ends With inputs from Ankit Sharma, Uttarakhand Published By: Akshat Trivedi Published On: Nov 9, 2025 01:33 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Brazilian hairdresser Larissa Nery call Rahul Gandhi a 'failed politician'?
content:
This translation of Nery's video, where she is speaking in Portuguese, is completely false. She made no mention of any politician or party in her video.
Larissa Nery, a Brazilian hairdresser, has been making headlines in India after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi pointed out at a presser that her photograph was used in alleged election fraud in Haryana. The Leader of Opposition showed that Nery's face featured on 22 voter ID cards with different names and addresses.
A video now going viral purports to show Nery addressing her newfound celebrity in India — while also taking a dig at Rahul Gandhi. In the video, she can be heard speaking in Portuguese, and many who shared it provided a translation of her words: "There's this failed politician that lost nearly 100 elections in India, using my old pics to amplify his lies and propaganda against the ruling party."
India Today Fact Check found that while the video does show Larissa Nery talking about her sudden fame in India, this translation is false. At no point does she make any remarks about Rahul Gandhi, the Congress party, or the Bharatiya Janata Party.
We used myriad tools, like Happyscribe, Evernote, Cockatoo, Google Translate, Turboscribe, Grok, and translate.mom, to transcribe and translate the video. The transcription provided by Happyscribe is given below:
" Gente, vou contar pra vocs uma fofoca — vocs vo rir demais. Esto usando uma foto minha, antiga. Minha foto velha, t? T novinha na foto, devia ter uns 18, 20 anos. Esto usando essa foto pra fazer, eu no sei se eleio, alguma coisa que tem que votar na ndia! Esto me colocando como indiana pra dar golpe nos outros, gente. Olha que loucura! Que doideira essa que a gente t vivendo?
A um repórter me chamou querendo saber sobre esse trem. Ligou l no salo do meu emprego querendo conversar comigo pra uma entrevista. Eu no respondi, falei pra Tata no passar meu nmero e tal. O cara achou meu Instagram e me chamou por l. Agora, uma outra pessoa que no tem nada a ver com o assunto — uma amiga minha de outra cidade — me manda uma foto. Vou colocar aqui pra vocs verem. Vocs no vo acreditar, gente! "
The same tool, Happyscribe, translated this to English:
" Guys, I'm going to tell you some gossip — you're going to laugh so much. No, really, I'm going to spill the tea. People are using an old photo of me. It's an old photo, okay? Look, I look super young in it — like 20, 18 years old. They're using my photo for, I don't know, an election or something you have to vote on. And in India. They're saying I'm Indian to scam people, guys. Look how crazy that is. What kind of madness are we living in?
Then a reporter reached out wanting to know about this thing. He called the salon where I work, wanting to talk to me for an interview, but I didn't respond. I told Tata not to give out my number and all that. The guy found my Instagram and messaged me there. Now someone else who has nothing to do with it — a friend of mine from another city — sends me a photo. I'm going to put it here for you, down below so you can see. Here. You won't believe it. Oh, guys. "
Translations provided by the other aforementioned tools were more or less consistent with this.
Besides, we also found many recent news reports about Larissa Nery. The hairdresser spoke to various news outlets and none of them featured her opinions about Indian parties and leaders. In fact, in speaking to The Print and The BBC , she only expressed surprise at how things unfolded. An NDTV report about Nery's video also features a translation that is consistent with the translations we got using various tools.
In another video , she added, "I have absolutely nothing to do with politics in India. My photo was purchased from a stock image platform and used without my involvement. It's not me. I've never even been to India. I'm a Brazilian digital influencer and a hairdresser, and I love the Indian people."
Thus, it's clear that the translation of Nery's video calling Rahul Gandhi a "failed politician" is trumped-up. She said no such thing.
(Written by Aryama Bhattacharjee) - Ends Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Nov 10, 2025 13:12 IST

title: EXCLUSIVE: Delhi blast prime suspect Umar Nabi was fired for patient's death in J&K
content:
A devastating blast on the busy street in front of the iconic Red Fort reverberated not just throughout the national capital but the entire country. Everyone, in its aftermath, was glued to their mobile or TV screens, anxiously waiting to find out who was the person driving the white Hyundai i20 that exploded.
Then, various news channels flashed the photo of Dr Umar Un Nabi, believed to be the man behind the steering wheel, whose body was also blown to pieces in the explosion. Investigative agencies have already nabbed members of Nabi's family in Kashmir and collected DNA samples. These will be matched against the DNA found at the scene of the carnage to confirm the driver's identity.
A fashionable buzz-cut, neatly trimmed beard, and transparent-framed glasses. Many who saw this photo of Dr Umar Nabi couldn't wrap their heads around the fact that he — a doctor, a man who was supposed to save lives — had scarred New Delhi, and killed at least 10 in the process.
Back in Kashmir, however, a retired medical professor watching the news was not very surprised, even if he was disheartened. He had already glimpsed something in Nabi that the world would eventually come to see.
Professor Dr Ghulam Jeelani Romshoo was among the four people who recommended terminating Nabi's employment at the Government Medical College in Anantnag.
The reason was the death of a patient.
This incident dates back to 2023. Nabi, at the time, was working as a senior resident (SR) at the Government Medical College after getting his MBBS and MD degrees from Srinagar. He came to Anantnag for a three-year residency programme, where Dr Jeelani was his superior in the general medicine department.
But Nabi proved to be a bad hire.
Complaints against him began piling up from the get-go. Fellow doctors, paramedical staff, and even patients alleged that Dr Umar Nabi was not just rude and inattentive but also often absent from the hospital.
This contradicts what Dr Nabi's sister-in-law, Muzamila, told reporters after the November 10 Delhi blast. According to her, he had always been an introvert who would mostly remain locked in his room, studying. #WATCH | Pulwama, J&K: Muzamila, sister-in-law of Dr Umar Un Nabi - a suspect in the blast near Red Fort yesterday, says, "They (security forces) have picked up my husband, brother-in-law and mother-in-law. They asked us about the whereabouts of Umar. We said he is in Delhi. Then pic.twitter.com/Ee7Vy4ZkQY — ANI (@ANI) November 11, 2025
#WATCH | Pulwama, J&K: Muzamila, sister-in-law of Dr Umar Un Nabi - a suspect in the blast near Red Fort yesterday, says, "They (security forces) have picked up my husband, brother-in-law and mother-in-law. They asked us about the whereabouts of Umar. We said he is in Delhi. Then pic.twitter.com/Ee7Vy4ZkQY — ANI (@ANI) November 11, 2025
But Dr Jeelani told India Today Fact Check that Nabi's negligence cost a patient at the government hospital their life.
The patient, who was in critical condition, was under Nabi's charge. But one day, the doctor, instead of tending to them, disappeared from duty. Meanwhile, the patient's condition worsened. A junior doctor present there tried to save him, but failed. The patient died.
The patient's family lodged a complaint against Nabi with the hospital's medical superintendent. Subsequently, a committee of four senior doctors was formed to investigate the matter, which included Dr Jeelani.
This committee also included three other senior doctors from the Government Medical College in Anantnag: Dr Muhammad Iqbal (the college's medical superintendent), Dr Mumtaz Ud Din Wani (professor of general surgery), and Dr Sanjeet Singh Risam (head of the dentistry department). India Today Fact Check reached out to them as well, and all three refused to give any further details on the matter.
According to Dr Jeelani, Nabi flatly denied being absent from his post. But when the hospital checked the CCTV footage from the day, his lie was immediately exposed. What was most surprising, Dr Jeelani said, was that even after being summoned several times during the investigation, Nabi did not appear before the committee to make his case. Finally, the committee recommended his termination, and he was subsequently fired.
According to reports, after his expulsion from the hospital in Anantnag, Dr Umar Un Nabi joined the Al-Falah School of Medical Science in Faridabad in 2023. When this doctor went from a caregiver to becoming an accessory to a terror attack, only further investigations will reveal. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 11, 2025 20:16 IST

title: From Jamia to jail: Chancellor of terror-tainted Al-Falah has a shady past
content:
"Al-Falah" is Arabic for success, prosperity, and well-being. It was an apt name for a medical college in Faridabad. And then the November 10 Delhi blast happened.
The Al-Falah School of Medical Sciences welcomed its debut batch of aspiring doctors just six years ago in 2019. Since then, it has turned into a sprawling campus, buzzing with students, teachers, and other staff.
The founder of Al-Falah University (of which the medical college is a part) is Jawad Ahmad Siddiqui. A former lecturer, Siddiqui is now the director and founder of approximately a dozen ventures under the Al-Falah Group of Companies umbrella. Needless to say, he did well for himself. And the thousands of students studying at his university, especially the would-be doctors, thought they would too.
But the explosion outside the Red Fort in New Delhi, which killed at least 12 people and injured many more, has not only thrust the Al-Falah Group into the spotlight for all the wrong reasons, but it has also tainted the reputation of the university beyond repair. And by extension, anyone involved with it.
Had his university not been in the news for being the hub of the terrorists who allegedly executed the Delhi blast — and who were planning something much more sinister — chancellor and founder Jawad Ahmad Siddiqui would have been planning his birthday party at his plush mansion, called Al-Falah House, in Jamia Nagar.
Sixty-one-year-old Jawad was born on November 15, 1964, as one of three sons to Hammad Ahmad Siddiqui. He grew up in Mhow, Madhya Pradesh, the birthplace of Bhimrao Ambedkar, after whom the town has now been renamed.
According to his (non-active) LinkedIn profile , Jawad Ahmad Siddiqui completed BTech in Industrial and Product Design from Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya in Indore. Later, his family moved to Delhi. Big dreams and shortcuts
According to a former colleague who spoke to India Today Fact Check on the condition of anonymity, Jawad became a Mechanical Engineering lecturer at Jamia Millia Islamia in 1993. But his ambitions far exceeded the humble podium of a college.
While working at Jamia, he dabbled in business and formed a few small companies with his brother Saood. Among these was Al-Falah Investments, which would eventually send them both to Tihar Jail for three years!
While at Jamia, Jawad persuaded some of his colleagues to invest in his business venture, promising hefty returns. However, he quickly became embroiled in a flurry of fraud, embezzlement, and cheating allegations. In 2000, a man called KR Singh lodged an FIR (No.43/2000) in Delhi's New Friends Colony against Al Falah Investments Ltd. The case was investigated by the Economic Offence Wing of the Crime Branch in Delhi. Jawad was arrested and subsequently languished in jail for over three years with his brother.
Rejecting his bail application in March 2003, the Delhi High Court noted that, in line with the allegations, the Forensic Science Laboratory in Delhi found that the "signatures of the investors were forged. The deposits were also received in the name of some of the companies which were non-existent. The petitioners diverted large funds received from the investors into their personal accounts and then misappropriated the same".
Jawad ultimately made bail in February 2004 and was later acquitted in the case by the Patiala Court in 2005, but only after he and his brother agreed to refund the investors they had defrauded. Faridabad college becomes 'mini-Kashmir'
According to reliable sources, who did not want to be quoted, the Al-Falah School of Medical Sciences had a decent start back in 2019. But gradually, the college began hiring many doctors from Kashmir, primarily because they were cheap. Already a minority university, the environment on the campus became more and more orthodox following this. The management was apprised of the situation. It chose to ignore it.
According to the same source, Dr Shaheen Saeed, who was arrested the day after the Delhi blast and has been linked to a terror module, was often seen persuading her colleagues and students into becoming more devout Muslims and wearing more conservative clothes like hijabs and burqas. In fact, she was even cautioned against such activities. More trouble at Al-Falah
During the Covid-19 pandemic, nurses at Al-Falah alleged that they were fired when they demanded life insurance for working in a high-risk environment. Last year, medical interns were suspended when they protested the college's poor infrastructure and the non-payment of stipends.
Jawad may have been able to weather these storms. But the arrest of several doctors working at his medical college on terror charges has put his institution under the harshest of scanners, that of the NIA.
Jawad's birthday is just three days away. But the noose of a terror investigation is already tightening around him. The chancellor of Al-Falah may not be able to have a blast this year. - Ends Published By: Harshita Das Published On: Nov 12, 2025 21:59 IST

title: Fact Check: Is Pak Army mobilising troops after Delhi terror attack? Viral video is OLD
content:
While it's likely from Pakistan, this video has been online since as early as April, and is therefore not related to the terror attack in Delhi.
The Centre assured Indians on November 12 that the perpetrators and sponsors of the terror attack near the Red Fort would be brought to justice swiftly. According to news reports, Pakistan-based outfits Jaish-e-Mohammad and Ansar Ghazwat-ul-Hind may be linked to the terror module that was nabbed in Faridabad the morning of the attack.
Now, a five-second-long video of a train carrying military tanks is being widely shared online. Allegedly, it shows the Pakistan army mobilising its troops from Balochistan to the Indian border, fearing retaliation from India.
Sharing the video on X, one user wrote, "Fearing Indian retaliation after the Delhi Blast, Pakistan Army is moving troops, Arms and ammunition from Balochistan to the Indian border. With PoK, Balochistan will also get freedom."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the video clip has been online since as early as April, and is therefore not related to the terror attack in Delhi. OUR PROBE
Reverse-searching a screenshot from the video led us to the same clip shared on TikTok . We checked the date of upload, which said April 26 this year. This proves that the video far precedes the November 10 terror attack in Delhi.
We then reviewed the profile "mrbeast66" that shared the video on TikTok. On the account, we found several posts geotagged to United King, Karachi, a bakery shop in Karachi's Badar Commercial Street.
Additionally, the video of the train shared by "mrbeast66" includes hashtags like "pak fooj zindabad" and "pakistan zindabad". Based on these details, it's likely that this video is from Pakistan.
That being said, we were unable to determine the exact location of the video, or where the train's destination was. Notably, however, April 25 was right in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack. India would go on to retaliate against Pakistan with Operation Sindoor in May.
Thus, it is evident that while the video of the train carrying military tanks is likely from Pakistan, it predates the Delhi terror attack by several months — making the two things unrelated.

title: Fact Check: Protest in Bihar against 'vote chori'? No, this video is from Gujarat
content:
This video from November 15 from Gujarat's Netrang town shows AAP MLA Chaitar Vasava leading a rally on the occasion of Birsa Munda's birth anniversary.

Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a similar video on Instagram , dated November 15. This video's Gujarati-language caption translates to, "Chaitar Vasava is a different kind of fun."
