title: Fact Check: This video of poll panel chief Gyanesh Kumar, Amit Shah is AI-generated
content:
This video is not real. It has been created with the help of Artificial Intelligence.
After the Bihar Assembly elections, several opposition parties, including the Congress, have raised questions over the impartiality of the Election Commission. A video now going viral purports to show Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar bowing at the feet of Home Minister Amit Shah.
One Facebook user wrote in Hindi alongside the viral video: "The Election Commission at the feet! Those who want to know why such results came in the Bihar elections can watch this video and understand the truth. In this video, the supreme sycophant, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, is seen kissing the feet of his master. Earlier, this gentleman was also his personal secretary. Those who are supposed to protect democracy while holding constitutional posts in India are brutally murdering democracy."
India Today Fact Check found that this video was created with the help of AI tools — it's not real. OUR PROBE
We observed several anomalies in the video. For example, when Gyanesh Kumar drapes the shawl over Amit Shah, the other end of the shawl automatically reaches down to Amit Shah's hand on its own. Also, both of them hold each other's hands for an unnaturally long time.
When we reverse-searched the keyframes of the video, we found an identical photo on the website of Content Garden . In it, Gyanesh Kumar can be seen draping a shawl over Amit Shah's shoulders. According to the information given there, this photo was from 2023 when Gyanesh Kumar was serving as Secretary in the Ministry of Cooperation.
On November 8, 2023, a national symposium was held in New Delhi to promote organic products. In the programme organised by National Cooperative Organics Limited, Gyanesh Kumar honoured Home Minister Amit Shah. According to a PIB press release , Amit Shah was the chief guest at this event.
We found the video of this programme on the YouTube channel of Krishi Jagran Business . At the beginning of the video, Gyanesh Kumar can be seen honouring Home Minister Shah by draping a shawl and presenting a bouquet. But he does not bow in front of the Home Minister in the manner shown in the viral video. Clearly, this portion of the video was created using AI.
We also tested the video with an AI detection tool. According to WasItAI, this video was generated using AI.
Thus, it's clear that the viral video is not real! - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Nov 18, 2025 17:54 IST

title: Fact Check: Bangladesh road rage video FALSELY shared as attack on Yunus press sec
content:
The video does not show Muhammaed Yunus's deputy press secretary. It's a road rage incident, likely from Dhaka.
On November 17, former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by the International Crimes Tribunal. Hasina, who is currently exiled in India, was found guilty of crimes against humanity for allowing lethal force that prosecutors claim resulted in over 1,400 protester deaths. She has vehemently denied the accusations, labelling the trial as "biased and politically motivated."
Amid all this, a video allegedly showing the deputy press secretary to Bangladesh's Chief Advisor Muhammad Yunus getting attacked in the middle of the road has gone viral.
Responding to such posts, many commented on how law and order were rapidly collapsing in Dhaka following the death sentence.
India Today Fact Check found, however, that the video has been online since as early as September 2025, and the person in the video is not Yunus's deputy press secretary.
A reverse image search led us to a longer version of the footage uploaded by the news organisation News Now Bangla on October 15. We also found another clip of the incident shared on September 30. All of this proves that this video predates Sheikh Hasina's death sentence.
In the video, we noticed a Bangladeshi number plate on one of the cars, indicating that the video was indeed from the country.
When we compared the face of the man in the car being attacked with bothdeputy press secretaries to Yunus in Bangladesh, Apurba Jahangir and Azad Majumdar. The comparison given below makes it clear that neither secretary is in the viral video.
Further, had Jahangir been publicly attacked, it would have made the national news in Bangladesh. We found no credible news reports about any such incident.
India Today Fact Check reached out to the assistant press secretary to Muhammad Yunus, Nayem Ali, who confirmed no such incident has occurred and that the man in the video was not affiliated to Yunus's press office.
A Dhaka-based news organisation named, The Dissent, also debunked this claim . It reported that the deputy press secretary was not assaulted and noted that this was just a road-rage incident from the Gulshan area of Dhaka.
Thus, it is evident that the viral claim is patently false. - Ends By Aryama Bhattacharjee Published By: Vivek Published On: Nov 20, 2025 20:29 IST

title: Fact Check: Illegal immigrants rush to Sealdah station post SIR? Here are the facts
content:
The video is indeed from Sealdah Station, but it has nothing to do with SIR. It, in fact, predates the announcement of SIR in West Bengal.
Since the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls commenced in West Bengal, illegal immigrants have reportedly begun leaving the state for Bangladesh. A video now going viral on social media purports to show a massive crowd of Rohingya passengers rushing at the Sealdah railway station in West Bengal.
One X user shared the video and wrote: "SIR comes to Bengal. Rohingyas run from Bengal. Sealdah railway station".
India Today Fact Check found that the video is indeed from Sealdah station, but it has nothing to do with SIR. Also, it predates the announcement of SIR in West Bengal. OUR PROBE
With the help of Google Lens, we found the same video in a Facebook post from October 15. It is to be noted that the Election Commission of India announced the second phase of the SIR in 12 states and Union Territories, including West Bengal, on October 27. So, the viral video cannot be linked to the ongoing SIR drive in the state.
The Facebook user who uploaded the video on October 15, Tofick Khan, wrote in the caption that a ruckus erupted at Sealdah Station as two children fell during a heavy rush of passengers from two trains. Apart from this, we found that he had also shared a clarification video about the viral claim on November 5. As per Khan, he had come to Sealdah Station from Lalgola on October 15. When he arrived, he found that another train had been announced on the same line.
Apart from this, we found that he had also shared a clarification video about the viral claim on November 5. As per Khan, he had come to Sealdah Station from Lalgola on October 15. When he arrived, he found that another train had been announced on the same line.
The announcement caused panic among the passengers, who started rushing out quickly from the train. Because of this, some children fell on the platform. Khan recorded the whole incident and shared the video on social media.
We compared the Lalgola–Sealdah passenger train's scheduled arrival time at Sealdah station with the time displayed on the platform clock in the viral video. The clock shows 16.19, or 4.19 pm, at the moment when the video was being recorded.
The Lalgola–Sealdah passenger train is scheduled to reach Sealdah at around 4 pm. However, it gets delayed sometimes. Also, a train leaves Sealdah for Lalgola at 4.10 pm.
It is possible that the small time margin between the trains and routine delays could create panic among the passengers. This provides validity to Khan's version of events.
Notably, since the announcement of the SIR drive in West Bengal, there has reportedly been a surge of undocumented immigrants leaving the state for Bangladesh. This video, however, does not show that. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 22, 2025 13:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video DOES NOT show illegals running away from WB amid SIR drive
content:
The viral video actually shows a Shyama Puja immersion procession from October 30 in West Bengal's Foonkotla.
As West Bengal undergoes the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, social media has been flooded with alarming claims. A video going viral right now purports to show undocumented Bangladeshi immigrants fleeing India because of the SIR drive in West Bengal.
Several people , who shared this video, shared the clip with captions like, "BREAKING | Movement at Indo–Bangladesh Border," and "A rush of Bangladeshis is heading back after SIR orders were issued in West Bengal ."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video shows the Shyama Puja immersion in West Bengal's Foonkotla. It is not related to the SIR drive at all.
Upon reverse searching, we found the profile of a woman who appeared in the same crowd. On her Facebook page, she had posted a live video on October 30 , captioned: "Foonkotla Shyama Maa farewell", referring to the immersion procession of Shyama Puja/Kaali Puja in Foonkotla, a West Bengal village near the Indo-Bangladesh border.
While comparing her Facebook Live video with the viral clip, we found the same people were visible in both videos. The background matched, including the barbed-wire fencing. The setting confirmed that the video was indeed from the West Bengal-Bangladesh border belt. Another 7-minute-52-second-long video ( https://www.facebook.com/reel/ 3867361026895047 ) posted by the same user from the same date and location shows people carrying a Kali idol for immersion, further establishing that this was a festival procession and not linked to the SIR drive. Most importantly, the video is from October 30, before the SIR process began in West Bengal on November 4. Hence, it cannot be connected to the ongoing SIR. SIR IN BENGAL Even though the video is unrelated, the ongoing situation in West Bengal explains why many were quick to connect the two. India Today's ground report found that many illegal immigrants, who had entered India illegally years ago and managed to obtain Aadhaar and voter ID cards, are now seeking to return to Bangladesh amid the SIR operation. advertisement Reportedly, since July, 200–300 people have been reaching the border daily to return to Bangladesh. Officials link this steady outflow to the ongoing voter list revision. So, while the viral video does not show the exodus of illegal immigrants in West Bengal, this is something that has been happening in the state for some time, which has now intensified since the SIR exercise began. - Ends (Written by Rashmi Gupta, with inputs from Riddhish Dutta) Published By: sharangee Published On: Nov 22, 2025 15:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Loot on the streets of UP? This video is actually AI-generated
content:
Neither is this video from Uttar Pradesh, nor does it show a real incident. It's AI-generated.
A video that's going viral on social media allegedly shows people in Uttar Pradesh looting money from the streets after a truck full of cash overturned on a highway. In the video, we can see a broken-down, overturned vehicle in a street littered with cash, and people rushing to grab it.
The video was shared with captions like: "Cash started flying on the road after a truck full of cash overturned on the highway of Uttar Pradesh. Seeing this, about 500 people gathered on the spot and looted the notes."
India Today Fact Check found out that neither is the video from UP, nor did such an incident occur recently. This video is AI-generated.
If such an incident had actually happened, it would have been in the news. However, we found no credible news reports about it from either Uttar Pradesh or the rest of India.
When we had a closer look at the video, we found some telltale clues that indicate it's an AI-generated video. One, the video has a smooth, glossy texture that's typical of synthetic media. Two, the limbs and faces of people in the crowd appeared distorted in many instances. Third, an autorickshaw visible in the video was misshapen and also did not have a door on its side at all. These clues and many others hinted at the video being AI-generated.
On reverse-searching keyframes from the video, we found it was shared by an Instagram account named Arshad Arsh Edits. Its caption clearly states that this video is AI-generated, created for entertainment purposes. The account features numerous other AI-generated videos, and its bio also mentions "Animations Memes & AI Video Editor".
We also examined the video using an AI-detection tool. Hive Moderation indicated a 99 per cent likelihood that this video was created using AI.
Therefore, it's clear that the video does not show a real incident at all. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Nov 25, 2025 21:15 IST

title: Fact Check: This clip DOES NOT show student dying after 100 sit-ups as punishment
content:
This video does not show the Maharashtra student who died after a 100 sit-up punishment. It shows an eight-year-old who suffered a cardiac arrest and died on January 10 in Ahmedabad. No news reports about this incident mention corporal punishment as a cause.
In Maharashtra's Vasai, a 13-year-old schoolgirl reportedly died after being subjected to corporal punishment for being late. The class VI student was allegedly made to do 100 sit-ups as punishment for arriving late on November 8.
The student, Anshika Gaud — though news reports have also used the name Kajal Gaud — was reportedly suffering from a pre-existing medical condition, experienced difficulty in breathing later that day, and was hospitalised. She died on November 14.
A video now going viral shows a schoolgirl collapsing onto a bench in a school corridor. Those sharing the clip claimed that this eight-year-old collapsed and died after being punished with 100 sit-ups for arriving late to school. A Facebook user shared the video and wrote, "8 Years Old Died Due to Cardiac Arrest After 100 Sit-ups Punishment in School."
India Today Fact Check India Today Fact Check found that while this video does show an eight-year-old dying because of cardiac arrest, it has nothing to do with corporal punishment. Here's what we found: OUR PROBE
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to the same video shared by an X account on January 10. The Gujarati caption stated that an eight-year-old student named Gargi Ranpara died after experiencing chest pain at Zebar School in Ahmedabad's Thaltej. This makes it evident that the video is not recent and has nothing to do with the death of the 13-year-old schoolgirl from Vasai. 8 ! | 8 . 8 . . pic.twitter.com/KLRudt3qhx — Sagar Patoliya (@kathiyawadiii) January 10, 2025 We found several news reports about this incident, which said that the girl, Gargi Ranpara, died after collapsing at Zebar School for Children in Thaltej, Ahmedabad, on January 10. Gargi, a third-grader, became unwell shortly after arriving and slumped on a bench in the school corridor. Teachers quickly rushed her to Asarwa Civil Hospital. Sharmistha Sinha, the principal of the school, stated, "The girl had no prior health issues. Doctors informed us that Gargi had suffered a cardiac arrest. They attempted to revive her and placed her on a ventilator support, but unfortunately, she did not survive." Atul Tiwari, the Ahmedabad correspondent for India Today, who covered the story , confirmed the information, stating, "On the morning of January 10, Gargi Ranpara climbed the stairs to school and suffered a cardiac arrest. This incident is unrelated to the 100 sit-ups or any other punishment administered by the school teachers." According to a January 11 Times of India report, hospital authorities informed the police after Gargi's death. The police thereafter launched an investigation and sent her body for postmortem examination to determine the exact cause of her death. Bodakdev police inspector Apurva Patel said a case of accidental death had been lodged. advertisement We did not find any news reports about what a medical examiner's post-mortem report found. It is, however, evident that the viral video has nothing to do with the student who died after doing 100 sit-ups as punishment. - Ends Published By: Shipra Parashar Published On: Nov 26, 2025 15:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Lawrence Bishnoi just get bail? No, this is an old video
content:
The video is from 2020 and shows Bishnoi being presented before the court in Fazilka. He is still lodged at Sabarmati Central Jail in Ahmedabad.
A video going viral on social media allegedly shows gangster Lawrence Bishnoi being released on bail. The video shows the gangster being escorted by police officers.
In the video, the location was identified as Fazilka, a district in Punjab where Bishnoi was born. A reporter in the video asks Bishnoi how he felt, to which he responds in Hindi, "It feels great. Hopefully, all other cases turn out like this one."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from 2020. Bishnoi hasn't been granted bail.
We did not find any credible news reports about Lawrence Bishnoi being granted bail. He is currently imprisoned in Sabarmati Central Jail in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. According to an Indian Express report, the Ministry of Home Affairs renewed its order in August this year to restrict his movement for another year.
A reverse image search led us to a longer version of the video, uploaded to YouTube by RB Live Media on February 24, 2020.
According to the information provided by RB Live Media, the video is from the same day when Bishnoi was produced in the Fazilka court in Punjab. This was in connection with an attempted murder case under Section 307 of the Indian Penal Code. He was acquitted on that charge.
Recently, the Bishnoi gang returned to the headlines when, on November 19, Anmol Bishnoi , Lawrence's younger brother, was brought back from the United States of America to India and handed over to the National Investigation Agency.
Anmol is wanted in connection with the killing of Nationalist Congress Party leader Baba Siddique, a shooting at actor Salman Khan's residence, and the murder of Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala, among other charges. He has been absconding since 2022.
Therefore, we can conclude that the video being shared does not show Lawrence Bishnoi being granted bail.

title: Fact Check: UP wedding ruckus viral as RSS attack on Catholic school in Telangana
content:
This video actually shows a crowd looting snacks and other food items at a mass wedding in Hamirpur, UP.
A video of a large crowd creating a ruckus is making the rounds on social media. In it, people can be seen rushing hither and thither, hurling cartons. Those sharing the video claimed that it was from Telangana, where Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh workers attacked a Catholic school.
Sharing the video on X, one person wrote , "After attacking Muslims, RSS extremists have now turned their violence towards Christians. At St. Mother Teresa Catholic School in Mancherial, Telangana, they attacked the principal, Fr. Raimon Joseph, and forcibly marked his forehead with a tilak. This is not Gandhi's India."
India Today Fact Check found that the video actually shows a crowd looting snacks and other food items at a wedding in Uttar Pradesh's Hamirpur.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip shared by Jist News on Instagram on November 27. Its caption noted that at a mass wedding in Uttar Pradesh's Hamirpur, chaos ensued when people rushed toward the snack counters after the ceremonies, leading to a stampede-like situation. Several people reportedly fell and were injured. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jist (@jist.news)
A post shared by Jist (@jist.news)
We found several news reports about the incident. According to an Indian Express report, it was a government-sponsored mass wedding held on November 25 at the playground of Swami Brahmanand Vidyalaya in Rath town. Guests rushed to grab snacks and looted boxes of chips and other food items.
Moreover, we found no credible news reports of any recent attack on a Catholic school in Telangana. However, in April 2024, a school in Telangana was attacked over a saffron clothing dispute. As per a report by the Indian Express , a missionary-run school in the Mancherial district was attacked by a group of villagers after students dressed in saffron religious clothing were reportedly informed that their parents needed prior approval for them to attend school without the standard uniform.

title: Fact Check: Did goons attack fish markets in Bengal? No, this video is from Delhi
content:
The video is from the Gokulpuri area in New Delhi where a Hindu group threatened vendors for selling meat and fish close to a temple.
A video is being widely shared online with claims that it shows a tense scene of a group of men threatening a local fish seller and other meat shop owners in West Bengal.
In the video, one man starts vandalising a fish vendor's shop, threatening: "No meat should be visible around." The video was shared with captions like: "Shocking: Reportedly, a group of goons entered a fish market in Bengal and vandalised several local fish shops. So now they want to stop Bengalis from eating fish too?"
India Today Fact Check found that the incident happened in the Gokulpuri area of Delhi on November 27.
A reverse image search of the video's keyframes led to a longer video on Instagram, which identified the location and date. The video was captioned: "Hindu nationalist supporters forcibly evicted meat sellers and shut down their shops, citing the presence of a nearby temple." The location was listed as Delhi's Gokulpuri, and the date was November 27.
A closer look at the footage revealed "Gokulpuri" clearly visible on several walls, confirming the incident's location.
In the comments of this video, we also observed that many had tagged the account of one Rahul Pachauri, the man allegedly behind these attacks.
We checked his Instagram account (@hindu_52_07), and found the viral video shared on November 28 with the caption: "There was news coming from Gokulpuri area that meat trading was taking place within 30 metres of the temple by Hindu and Muslim traders despite previously being warned by the police. Hindu youths banded together and warned the meat traders that if they want to do this in future, do it at a distance from the temple. If someone is found doing business around the temple, legal action will be taken against them."
We found another video shared by the account the same day, captioned, "Meat trade was going on in Gokulpuri. Today, a warning has been given openly that meat trade will be removed from the temple soon. Otherwise, police action will be taken." In the video, Pachauri asserted that they were enforcing a specific rule: that meat vendors must maintain a distance of at least 500 metres from any religious place. Failure to do so would result in police action.
The man in the viral video threatening the fish vendor can be seen in this video, standing behind Pachauri. We found his Instagram account, which stated that his name is Aakash Pandat .
We reached out to Rahul Pachauri to verify the details of the incident. He confirmed to India Today Fact Check that it took place on November 27, between 6 and 7 pm. He claimed he was falsely accused of specifically targeting Muslim-owned shops. According to him, he had no animosity towards Muslims. His concern, he said, was that meat shops should not operate near a temple.
He added that he and his companions, who were detained by the police, have since been released.
Notably, we also did not find any credible news reports of meat traders being harassed in West Bengal recently. Thus, it is clear that the viral video has been shared with misleading claims.
(Written by Aryama Bhattacharjee) - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 1, 2025 17:08 IST

title: Privacy nightmare: Your personal data is now out in the open — just a click away
content:
A massive Indian data leak appears to have become publicly available. A website called ProxyEarth.org now lets you search for anyone's personal information by just entering their phone number!
The website has a sleek, easy-to-use user interface. All you have to do is input an Indian mobile number. The website says it works only for numbers starting with 6, 7, 8, or 9.
When you enter the mobile number, the site appears to run commands and then triangulate the location on a map. It even seems to show the network strength of the number at that location.
The website also shows your name, address, father's name, an alternate mobile number, the name of your cellular service, email address, and either an Aadhaar, voter ID, PAN, or a driving licence number.
As many people are flagging it on social media tagging the government, it is possible that the site might be blocked. What you should worry about
The other data, when available, is largely accurate, if not up to date. The data available on the website appears to be information provided at the time of buying a SIM card: name, father's name, home address, alternate number, and ID proof.
There may be a silver lining for some people here. The data appears outdated in many cases. In several instances, we found old addresses and even old network carriers (which may have been ported to new carriers since). This indicates that the data is most likely old and from when one parched the SIM card. What not to worry about
The website does not track live locations. Nor does it show the number bars your device has. These features are there to add more credibility to it.
The live location was wrong in every instance we checked, where we knew the person's current location.
The network strength gives the impression of live tracking. But the "good" or "bad" rating alongside it likely indicates how much data is part of the leak. This means a "good" rating is bad news. And vice versa.
One can also see a "Live" logo in the upper right corner of the screen. This is also an embellishment to add to the website's credibility for "live tracking" and is misleading. What is ProxyEarth.org?
According to WhoIs, a tool that tells you details about any site's registration, the website was created on October 17 this year. Recent data breaches
As of now, it appears that this might not be a new data breach. Rather, someone has likely compiled data from older breaches — already available for sale on the dark web — in an easy-to-use interface.
In January 2024, personal data, including the names of mobile users, their phone numbers, residential addresses, Aadhaar details, and names of family members of nearly 75 crore Indians, were reported to be put up for sale online. And in 2023, an American cybersecurity company said that personally identifiable information of 81.5 crore Indian citizens, including Aadhaar numbers and passport details, was being sold on the dark web for $80,000.
To check if your personal data has been part of an existing leak, search for your email address on haveibeenpwned.com . It is advisable not to run ProxyEarth.org on your mobile device, as we do not know who is behind this website and what their motives are. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 1, 2025 20:42 IST

title: 'Not doing anything wrong': Meet the man who's making your private data public
content:
On December 1, we published a report about a website called ProxyEarth.org that allows you to fetch the personal data (address, ID proof, alternate numbers, etc.) of Indians using only phone numbers.
While the website had not been blocked in India at the time of writing this, in the aftermath of our report, it began running at a reduced capacity, often with glitches. Nevertheless, we decided to dig deeper.
India Today Fact Check's investigation led us to a man who identifies himself as Rakesh, one of the key persons behind ProxyEarth.org. While this might not be his real name, we will henceforth refer to him as such for convenience.
Under the pretext of purchasing leaked data in bulk for marketing, we spoke to Rakesh at length. And among other things, Rakesh said he had done no wrong in creating this website.
Rakesh has a fairly wide but anonymous presence online. But we managed to connect his many accounts thanks to a common element: his profile photo, which is an anime-style portrait of a young man wearing a plaid shirt and featuring the Indian flag and the logos of CapCut and Adobe After Effects.
We found Instagram, X, and YouTube accounts featuring the same photo. All of these accounts share more or less the same type of content: hacks for pirating premium video editing apps, sending bulk messages, temporary OTPs, live webcams, etc.
We were still looking for a face when we found the Threads account connected to his Instagram. It had a different profile photo — not exactly a real face, but something close. It appears to be a heavily edited version of a real person's face, with the same After Effects logo in the back. We aren't sure if this is actually Rakesh.
Upon examining the source code (backend) of the website, we found mention of a Telegram channel called "@uploadfileofficial". On that channel, we found the link to another Telegram channel called "@rakeshxofficial".
On "@rakeshxofficial", he identified himself as an editor and a programmer. Both channels had the same profile photos mentioned earlier.
While investigating the web of multiple social media accounts, websites, and Telegram channels, we found a phone number. We then called this number on the pretext of buying a package of leaked data.
Rakesh believed us and asked for details about the kind of data we wanted. During this conversation, he said that he worked with a team of 10–12 people, who had together created the ProxyEarth.org website. He said that this was only one of their many projects.
Rakesh also claimed that he was from Bihar, from a town bordering Eastern Uttar Pradesh. This matched with his number's TrueCaller information.
Rakesh said that he was not doing anything wrong. He told us that he was not responsible for any of the data breaches — he was only using existing data leaks to power the website. He said that he had only merged multiple such databases for this website.
We found that whenever you enter a mobile number on the website, it initiates an API call to connect with leaked databases at the backend. As we mentioned in our previous story , there have been reports of several major leaks related to Indians in the last couple of years. Why did he do this?
For Rakesh, the opportunity to access people's personal data was just a bait. He wanted people to explore his other ventures, which are his actual source of income.
As mentioned above, Rakesh advertises hacks for pirating premium video editing apps, live webcams, and other services on his social media. He told India Today Fact Check, "I am using this website as a platform to attract traffic and to advertise my other products."
When we pointed out that the Department of Telecom may soon block his website, Rakesh said calmly that creating a replica with a different domain name would not be difficult at all. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 2, 2025 22:10 IST

title: Fact Check: Muslim man kills Hindu live-in partner? Delhi murder case falsely given communal angle
content:
This incident from Delhi has no communal angle. Virendra Singh killed his live‑in partner, Radha, after they had a heated argument over drinking.
A Muslim man allegedly killed his Hindu live-in partner, stuffed her body in his car, and was on his way to dispose of it when the police caught him at a checkpoint. This allegation has been widely shared online alongside a Hindi TV9 Bharatvarsh headline that reads: "In Delhi, man murders live-in partner, stores her body in a car and goes to sleep."
The headline was shared with captions like, "My Abdul is different... Abdul has committed another crime. He killed his loving partner, a Hindu girl, in Delhi and was taking her body into his car to dispose of it... On the way, his car was caught during police checking, and it was found that he had killed the Hindu woman living with him." The name Abdul is often used as a euphemism for Muslims on social media.
India Today Fact Check found that this incident took place on November 26 in Delhi. The person accused of murdering his live-in partner, however, is a Hindu man called Virendra Singh.
We searched TV9 Bharatvarsh's social media accounts and found the same graphic in a November 27 Facebook post , which also contained a link to a news report . Curiously, the report's details did not match the viral claim.
According to TV9 Bharatvarsh, 35-year-old Virendra Singh strangled his live-in girlfriend to death following a dispute over drinking alcohol. He left her body in his car and went to sleep drunk. In the morning, a neighbour's complaint led to the police recovering the body and arresting Singh. No communal angle was mentioned in the report.
Subsequently, we found more news reports about the incident. According to The Times of India , the victim was a 44-year-old woman named Radha. She was murdered by her live-in partner, Virendra Singh, who was already married and had kids.
Reportedly, Singh was heavily intoxicated when he killed Radha. He carried her body to his car with the help of two other associates. Per the report, he intended to dispose of the body later but fell asleep before he could do so.
A police officer told the Indian Express , "The house they were living in is in Virender's name. He had convinced the woman to sell her own house in Palam and bought the three-storey house, which they were currently living in, with the money made from the sale. Cash worth Rs 21 lakh was found in the house."
According to a police statement, on the morning of November 26, the Chhawla police station received a PCR call. When the police reached the spot at Najafgarh's Deenpur Extension, they found a Swift car locked and parked with a woman's dead body on the rear seat.
Upon interrogation, Virendra Singh admitted his guilt and said that when the victim asked him not to drink, they got into a quarrel. During this, he strangulated her and put her body in his car.
Speaking to India Today Fact Check, DCP Dwarka, Ankit Kumar Singh, confirmed there was no communal angle to the case, and both the victim and the killer were Hindu.
Thus, it's clear that the viral claim is false.
(Written by Aryama Bhattacharjee) - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Dec 4, 2025 16:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Aviation minister dancing amid IndiGo crisis? This video is OLD
content:
The video is from July. K Ram Mohan Naidu was dancing during the Sangeet function at his cousin's wedding in Andhra Pradesh.
IndiGo, India's largest domestic airline, is battling its worst-ever operational crisis , having cancelled more than 4,500 flights in a week. The disruptions entered their seventh straight day on Monday.
A video now going viral purports to show Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu dancing on a stage during the crisis. "Flights delayed, terminals overcrowded, passengers helpless and the Aviation Minister is dancing. This government has mastered one thing: entertainment over governance. Stop dancing and start managing the mess you created," read a post featuring the video.
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from July this year, recorded during the wedding of the minister's cousin.
Several people commented on the viral post claiming it was old. Using relevant keywords, we found the video posted by Tone News, a news outlet covering Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, on July 29.
Another report published by News 18 Telugu stated that Naidu danced at the sangeet ceremony of his cousin's wedding in the Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh. ETV Andhra Pradesh reported that he attended the wedding celebrations of his uncle Prabhakar's son at a resort in Bhogapuram in Srikakulam.
We also reached out to the Ministry of Civil Aviation, which confirmed that Minister K Ram Mohan Naidu has been in New Delhi for the last few days.
In an exclusive interview with India Today on December 6, the Civil Aviation Minister said that IndiGo alone was responsible for the ongoing crisis. He described the situation as unexpected and deeply unsettling for the aviation sector. Naidu, a Telugu Desam Party MP from Srikakulam, also told India Today that his top priority — and the government's — was the passengers.
Hence, it's clear that the viral video is old and does not show Minister K Ram Mohan Naidu dancing during the Indigo flight crisis. - Ends (Written by Aryama Bhattacharjee) Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 8, 2025 19:10 IST

title: Fact Check: Bangladesh video FALSELY shared as Muslims praying for Assam CM's removal
content:
This video is neither from Assam nor from India. It shows a religious gathering at the Charmonai Darbar Sharif in Bangladesh.
The Bharatiya Janata Party government in Assam has carried out eviction drives across several districts, including Golpara, demolishing numerous homes. Many affected residents have alleged that under Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, only Muslim houses were demolished, while the houses of Hindus and other faiths were not. The Assam government has rejected these allegations.
A video now going viral shows a gathering of Muslims where thousands of people can be seen and heard chanting "Allah-Allah" both on and off the stage. Those sharing the clip claimed that Muslims in Assam are praying for the removal of Sarma as CM.
An X user shared the clip and wrote : "Muslims in Assam praying to Allah to remove Himanta Biswa Sarma from the Chief Minister post."
India Today Fact Check found that this video is neither from Assam nor from India. It shows a religious congregation at the Charmonai Darbar Sharif in Barisal, Bangladesh. OUR PROBE
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to the same video shared by a Bangladeshi Maulana named Muhammad Raj on his Facebook page on November 27. According to the Bengali caption of the post, Maulana Muhammad Raj was present at this event and recorded the video himself. However, no information was provided regarding when or where the video was filmed.
Upon further examination of Maulana Muhammad Raj's Facebook page, we found another video recorded on stage at the same event, shared on November 29. In the Bengali caption of this video, Muhammad Raj said it was from the "Charmonai Mahfil" that he was attending.
A subsequent keyword search for "Charmonai Mahfil" led us to reports published by several Bangladeshi news outlets, including The Business Standard and Deshkal News . These reports explained that the Charmonai Mahfil is an event organised at the Charmonai Darbar Sharif in Barisal, Bangladesh. It is typically held twice a year: once in the Bengali month of Agrahayan and once in Falgun. The 2025 Falgun Mahfil began on February 19, while the most recent Agrahayan Mahfil was from November 26 to 28.
Additionally, a video of the Charmonai Mahfil 2025, held on November 27, is available on the YouTube channel Abu Bakar Media . The 26-minute-49-second mark in that video features the same frame as the viral video. A comparison of the two videos can be seen below.
We also contacted Moulana Muhammad Raj, who confirmed to India Today Fact Check that the video is from the Charmonai Mahfil in Bangladesh and was recorded on November 27.
Thus, it is clear that the video does not show Assamese Muslims praying to remove CM Himanta Biswa Sarma from his post. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 9, 2025 15:11 IST

title: Fact Check: RSS members dancing before British Raj? This clip is from 2015 — NOT 1942
content:
The video is from December 2015, when RSS members were celebrating the anniversary of the Sangh Shiksha Varg in Nagpur.
A video going viral on social media purports to show archival footage from the British Broadcasting Corporation of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh members dancing in British-colonised India.
The video was shared with captions like: "Archival footage from British Broadcasting Corporation. Date? Maybe 1942? Or, maybe later. Some people sing some weird song & dance on it when other Indians were singing Vande Mataram and Inquilab Zindabaad. RSS dancing in 1942 — when India was shouting Inquilab Zindabaad, they were literally doing choreography for the Raj. History has receipts, and they jiggle."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from December 2015, when RSS members were celebrating the anniversary of the Sangh's Shiksha Varg in Nagpur.
We could not find this video or any similar video of RSS members dancing in pre-independence India on the BBC's online archive.
However, a search using relevant keywords on Google led us to the same video shared by the YouTube channel of Zee 24 Taas on December 17, 2015.
We used NotebookLM to transcribe the Marathi-language news report and translate it into English. Per the translation, this video was of a Sangh Shiksha Varg training camp organised by the RSS at Reshimbagh in Maharashtra's Nagpur. There, Sangh members were recorded singing and dancing.
According to an Aaj Tak report , Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, his then-cabinet, and other Bharatiya Janata Party MLAs were also present at the RSS event held at the Hedgewar Smruti Bhawan — the RSS headquarters — in Nagpur's Reshimbagh.
Therefore, we concluded that the video is not the BBC's archival video from pre-Independence India.
(Written by Aryama Bhattacharjee) - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 11, 2025 15:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Photoshopped RTI peddles FAKE claim that IAF pilots are quitting after Op Sindoor
content:
This RTI response is doctored. The original response is from 2020 and was obtained by India Today.
Did 163 Indian Air Force pilots quit their jobs this year after Operation Sindoor? That's what's being claimed on social media, with a Right To Information response to support it.
One such post claimed: "Documents of IAF show that 780 pilots resigned in 5 years, and after the Pakistan-India war, 163 pilots resigned. Many families whose pilots were martyred in the war are still facing oppression to keep them silent, @RahulGandhi has been proven right once again today."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral RTI response has been edited. The original document is from 2020. We could not find any credible news reports about the number of IAF pilots who resigned from their posts in 2025.
The RTI response that was doctored to make the viral post was originally obtained by India Today's Ashok Kumar Upadhyay in August 2020. A news report about it, published five years ago, can be read here . The report highlighted that between 2010 and 2019, 798 IAF pilots had resigned, and of them, 289 were given no-objection certificates to fly for private airlines.
There are several visible discrepancies in the document that's being shared right now. Comparing it with the original RTI response reveals several edits that have been made. Notably, the RTI number — "MODEF/R/E/20/00534/D(RTI)" — which is a unique ID for RTI requests, was the same in both letters.
The years referenced in the original letter were from 2010 to 2019, not from 2017 to 2025. The date of the original letter was edited from December 7, 2020, to August 7, 2025.
The RTI response featured two tables. In the first table, the 2018 number (of 90 pilots) had been edited to falsely state that 163 pilots resigned in 2025.
Apart from that, the viral post letter features the signature of the Central Public Information Officer, Wing Commander SK Ojha. This name does not appear in the list of eight CPIOs on the Indian Air Force's official website. HOW MANY IAF PILOTS RESIGNED IN 2025?
We could find no credible reports about Indian Air Force pilots resigning from their posts in 2025, let alone after Operation Sindoor. An IAF suo-motu disclosure of information report from July this year did not list any such figures.
The only relevant significance of the number 163 we could find was that the number of Indian airports increased from 74 in 2014 to 163 in 2025, according to a press release by the Press Information Bureau. TREND OF DEFENCE DISINFORMATION
Recently, the Centre debunked a fake letter being circulated on social media claiming that the Indian Air Force is planning to abandon the Tejas fighter jets.
The PIB's fact-check unit also highlighted earlier this month that several "Pakistani propaganda accounts" were circulating a fabricated letter that they claimed was a "top-secret Ministry of External Affairs document that allegedly leaked online." #PAKISTAN Propaganda Alert! Several Pakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a letter on social media, claiming it to be a top-secret Ministry of External Affairs document that allegedly leaked online. The fabricated letter claims that the Indian Government has requested pic.twitter.com/DWxalnwjjM — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) December 1, 2025
#PAKISTAN Propaganda Alert! Several Pakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a letter on social media, claiming it to be a top-secret Ministry of External Affairs document that allegedly leaked online. The fabricated letter claims that the Indian Government has requested pic.twitter.com/DWxalnwjjM — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) December 1, 2025
Thus, it is clear that the viral claim is completely false. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 12, 2025 20:59 IST

title: Fact Check: Muslim cleric celebrates Bondi Beach attack in Sydney? This video is 2 years old
content:
This video is from 2023 and shows a Muslim cleric celebrating the October 7 Hamas attack on Israel.
Two gunmen, a father-son duo, shot and killed at least 15 people and injured dozens more at Sydney's Bondi Beach during the Jewish festival of Hanukkah on December 14. The killers, according to various news reports , have been identified as Naveed Akram and Sajid Akram.
A video now going viral shows a Muslim cleric delivering a speech in front of a crowd with chants of "Allah-Hu-Akbar". Allegedly, this video showed Muslims in Sydney celebrating the Bondi Beach terror attack.
One such post said, "The Muslims in Australia are smiling and happy about the Bondi massacre; they even lit fireworks to celebrate. They need to all be deported from every country to Arabic pig countries."
India Today Fact Check found that the video predates the Bondi Beach attack by two years. This 2023 clip shows a controversial Muslim cleric celebrating Hamas's October 7 attack on Israel. Our Probe
Reverse-searching keyframes from the video led us to a post from October 9, 2023, featuring the same clip. This makes it evident that the video is unrelated to the Bondi Beach shootout.
A subsequent search led us to a Sky News Australia report from October 9, 2023, on YouTube. The video report said the man speaking was a controversial Muslim cleric called Ibrahim Dadoun. At Lakemba in south-west Sydney on October 8, Dadoun told a crowd that he felt "elated", describing the October 7 Hamas attack as a "day of courage a day of pride a day of victory".
An ABC report from the time noted that the Prime Minister of Australia, Anthony Albanese, condemned these comments. "There's nothing to celebrate in the murder of innocent civilians going about their day. Some of those who have been captured are young people who were attending a rave, enjoying life, and enjoying each other's company. There's nothing to celebrate here," he said.
According to a Daily Mail report , after some backlash, the cleric walked back his comments in a Facebook post and said: "To be clear, at no stage did I express any support for, nor refer to, the loss of lives on any side. I made no reference to the killing of the innocent people. I do not condone nor celebrate the killing of innocent people from any side, particularly women and children."
It is thus abundantly clear that the viral video predates the attack by two years. Celebratory fireworks?
Another video making the rounds online purports to show Muslims in Australia celebrating the terror attack with fireworks. This claim, however, was debunked by The Straits Times .
According to its report, while there were fireworks around Canterbury Bankstown on the evening of December 14 (the day of the attack), they were actually a preplanned display for Christmas celebrations.
"The fireworks were part of our annual Christmas Carols event; this event and the fireworks display were planned months in advance," said the Rotary Club of Padstow. "They were not in any way related to the terrorist attack at Bondi." - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 15, 2025 21:54 IST

title: Fact Check: Did a little girl save her father's life at a construction site?
content:
A miracle caught on camera? A video going viral right now shows a construction worker narrowly escaping death. When his young daughter runs up to him for a hug, the construction worker turns just moments before a heavy concrete block crashes down where he was standing.
Sharing the video on Instagram, one user wrote: "A hug that became a miracle. In a moment that feels straight out of a movie, a construction worker in Canada escaped de@th by less than a second — and his lifesaver was his own little daughter." The video has been widely shared with similar emotional claims here , here , and here .
But is this dramatic moment real? India Today Fact Check found that this video is AI-generated. Our Probe
A closer look at the video revealed multiple visual inconsistencies, telltale signs of AI-generated content. The girl's face appeared distorted. The head of the shovel shrinks in size after the block falls on it. The shape of the shovel also changes across frames.
The iron rods in the concrete column repeatedly change shape, from straight lines in one frame to mesh in another. And while the block falling caused a giant cloud of dust to rise up, the construction worker walking in the same place before resulted in no footprints.
These inconsistencies strongly indicated that this video was synthetic content and did not show a real incident. To further confirm this, we analysed the video using two AI-detection tools.
Hive Moderation found that there was a 99.8 per cent probability that the video was AI-generated. Sight Engine, said the same with 97 per cent certainty.
Additionally, we found no credible news reports about such an incident occurring anywhere in Canada.
Thus, it is clear that the viral video does not show a real incident.
(Written by Rashmi Gupta) - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 15, 2025 21:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Scripted video VIRAL as bride saying final goodbye to ex before wedding
content:
This video is staged. It does not show a real incident.
A video allegedly showing a bride-to-be meeting her ex, hours before her wedding, is going viral on social media. In the video, a friend of the teary-eyed bride, who drives her to the ex, says, "Her name is Shreya and she is my friend. She asked me to help her meet her boyfriend just once. She couldn't marry him because of family pressure."
An X user shared this video and wrote, "She is getting married but still went to meet her ex-boyfriend. There are many such cases in society where girls meet their ex before marriage and some even after marriage. The past always matters."
Many news outlets, like News 18 and Amar Ujala , also reported it as a real incident.
India Today Fact Check, however, found that the video in question is scripted. Aarav Mavi, the content creator who made this video, confirmed this.
A quick reverse search of the viral keyframes led us to a December 13 post by an Instagram account called @chalte_phirte098. This account belongs to one Aarav Mavi, a digital creator. The account's bio says, "Turning heartbreaks into timeless stories. Every shattered heart has a story. Share yours with me!" This implies that the video might be a dramatisation, and not an actual incident.
We also found a video on his Instagram account, in which he asks people to send their stories if they want him to create reels about them. Mavi often creates such scripted videos on subjects like love and relationships. Some such videos can be seen here , and here . In one of his videos , shooting equipment like a camera and lights can also be seen.
We also found Mavi's other Instagram account where he has described himself as an aspiring actor. The highlights section of his account features a category called "shoot mode" which has visuals captured during shooting.
India Today Fact Check also spoke to Mavi, who said that the viral video was indeed scripted. Thus, it's clear that the clip does not show a real incident. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Dec 16, 2025 14:20 IST

title: Fact Check: TIME did not name Bondi hero Ahmed Al Ahmed as 'Person Of The Year'
content:
This cover is fake. On December 11, TIME magazine announced the 'Architects of AI' as its 'Person of the Year' for 2025.
As Sajid Akram and his son Naveed opened fire at people celebrating the Jewish festival of Hanukkah at Bondi Beach in Sydney, Australia, a fruit seller showed incredible valour. Ahmed Al Ahmed, 43, risked his life and neutralised one of the gunmen.
This act of heroism has now allegedly earned Ahmed Al Ahmed the coveted position on the cover of TIME magazine as its "Person of the Year" .
India Today Fact Check found that this is untrue. TIME magazine announced its "Person Of The Year" for 2025 on December 11, a couple of days before the terror attack at Bondi Beach.
We found a BBC report from December 11 about TIME magazine's 2025 "Person Of The Year" not being a single person, unlike every year. Per it, the magazine has recognised the year's most influential figure as "the architects" of artificial intelligence. Among the people featured in the "Person Of The Year" list this time are X owner Elon Musk, Meta head Mark Zuckerberg, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and OpenAI boss Sam Altman.
The official X account of TIME magazine also shared the same information on December 11, in a post that said, "2025 was the year when artificial intelligence's full potential roared into view, and when it became clear that there will be no turning back."
"For delivering the age of thinking machines, for wowing and worrying humanity, for transforming the present and transcending the possible, the Architects of AI are TIME's 2025 Person of the Year." It further added. 2025 was the year when artificial intelligence's full potential roared into view, and when it became clear that there will be no turning back. Addressing the story behind these covers, a TIME report dated December 11 mentioned that these two covers were designed by illustrator and graphics animator Peter Crowther and digital painter Jason Seiler, to portray the "duality AI has produced – man vs machine."
It is also noteworthy that TIME magazine's December 15 edition , which reports on the Bondi Beach massacre, features an image of the Sydney Opera House with a Jewish menorah on the cover. According to an Al Jazeera report , Al Ahmed is an Australian Muslim citizen of Syrian origin. According to his relative, Mustafa Asad, Al Ahmed is from the village of al-Nayrab, near Idlib in Syria, and moved to Australia in 2006.
Al Ahmed was shot twice during the incident and is currently being treated at Saint George Hospital in Kogarah, New South Wales. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told reporters: "I thanked him for the lives that he helped to save, and I wished him all the very best with his surgery that he will undertake tomorrow." - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 16, 2025 18:46 IST

title: Fact check: Video of Owaisi saying he knew Bondi Beach shooters is a deepfake!
content:
This video is a deepfake. The Hyderabad MP confirmed the same to India Today Fact Check.
What began as a Jewish festival at Australia's Bondi Beach on Sunday ended with a deadly shooting. At least 15 people were killed in a terror attack. In the immediate aftermath, social media — and news reports — were rife with the claim that the two gunmen, the father-son duo of Sajid and Naveed Akram, were of Pakistani origin.
According to a Reuters report , however, the Philippines Bureau of Immigration said on December 16 that the two gunmen had travelled to the country recently, and that Sajid Akram had an Indian passport. The Hindu also quoted Indian government officials saying that Sajid was from Hyderabad and had last visited India in 2022.
A video now going viral purports to show Hyderabad MP Assaduddin Owaisi saying on camera that he knew the Bondi Beach gunmen.
The video starts with FirstPost's Palki Sharma saying this was Owaisi's exclusive statement on the terror attack. The video then cuts to the AIMIM chief, who can be heard saying that while Sajid Akram was a decent man, his son Naveed was mentally ill. He then said that he couldn't believe that Sajid would commit such a heinous act.
India Today Fact Check's investigation found that the video is a deepfake. Owaisi made no such statement. Our Probe
A reverse search of frames from the video led us to a Palki Sharma broadcast about Donald Trump and Taiwan, which was streamed on FirstPost's YouTube channel on November 25. In this clip, she can be seen wearing the same outfit. This obviously predates the Bondi Beach terror attack. We also found Sharma's show about the terror attack, in which she wears a very different outfit.
A similar search for the Asaduddin Owaisi video led to an interview with ANI in which he is seen wearing the same clothes and sitting in front of the same background. That video is from October 11 and was about a shoe being hurled at the Chief Justice of India. "Respectfully disagree with CJI Gavai...wrong message went across country": Owaisi on shoe-hurling incident in Supreme Court Read @ANI Story | https://t.co/7X46bRv7U4 #AsaddudinOwaisi #AIMIM #CJIBRGavai pic.twitter.com/CzUG2OKdbr — ANI Digital (@ani_digital) October 11, 2025
"Respectfully disagree with CJI Gavai...wrong message went across country": Owaisi on shoe-hurling incident in Supreme Court Read @ANI Story | https://t.co/7X46bRv7U4 #AsaddudinOwaisi #AIMIM #CJIBRGavai pic.twitter.com/CzUG2OKdbr — ANI Digital (@ani_digital) October 11, 2025
This hinted that the video of Owaisi speaking about the Bondi Beach gunmen was a deepfake. To confirm this, India Today Fact Check reached out to the MP. He rubbished the viral video as "all false" and said: "I have always condemned terrorism."
Thus, it is clear that the video of Assaduddin Owaisi saying he knew Sajid Akram and his son Naveed is a deepfake.
(Written by Rashmi Gupta) - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 16, 2025 20:27 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of medicine vials being unhygienically recycled is NOT from India
content:
This video is not from India. It is from Pakistan.
A video going viral allegedly shows the state of the Indian pharmaceutical industry. In the video, heaps of glass medicine vials can be seen being cleaned in dirty water.
The voiceover in the video says, "Today, we step into India's most sterile and trustworthy vial rebirth centre. Not glass recycling, but a full spiritual cleansing for medical waste."
A Facebook user shared the video and wrote: "The second life of Indian hospital vials."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is not from India at all. It is from Pakistan. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes of the viral video led us to the same video uploaded to the YouTube channel Work Skill Masters on November 28. The caption and description of this video said it showed the recycling process of injection vials.
Notably, the original video did not specify where it was recorded, nor did the channel disclose its location in the "About" section.
However, on closer inspection, several vials visible in the video carried labels printed in Urdu, an uncommon sight in India.
In one frame, we observed an empty vial whose label said "Zecef". This is an injectable medicine manufactured by a Pakistani pharmaceutical company called Bosch Pharmaceuticals Private Limited. The company is based in the Korangi industrial area of Karachi.
According to the company's distribution details , Bosch Pharmaceuticals supplies medicines exclusively within Pakistan and does not export them abroad.
Further, a man in the video can be seen carrying a sack bearing the name Lucky Core Industries Limited , a Pakistani conglomerate headquartered in Karachi, with operations spanning polyester, pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, soda ash, and veterinary medicines.
We observed another sack labelled Nayab Maida (flour). A keyword search led us to a Pakistani e-commerce website, Niagra , selling the same brand of flour.
We also came across the Facebook page of Nayab , containing a Pakistani contact number and a website , which revealed that Nayab is a brand of Maqsood Flour Mill, based in Lahore.
Although we could not verify the date and exact location of the video, it is more than clear that it originates from Pakistan. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 18, 2025 19:26 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show Bangladesh police handing over Dipu Das to extremists
content:
This video predates the lynching of Dipu Das. It was first shared on November 18 and shows a Dhaka College student.
A video of Bangladeshi police officers dragging a man by his collar has gone viral on social media. Those sharing this clip claimed that it captured the final moments of Dipu Chandra Das, a 25-year-old Hindu man who was lynched by a mob in Bangladesh's Mymensingh following allegations of blasphemy. Notably, Bangladesh's Rapid Action Battalion has said that it has found no evidence of blasphemy against Das.
Many, including the Bharatiya Janata Party's Tajinder Bagga , shared this clip with claims like, "Deepu Chandra Das kept crying. He kept pleading. But the Bangladesh police handed him over to die at the hands of a radical Muslim mob. Deepu kept saying again and again. Sir, I am innocent. Sir, I am innocent. Sir, I have done nothing wrong." View this post on Instagram A post shared by Tajinder Bagga (@baggatajinder)
A post shared by Tajinder Bagga (@baggatajinder)
Another such post was captioned: "He was pleading till his last moments. Deepu Chandra Das kept crying. He kept pleading, but the Bangladesh police handed him over to die at the hands of radical extremists."
India Today Fact Check found that the video has been on the internet since November and predates the lynching of Dipu Das.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the original clip shared by a Bangladeshi news portal called Bhorer Kagoj on November 18. The caption of this post said, "What happened to this Dhaka College student?"
This makes it evident that the video can not be related to Dipu Das's death at all. According to multiple news reports , Das was beaten to death, and his body was set on fire on Thursday, December 18, in Mymensingh's Bhaluka Upazila.
A thorough review of the original 47-second clip revealed several additional points. Around the nine-second mark, the man under police custody can be heard saying in Bangla, "Brother, I am from Dhaka College, brother."
Das was employed at the Pioneer Knit Composite Factory in the Square Masterbari area of Mymensingh city. According to the Bangladesh Rapid Action Battalion , the factory floor manager, Alamgir Hossain, forced Das to resign and then handed him over to the mob.
Around the 15-second mark, he repeats the same. Additionally, around the 29-second mark, he says, "If the DC hadn't intervened, they would have killed me. He saved me."
This version of the video also contained parts that were clipped out from the viral one. Around the 32-second mark, the police officer can be seen letting the man go, saying, "You first go, go from here," following which, another voice asks the man, "Where will you go first, to the Hall or Hospital?" Responding to this, the man says in Bangla, "The Hall." In Bangladesh, halls refer to residential dormitories where students live.
We also found that the man was wearing a T-shirt with the logo of Dhaka College on the left, and "Session 2022–23" written on the right side. In a part clipped from the viral video, the name "Momin" can be seen printed on the back of his T-shirt.
To check further, India Today Fact Check shared this video with Bangladeshi reporters and fact-checkers. They identified the police officer seen setting the man free as Masud Alam , the Deputy Commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (Ramana Department). Notably, Dipu Chandra Das was lynched in Bhaluka Upazila of the Mymensingh district, which is about 90 kilometres away from Dhaka City.
Furthermore, at the end of the original video, another man says in Bangla, "We came from our campus just now, you have to be more careful."
On another Bangladesh-based Facebook page named Dainik Sokal, we came across a different video of the same incident, dated November 18. Here, Dhaka Metropolitan Police DC Masud Alam can be seen helping the man board a rickshaw and sending him back to his hostel.
The video was captioned in Bangla: "DC Masud sent the injured student to the hall by renting a rickshaw in Dhanmondi 32." Dhanmondi 32 is the name of the former personal residence of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. It now houses the Bangabandhu Memorial Museum and is located in Dhanmondi, Dhaka.
Therefore, it is more than evident that an old video is being falsely peddled as the final moments of Dipu Chandra Das pleading for mercy.
Update: Following the publishing of the story, we came across another video of the same incident. We have updated the story accordingly. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 23, 2025 13:16 IST

title: Fact Check: Muhammad Yunus NEVER said his mother was raped by Pak soldiers
content:
This postcard is doctored. He never said this.
Amid the unrest in Bangladesh, a shocking statement attributed to the country's interim leader, Muhammad Yunus, has gone viral. The postcard being shared features Yunus's photo and the words, "My own mother was r*ped by Pakistani soldiers during the freedom struggle of 1971, says CA Yunus."
It also featured the logo of the popular Bangladeshi news outlet Dhaka Tribune. A Facebook user shared this postcard with the caption, "And then this man was born."
India Today Fact Check found that this quote is fake. Muhammad Yunus never said this.
Using reverse search, we found a December 14 post by Dhaka Tribune with the same photo, layout, and design. The only differences were that the text here read, "CA Yunus mourns the casualties of Bangladeshi peacekeepers in drone attack in Sudan," and the font.
We couldn't find any credible news reports about Muhammad Yunus making such a statement about his mother. To confirm further, we shared the viral postcard with Nayem Ali, the Assistant Press Secretary to Muhammad Yunus. He told us that Yunus hadn't said anything like this.
According to news reports , Muhammad Yunus's mother, Sofia Khatun, had a great influence on him during his early years.
Thus, it is clear that the postcard being shared is doctored. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 23, 2025 22:57 IST

title: Fact Check: Hindu man pleading for life in Bangladesh? This video is AI
content:
An Indian digital creator named Kuldeep Meena created this video using AI. This video does not show a real person.
After Dipu Chandra Das, another Hindu man called Amrit Mondal has been reportedly lynched by a mob in Bangladesh. A video now going viral allegedly shows a Hindu man in Bangladesh pleading for the safety of his life and that of other Hindus.
This nighttime selfie video shows a man passing along a street with several shops on fire. He says, "I'm in Bangladesh. It's nighttime. Like 'Dipu Chadar', they'll kill us as well. You can see what is happening here. Share this video as much as possible so that somebody can save us. I don't understand anything. Things deteriorated so suddenly."
An X user posted this video with the caption, "Bangladesh is getting out of hand." Some people also claimed this video was recorded on December 23. Sudarshan News journalist Sagar Kumar shared this video with the caption, "Hindus in Bangladesh are dying every day. Hindus in Bangladesh are asking, 'Who will save us?' Narendra Modi ji, please save them."
India Today Fact Check found that this video is AI-generated. It does not show an actual person.
There are many clues in the video that point to it being AI-generated. For example, the man mispronounces Dipu Chandra's name as "Dipu Chadar". Chadar is the Hindi word for sheet.
In the video, we can also see the middle of an electric pole emitting light with no source visible. We also observed a car whose door colour differs from the rest of the body.
A Bangladeshi flag can be seen hoisted on a pole. When the man passes by it, the colour of a portion of this pole changes to white.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the video, we found that it was originally posted by one Kuldeep Meena on Instagram on December 24. We noticed that this account had posted many AI-generated selfie videos featuring the same person.
He has posted multiple videos allegedly showing arson and atrocities against Hindus in Bangladesh. Comparing these with photos of Kuldeep posted on the account makes it clear that he has used his own pictures to create such AI videos.
Thus, it is clear that the viral video does not show a real Hindu person from Bangladesh pleading for his safety. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 26, 2025 21:18 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of an electric car exploding is NOT from Indore
content:
No such incident happened in Indore. This video was shared by several news websites in November, claiming it was from China.
A video of a car allegedly exploding in Indore has gone viral. Those sharing the video claimed that an electric car parked outside a house in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, exploded, causing panic in the area. At the beginning of the video, light smoke can be seen rising from under a car. The smoke then darkens and increases in volume quickly before an explosion occurs.
A Threads user shared the video and wrote , "Explosion in an electric car parked outside a house in Indore, panic in the area. Chaos erupted in a residential area of Indore city when a sudden massive explosion occurred in an electric car parked outside a house. The sound of the explosion was so loud that people nearby got scared and came out of their homes. The incident is said to have happened in the morning, when the car was not charging, yet it exploded all of a sudden." Its archive can be viewed here .
Several news outlets like Global Herald News , JSR Times , and the Indore Express shared the video, claiming it to be from Indore.
India Today Fact Check found that this video is not from Indore. It was shared by several Chinese news websites and channels in November, who claimed the incident was from the country.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video revealed that it was shared on November 19 by the Instagram account called @IntelligenceGo . According to the post, the car that exploded was the Feifan ER6, a sedan manufactured by China's SAIC Motor company . On the car auction-related website, we found a photo of this model. It matched the car in the viral video, suggesting the clip was from China.
A subsequent keyword search led us to several Chinese-language news reports. According to a report on news.nextapple.com , this incident occurred in a community car park in China. A person living nearby recorded the video of the incident, and when the explosion occurred, he shut his windows, fearing toxic smoke. According to other reports , production of the Feifan ER6 car has been discontinued in China.
There was an explosion in a moving e-rickshaw in Indore in November. But we found no recent news reports about an electric car exploding in Indore.
Although we cannot confirm with certainty the exact location and date of this video, it is more than clear that it is not from Indore. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 30, 2025 19:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Hindu holy man beaten up in Bangladesh? No, this video is from Punjab
content:
This video is from Punjab's Hoshiarpur district, where a man allegedly trying to abduct a child was beaten up by a mob.
The killing of Bajendra Biswas, who was shot dead by a colleague inside a garment factory in Bangladesh on December 29, is the latest in a disturbing trend of violence against minority Hindus in the country. A video now going viral claims to show another such incident.
The clip shows a man in saffron clothes being beaten up by the mob. Those sharing it used hashtags like "Hindu Lives Matter" and "Save Bangladeshi Hindus".
An X user wrote in Hindi while sharing the video: "In Bangladesh, nobody is ready to pay attention to the condition of the Hindus." Its archive can be viewed here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from Punjab's Hoshiarpur and shows a mob attacking an alleged child abductor. Our Probe
Upon reverse searching the keyframes of the viral video, we found that an Instagram user called @sagararjeet had posted it on December 21. As per the text superimposed on the video he posted, the man in saffron clothes was caught trying to abduct a three-year-old at the Tanda Railway Station.
This Instagram user, Arjeet Sagar, had shared multiple videos of this incident in December. In a video posted on December 14, some men can be seen holding sugarcane sticks and walking towards the man in saffron clothes, seemingly before beating him up.
In another such video, a reporter can be seen talking about the incident in Punjabi. He can be seen holding a mic branded with the logo of Dainik Savera, a news outlet primarily focused on Punjab, Haryana, and Himachal Pradesh. As per Google's NotebookLM, the reporter in the video said that at the Tanda railway station, a man dressed in religious attire attempted to abduct a child. View this post on Instagram A post shared by arjeet sagar (@sagararjeet) Where did this happen?
A post shared by arjeet sagar (@sagararjeet)
The Tanda Urmar Railway Station is located in Punjab's Hoshiyarpur district. To verify that this video was shot there, we looked at Google Maps photos of the station.
In the viral video, we noticed a State Bank of India ATM vestibule. We found the same in one of the Google Maps photos and in a YouTube video about the station posted by a content creator from Punjab, @Amardeepsinghpuria. We also noticed that the design of the metal benches was the same in Google Maps photos and the viral video.
Additionally, on one of the benches seen in the viral video, we observed a sticker with "GIC Re" written on it. This is the logo of the General Insurance Corporation of India.
India Today's Hoshiarpur correspondent Sunil Lakha has also confirmed that this incident occurred at the Tanda Urmar Railway Station. He told us that the man in religious attire had attempted to abduct the child, was caught by bystanders, and beaten up.
Thus, it is clear that the viral video is not from Bangladesh. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Dec 31, 2025 18:54 IST
